3. **Refresh-on-focus (the "no indication" fix).** When the canvas tab regains visibility/focus, `SaveStatusIndicator` re-reads the new lightweight `GET /api/items/:id/version` (`getItemVersion` — one `updated_at`, no body, owner-scoped) and, if it moved past what this canvas last saw, shows a dismissible "Updated on another device — Reload" banner. The baseline lives in `save-status.ts` (`knownVersion`), seeded at mount and advanced by every successful body save (exact, from the PATCH response) plus a `localSaveSinceSync` flag that absorbs the canvas's *own* writes so a refocus right after editing never reads your own change as remote. One tiny request per refocus, gated on `document.visibilityState`, so an idle tab costs nothing. No polling interval (a single user physically switches devices; focus is the signal).
**Why / alternatives:** *`If-Match`/`updated_at` optimistic token* — rejected as the body mechanism: every sibling control on the canvas (status, due, priority, properties) bumps `updated_at`, so a per-surface token would false-409 against your *own* device's field edits unless all ~12 hand-rolled writers refreshed it; content-hashing the body sidesteps that entirely. *Realtime sync (SSE / WebSocket / Postgres LISTEN-NOTIFY)* — rejected: long-lived connections fight Vercel's serverless model and it's a heavy dependency for a single user (principles 5, 8). *CRDT / Yjs co-editing* — rejected: large dependency for a problem that is "two stale tabs," not live multi-cursor. *Rely on revisions to recover clobbers* — rejected as the primary fix: it's a timing-dependent backstop, and "silently lose then maybe restore" is worse than "detect and ask."
**Scope boundary (defer-by-hiding):** the hard guard covers the markdown body editor (`ItemEditor` — notes/tasks/meetings, the scenario). Chord/Paper bodies (`useItemAutosave`) don't send the token yet; they advance the focus baseline on save (so no false stale banner) and rely on the refresh-on-focus alert, not the hard guard. Title clobber (both devices editing the title) stays last-write-wins, covered by the focus banner. Both are reasonable v1 boundaries; extending the token to them is additive later.
**Verified:** `scripts/verify-concurrent-edit.mts` against live Neon (throwaway owner, cleaned up) — `bodyDigest` determinism/sensitivity/format-agnosticism; matching digest writes; stale digest → 409 with the stored body untouched; resynced digest writes; no-token = last-write-wins; identical-body PATCH with a stale token is a safe no-op; `getItemVersion` returns `updated_at` and is owner-scoped. Plus the full HTTP round-trip in the dev-auth preview against a scratch note (since the Tiptap canvas doesn't hydrate under dev streaming): device-2 write 200 → device-1 stale guarded write **409, body preserved** → "Keep mine" (no token) **200, overwrites**; the `/version` route returns 200. tsc + eslint clean.
**Affects:** `src/lib/items.ts` (`ItemError` gains `"conflict"`; `ItemPatch.expectedBodyDigest`; the guard in `updateItem`; new `getItemVersion`), `src/lib/api.ts` (409 mapping), `src/lib/body.ts` (`bodyDigest`), `src/lib/item-input.ts` (parse `expectedBodyDigest`), `src/lib/save-status.ts` (conflict state + force-save registry + focus baseline), `src/components/markdown-editor/ItemEditor.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/SaveStatusIndicator.tsx` (+ props from `ItemCanvas.tsx`), `src/components/chord-editor/useItemAutosave.ts`; new route `src/app/api/items/[id]/version/route.ts`; new `scripts/verify-concurrent-edit.mts`. No migration (uses existing `items.updated_at`). Reversible: the request field and 409 are additive; reverting the client stops sending the token and the server falls back to last-write-wins.

## ADR-135: Multi-select on related panels + meeting "Open tasks" on the lens system
**Date:** 2026-06-30
**Status:** accepted (Brandon-directed, built). **Not core** — UI/view-rendering layer only: the view engine (`queryViewItems`/`ViewFilter`) is untouched, no schema/migration, no machine-API change. Solo-movable.
**Context:** PR #129 gave every related-type group on an item ("Linked here") the owner's chosen **lens** (the type's saved lenses/views rendered through the shared `ViewRenderer`). Brandon flagged two gaps when viewing a **meeting**: (1) the lens treatment didn't reach the tasks he actually works from there, and (2) there was no multi-select on those tasks. Root cause on (1): a meeting's tasks mostly surface in the **"Open tasks"** panel (`MeetingPrep`), which is **rule-pulled** (tasks related to the event's people, or by tag — ADR-094 E4), not directly related to the meeting — so it rendered through a bespoke client list (`PrepTaskList`) with an old lightweight sort/filter bar, bypassing the lens path entirely. On (2): even "Linked here" (`RelatedGroupView`) called `ViewRenderer` **without** `selectable`, so the multi-select standard (ADR-118 — "every list surface") had an unintentional gap across all related panels.
**Decision.** Three reuse-first moves, no new rendering machinery:
1. **`ViewLensBody` becomes the one selectable view-body**, gaining an optional `rowActions` pass-through. It already wrapped `ViewRenderer` in `SelectionProvider` + `SelectModeToggle` + `BulkActionBar` (gating board/calendar out per ADR-118); adding `rowActions` lets the related panels reuse it verbatim instead of calling `ViewRenderer` directly.
2. **`RelatedGroupView` routes through `ViewLensBody`** and takes an optional `bulkConfig`. A related group is always one type, so the caller passes that type's **full** `bulkConfigForType` (status/date/select + Move + Delete) — richer than a mixed surface's Move+Delete. `RelatedPanel` resolves each group's `typeDef` and hands down its config; a type that fails to resolve renders read-only. The leading select checkbox and the trailing relation controls (un-relate, @-marker) **coexist** in the list/table layouts.
3. **Meeting "Open tasks" joins the lens path** via a new `resolveProvidedGroup(rows, typeKey, lens, hideCompleted)` (`related-views.ts`): it renders an **already-resolved** row set (membership decided by the pull rule, not a `ViewFilter`) through the same `ViewLensData` shape, applying the lens's order **in memory** (`sortInMemory`, mirroring the engine's nulls-last rules; `mostLinked` keeps the rule's order since a body-free row carries no relation count). `MeetingPrep` then renders the standard `CanvasSection` ("Open tasks" + the existing `TaskPullControl`) with the lens picker in the section's action slot and `ViewLensBody` for the rows. `PrepTaskList` is deleted (fully replaced).
**Why / alternatives:** *Restrict the Open-tasks picker to SORT lenses* (not view lenses) — chosen deliberately: a saved **view** lens carries its own `filter`, and applying that filter to a rule-chosen set would silently drop tasks the rule deliberately pulled in; a view lens's `relatedTo` wouldn't even match (these tasks relate to the *people*, not the meeting). Sort lenses contribute order only, which composes cleanly. *Add an `ids`/multi-`relatedTo` filter to `ViewFilter`* so the rule-pull rides the real query engine — rejected: that's a change to the shared/core view engine (both-agree + ADR) for what is a presentation need; in-memory sort of an in-hand, body-free, capped row set is cheap and keeps this solo. *One panel-wide `SelectionProvider` with mixed-type Move+Delete config* — rejected: each related group is single-type, so per-group providers give the richer, type-appropriate bulk actions Brandon wants for tasks (set status, reschedule); the floating bar only appears for the group you're selecting in. The Open-tasks lens choice shares the `(event:task)` key with any Linked-here task group, so "how I view this meeting's tasks" stays one setting.
**Verified:** dev-auth preview against the prod DB on a real meeting ("Brandon/Roger Check-in", 21 pulled tasks): the Open-tasks panel shows the **Lens** picker (Recent/Newest/A→Z/Most linked — view lenses correctly excluded) + a **Select** toggle (off by default, ADR-121); switching to "A→Z" re-sorts the rows alphabetically and persists; entering select mode reveals 21 row checkboxes and the floating bar (**Set… → Status To Do/Done/Archived + Due date + Scheduled date, Move…, Delete, Clear**). The "Linked here" Person group shows its own Select toggle, and a row carries **both** the select checkbox and the un-relate (✕) control. Clean reload = exactly two toggles, both off. No console/server errors; tsc + eslint clean.
**Affects:** `src/components/lists/ViewLensBody.tsx` (`rowActions`), `src/components/relations/RelatedGroupView.tsx` (→ `ViewLensBody`, `bulkConfig`), `src/components/relations/RelatedPanel.tsx` (per-group `bulkConfigForType`), `src/lib/related-views.ts` (`resolveProvidedGroup` + `sortInMemory`/`sortKey`), `src/components/meetings/MeetingPrep.tsx` (Open tasks → lens path + multi-select); deletes `src/components/meetings/PrepTaskList.tsx`. No migration. Reversible (UI wiring only). **Scope boundary (defer-by-hiding):** Open tasks stays the `list` layout (rule-pulled rows don't need board/calendar); board/calendar layouts remain non-selectable per ADR-118.

## ADR-136: Calendar feed + event timeline as bespoke lenses; unify events onto `/list/event`
**Date:** 2026-07-01
**Status:** accepted (Brandon-directed, built). **Core-adjacent** — extends the shared `Lens` union (`list-lenses.ts`, first defined ADR-105) with two new *kinds*, which is shared code both instances use, so it gets an ADR + a `COLLAB.md` heads-up to Tyler. But the two new kinds' **bodies and defaults are event-module internals** (Microsoft calendar adapter + the event timeline), enabled only for the `event` type; no schema/migration, no view-engine or machine-API change. Solo-movable in practice.
**Context:** The calendar-import feature (browse upcoming Outlook meetings, click **Add** to pull each into Ledgr as an `event` to take notes on — ADR-094 E3) went missing from Brandon's view. Root cause was a **routing split** the lens era introduced, not a deletion: the feed + the Upcoming/Past/No-date timeline lived only on the bespoke `/events` page (which had **no** lens tab strip), while the destination picker (`nav-slot-options.ts`) mapped the `event` type to the *generic* `/list/event` page (which had lenses but **no** feed). Navigating to "Events" landed on the lensed page and the feed silently fell out of view. Two divergent events pages was the real problem.
**Decision.** Unify onto the generic `/list/event` page (Brandon's call over keeping two pages) and make the two event surfaces **lenses**:
1. **Two bespoke lens kinds** on the shared `Lens` union — `{kind:"calendar"}` (the un-promoted upcoming feed + one-click **Add**, external data) and `{kind:"timeline"}` (the Upcoming/Past/No-date grouping by `meetingAt`). Both carry only `id`+`label` (no sort/source); the list page branches on `kind` to pick the body. Neither is expressible as a sort or view lens (external data / bespoke grouping), which is why they earn their own kinds rather than riding `view`.
2. **`defaultLenses(typeKey?)` is now type-aware:** `event` gets `[Calendar, Timeline, Recent, Newest, A→Z, Most linked]` (Calendar default/leftmost); every other type keeps the four generic sorts unchanged. Hiding/reordering is the ordinary Build → Types tabs editor (`ListTabsEditor`), which also offers an **"Event views"** group to re-add Calendar/Timeline after removal, and resets to the event defaults.
3. **The generic list page** (`/list/[type]`) fetches `listCalendarFeed` for the calendar lens (with an empty state, since it's the default landing) and the meeting-time-ordered split for the timeline lens (wrapped in the standard `SelectionProvider`/`SelectModeToggle`/`BulkActionBar`). The feed + timeline rendering moved out of the retired page into `CalendarFeed`/`EventTimeline` components + a shared `event-format.ts`. The bespoke `/events` route becomes a `redirect("/list/event")` (defer-by-hiding, not deleted) and `ListTabs` points events at `/list/event` (tab key aligned to the type key `event`, mirroring `person`).
**Why / alternatives:** *Just fix nav to re-point at the bespoke `/events`* — rejected by Brandon; leaves two divergent pages and keeps lenses off events. *Rebuild the feed/timeline as saved **view** lenses instead of new kinds* — the calendar feed reads external `calendar_events` (not `items`), so no `ViewFilter` can express it; the timeline's Upcoming/Past grouping is bespoke. New kinds are the honest model. *Let bespoke lenses flow into related panels* — rejected: a calendar feed or timeline inside a host item's "Linked here" makes no sense, and `event` is now the first default lens (so it would become the related-group default). Fixed with `relatedLensCandidates()` — related panels offer/​default to **sort + view lenses only** — and `resolveRelatedGroup` defaults a stray bespoke lens to `updatedAt desc` instead of asserting non-null.
**Verified:** dev-auth preview against the prod DB. `/list/event` strip reads **Calendar · Timeline · Recent · Newest · A→Z · Most linked**, Calendar active by default, showing 12 real upcoming events each with **Add**; Timeline lens renders Upcoming/Past; `/events` redirects to `/list/event`; Build → Types → Event shows the six event defaults and the re-addable "Event views" options; `/list/person` still shows only the four generic sorts (no leak). No console/server errors; tsc + eslint clean.
**Affects:** `src/lib/list-lenses.ts` (union + `defaultLenses(typeKey)` + `relatedLensCandidates` + parse), `src/app/list/[type]/page.tsx` (kind branches), `src/components/calendar/CalendarFeed.tsx` + `src/components/events/EventTimeline.tsx` + `src/lib/event-format.ts` (extracted bodies), `src/app/events/page.tsx` (→ redirect), `src/components/lists/ListTabs.tsx` (events → `/list/event`), `src/components/build/ListTabsEditor.tsx` (badges/describe/reset/re-add), `src/components/relations/RelatedPanel.tsx` + `src/lib/related-views.ts` (bespoke-lens guards). No migration (lenses live in `users.settings.listTabs`). Reversible.

## ADR-137: AI Memory — a `memory` type + always-on "stumps" + `remember`, read over MCP, behind a setting
**Date:** 2026-07-01
**Status:** accepted (Brandon-directed, built; **Tyler pre-cleared** — a `COLLAB.md` heads-up pairs with this). **Core** — it extends the machine/MCP API contract (two new tools + one resource) and adds a cross-cutting owner setting, so it takes an ADR + both-agree. The `memory` type itself is a bespoke type (not a schema change), and everything else reuses existing libs (items/relations/views/settings), so the surface area is small.
**Context:** Brandon wanted his AI's memory to live in **his** system, not a provider's, so it's portable across AI vendors and unifies with everything else Ledgr holds. The design (worked out in-session) landed on a two-layer model: tiny always-on **stumps** (an index the assistant carries each session) over deep, **linked** memories pulled on demand — where Ledgr's existing relation graph is the serendipity engine (a memory about a person is a doorway into everything related to that person). Key sub-decisions: keep it *deterministic* (the AI decides what to remember; no model in the plumbing); make the whole thing opt-in so a plain MCP client is unchanged; and let recall follow the graph with judgment rather than a fixed depth.
**Decision.** Five reuse-first pieces:
1. **A `memory` item type** (migration `0040_memory_type.sql` + `seed.mjs`, additive `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`). Bespoke, `hidden=true` — so it's out of every Work surface, the destination picker, and the generic MCP `list_types` (an AI/system concern, like `unmarked`), while `getType` still renders `/list/memory` and Build → Types (`includeHidden`) still lets the owner add their own properties on top. Built-in properties: `kind` (user|feedback|project|reference), `horizon` (evergreen|seasonal|episodic), `pinned` (checkbox). "About" links use the **universal** relations, not a typed relation field, so a memory can point at a person *and* a project *and* a note.
2. **Two gated MCP tools** (`src/lib/mcp/tools.ts`): `get_memory_stumps` (body-free index — id/title/kind/horizon/pinned + up to 4 linked neighbours via the batched `relatedSummaryFor`; default returns the always-on set, `includeAll` the whole store) and `remember` (one call: create the memory + set the facets + link `about` ids). `getMemoryStumps` lives in a new `src/lib/memory.ts`, shared with the Build page. Reads/writes go through the same `queryViewItems`/`createItem`/`relateItems` as the rest of the app.
3. **A `memory-protocol` MCP resource** (`ledgr://guide/memory-protocol`, `guide.ts`): the recall rule and write conventions written once so any connected AI follows them.
4. **A master setting `aiMemoryEnabled`** (default **off**, `users.settings` jsonb). Off ⇒ `listToolDefs`/`callTool` filter the two tools, `resources/list`+`resources/read` hide the protocol, and the Build sidebar drops the entry — a vanilla MCP client sees nothing. A toggle in User Settings; `listToolDefs` became owner-aware (async) to gate.
5. **A Build → AI Memory surface** (`/build/memory`, MAINTAIN, labelled to read as an AI/maintenance tool, not Work). Shows the live stump index (always-on vs pull-only) and links to `/list/memory` for full CRUD (generic list + multi-select for free). Gated: off ⇒ an enable prompt; the sidebar entry is hidden via a new `gatedBy` field on `BuildEntry`, threaded `Nav → NavShell → BuildSidebar`.
**Recall model (in the protocol resource): a rising bar, not a hop cap.** Follow a link only when it may change what you'd say/do; the bar rises with each hop out; relevance outranks distance; stop at diminishing returns. Chosen over a fixed "≤N hops" so a rich trail can run long while a cold one is refused early.
**Why / alternatives:** *Store memories as local Markdown files* (the built-in memory feature) — rejected as the deep store: flat files have no relation graph, which is the whole point; kept only as the model for orphan working-preferences, which gain nothing from links. *A `SessionStart` hook that queries Ledgr* — deferred: the stump read is one cheap body-free call at session start, cached thereafter, and Ledgr-direct works identically on every device (phone included) with no per-machine cron or sync; a local cache is a later optimization if session-start latency ever bites. *A typed relation field for "about"* — rejected: typed fields lock to one target type; universal relations let a memory link anything. *A hard hop limit for recall* — rejected for the rising-bar heuristic (more serendipity, still bounded). *Show the memory type in normal type lists* — rejected: `hidden=true` keeps it out of Work while staying editable in Build and browsable at `/list/memory`. *Episodic facts as memories* — discouraged in the protocol: a one-time event is better as an ordinary linked item; memories are the durable distillations.
**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; `verify-mcp.mts` updated for the async `listToolDefs(ownerId)` and asserts the memory tools are **absent** for a settings-less owner (gating on by default-off). Full end-to-end (toggle on → tools/resource appear, `remember` writes a linked memory, `get_memory_stumps` returns it, Build page renders) pending the verify phase; the additive migration is applied to prod on Brandon's explicit go (local env = prod DB).
**Affects:** new `drizzle/0040_memory_type.sql`, `scripts/seed.mjs` (type row); new `src/lib/memory.ts`; `src/lib/settings.ts` (`aiMemoryEnabled`); `src/components/settings/SettingsForm.tsx` (toggle); `src/lib/mcp/tools.ts` (2 tools + owner-aware gating), `src/lib/mcp/server.ts` (await + resource gate), `src/lib/mcp/guide.ts` (protocol resource); `src/lib/build-nav.ts` (`gatedBy` + entry), `src/components/nav/{BuildSidebar,NavShell,Nav}.tsx` (thread the flag); new `src/app/build/memory/page.tsx`; `scripts/verify-mcp.mts`. Reversible: the setting defaults off (feature invisible); the type row is additive and its items soft-delete like any other. **Scope boundary (defer-by-hiding):** no local stump cache, no `remember`-by-name create-on-miss (link by id for now), and the power-user surfaces (destination picker, command palette, `describe_workspace`) still list the Build entry when the feature is off — only the sidebar doorway + the tools/resource/page are gated. All additive later.

### ADR-137 addendum (2026-07-02) — AI Memory improvements: activation + hygiene
**Status:** accepted (Brandon-directed, built). Additive-only within the existing ADR-137 contract; **Tyler heads-up in `COLLAB.md`** (touches the MCP instructions/resource text, still gated behind `aiMemoryEnabled`, no new tool/schema/protocol-version). Follows a review of the subsystem: the design was sound but had an activation gap and no maintenance loop.
**Decision.** Four reuse-first changes:
1. **Owner-aware connect-time instructions.** `server.ts` gains `buildInstructions(ownerId)`; `initialize` now returns the base `INSTRUCTIONS` plus a short **memory addendum** (call `get_memory_stumps` at session start, file with `remember`, read the protocol resource) **only when `aiMemoryEnabled`**. This is the fix that actually gets the feature used: the connect-time instructions are the one surface every MCP client reliably shows the model, whereas tool descriptions are only read once a tool is under consideration and resources are rarely fetched unprompted. When AI Memory is off, the instructions are **byte-identical** to before (verified), so a vanilla client is unchanged.
2. **A "Maintain the store" section in the memory protocol** (`guide.ts`): update-over-duplicate (check loaded stumps before filing a near-duplicate; `update_item` the existing one), enrich links with `relate_items`, touch a still-true seasonal memory to keep it always-on, correct-in-place / flag-for-owner-removal (no silent drops), and prefer few dense memories over many thin ones. Closes the write-only gap — the protocol taught *when to remember* but never *how to revise*.
3. **Per-horizon aging windows** (`memory.ts`): the single 45-day always-on window split into `seasonal: 45` / `episodic: 10` (evergreen/pinned still never age). "A moment" now actually ages faster than "a while."
4. **`remember` partial-link hardening**: new exported `assertOwnedItems(ownerId, ids)` (one batched owner-scoped existence check) validates every `about` id **before** the memory is created, so a bad/hallucinated id fails the whole call instead of leaving a memory created-but-unlinked.
**Also:** a one-off live-data fix — the seeded memory titled `Trellis &amp; Vine…` had a double-escaped ampersand in its title (stored literally as `&amp;`); corrected to `Trellis & Vine…` via `update_item` (revision snapshotted). The seed source is a one-off loader outside the repo, so there was no in-repo source to fix; the other 20 titles were clean.
**Explicitly deferred (defer-by-hiding):** AI-initiated retirement (a `forget` tool / MCP soft-delete) — the protocol's "flag it to the owner" path stands until it proves annoying; aging-by-recall (touch on pull); automated consolidation + a Build-page "always-on set is large" nudge; and (unchanged from ADR-137) the local stump cache / SessionStart hook. The privacy angle (a per-memory pull-only/quiet flag so sensitive memories stay searchable but never auto-load) was **declined** as overbuilding, consistent with ADR-075.
**Gating boundary (recorded on purpose):** toggling AI Memory off hides the tools, the protocol resource, the instructions addendum, and the sidebar doorway — but existing `memory` items remain reachable via the generic `search_items`/`get_item` (they're ordinary hidden-type items). "A vanilla client sees nothing" is a statement about the memory *tools/resource*, not about filtering the type out of generic search; data-level hiding was not added.
**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` + eslint clean; `verify-mcp.mts` extended (now covers: instructions omit the addendum when off / gain it when on; memory tools gated; `remember` rejected when off; a bad-`about` `remember` errors and creates **no** memory; the happy path links + `get_memory_stumps` returns it always-on with its neighbour; seasonal survives 11 days while episodic ages out but stays visible via `includeAll`) — **ALL PASS** on the dev Neon branch.
**Affects:** `src/lib/mcp/server.ts` (`buildInstructions` + memory addendum), `src/lib/mcp/guide.ts` (Maintain section), `src/lib/memory.ts` (per-horizon windows), `src/lib/relations.ts` (`assertOwnedItems`), `src/lib/mcp/tools/memory.ts` (pre-validate `about`), `scripts/verify-mcp.mts`. No schema, no migration, no new tool, no protocol-version change, no new dependency.

## ADR-138: Project Type & widget-composed homepages — PJ1: containment + activity log
**Date:** 2026-06-29
**Status:** accepted
**Context:** Tyler's last open v1.0 goal — a Project type that's a hub for tasks/notes/meetings. The PRD (`ledgr-project-type-prd.md`) reframes it as the first adopter of a universal capability: **Types become widget-composed**, where the same widget runs in two scopes (unscoped on a Dashboard, bound to the current record on a Type page). CORE (touches `items`/`relations`/`types`, the type/canvas model, a new platform layer); Brandon agreed to proceed (2026-06-29). Tyler expanded scope: the composable homepage is a per-type capability, not Project-only. Decisions resolved with Tyler: reuse the existing dashboard widget engine (record page = a dashboard focused on the record) not the canvas_layout field grid; Digest ships push-first (outbound email isn't built); fresh installs default the project status_schema to Planning/Active/On Hold/Done while Tyler keeps his Todoist buckets. Built as a slice series **PJ1–PJ11**, one PR each (the E/TPL/T precedent). This entry covers **PJ1** (the spine: containment + the activity log); later PJ slices append their own notes here.
**Decision (PJ1):**
1. **`relations.home boolean not null default false`** + a partial unique index `relations_one_home_per_source_uq ON (source_id) WHERE home`. The containment residence bit from PRD §1: on a child→parent edge, `home=true` is the child's primary residence; `home=false` is surfaced-elsewhere. Orthogonal to `role` (what kind of edge) and `match_state` (trusted vs suggested); the `(source,target,role)` unique is unchanged. "A note is still a note" — containment is purely this edge, no per-parent schema fork. A record has at most one home parent (the partial unique). Default false leaves every existing edge (tags, mentions, typed relation fields, the existing `task→project` edge) untouched and non-home.
2. **Containment via relations, not `parent_id`.** `parent_id` stays reserved for subtasks + recurrence occurrences (schema.md §10). A Project contains tasks/notes/meetings/milestones/typed records through home edges. New `setHome(ownerId, child, parent, role="contains")` (tasks keep `role="project"`); `relateItems` gains an optional `{home}`; both clear any prior home edge first so the invariant holds. `homeParentOf()` resolves the single home parent.
3. **`activity_events` table** (+ `activity_kind` pgEnum) — the append-only, owner-scoped log the PRD calls its most important table; Recent Activity, the Digest, and the Story weave all read from it. Subject = the record narrated (a project); actor = what triggered it (a completed task) when distinct. Indexed `(subject_id, occurred_at)`, `(owner_id, occurred_at)`, and a partial `WHERE kind='checkin_reviewed'`. `subject_id` cascades on delete (purge stays complete); `actor_id` SET NULL.
4. **Emission in the server write paths** (`src/lib/activity.ts` + `items.ts`/`relations.ts`, best-effort/never breaks a save): `record_created` (tracked types), `status_changed` (a tracked record's own status, payload from/to), `task_completed` (a contained item moving to the done category, on its tracked home parent), `task_added`/`note_added`/`milestone_added`/`record_related` (containment via `setHome`). A "tracked subject" is `isTrackedSubjectType` = `project` for now (pursuit + Digest-on types join later). **Inbox items with no tracked home parent log nothing** — keeps the log a project narrative, not a global firehose.
5. **`last_reviewed_at` is derived** (max `occurred_at` of `checkin_reviewed`, served by the partial index), not a column; `reviewCheckin()` writes the event and resets the staleness clock the Digest (PJ7) keys off.
**Why / alternatives:** *Reuse the dashboard engine over extending canvas_layout* — the dashboards engine already models the PRD's "same widget two scopes" via `focusItemId`/`applyFocus`, so a record page is a focused dashboard with no widget-side Type-branching; canvas_layout's cards are fields of one item (wrong granularity, no query/focus). *`home` as a boolean not a `home|referenced` enum* — it's one bit; boolean default-false is migration-cheap and avoids a pgEnum extension later. *`activity_kind` as pgEnum (vs text like `status`)* — activity kinds are a closed, code-owned vocabulary, so an enum gives the narrator switch compile-time exhaustiveness. *Derive `last_reviewed_at`* — matches Ledgr's derive-don't-store discipline (ADR-109 plan-date). *Don't log inbox-task completions* — the log is a container narrative; logging homeless items would make it a firehose.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-containment.mts` 11/11 + `scripts/verify-activity-log.mts` 13/13 on live Neon (home set/move/invariant, Related panel carries home, containment activity on tracked-only parents, owner-scoping; record_created/status_changed/task_completed emission gated correctly, checkin resets the derived clock, newest-first). `verify-relations`/`verify-items`/`verify-recurrence` regress green; tsc/eslint/`next build` clean. Migration 0034 applied to Neon.
**Affects:** `src/db/schema.ts` (`activity_kind` enum, `relations.home` + index, `activity_events` table), `drizzle/0034_solid_leech.sql`, new `src/lib/activity.ts`, `src/lib/items.ts` (emission in createItem/updateItem), `src/lib/relations.ts` (`setHome`/`clearHomeEdges`/`relateItems({home})`/containment emission + `home` in the Related select), `scripts/verify-containment.mts` + `scripts/verify-activity-log.mts`. Merged to main (2026-06-29; Tyler dropped the both-agree merge gate for this chunk — Brandon agreed to proceed).

### PJ2 (2026-06-29) — record base fields + project status default
**Decision:** `items.next_action_task_id` (uuid → items, ON DELETE SET NULL) + `items.next_action_text` (the record's single pinned next step — a task pointer that auto-advances on completion, or free text); `items.composition` jsonb (Layer 3 per-record widget override, null = inherit) + `types.default_widgets` jsonb (Layer 2 per-type default composition). All three `items` columns ride `itemColumns` (getItem only, never lists). New `initialStatusKey(schema)` (`src/lib/status.ts`): a new item prefers the schema's first explicitly-default NON-terminal status, so a type whose working default is `in_progress` (a Project's Active/Ongoing) starts there instead of a `not_started` bucket; `createItem` uses it (task/note unchanged). Project status (migration 0035 data step): fresh/unused instances adopt the PRD §5 default **Planning/Active/On Hold/Done**; in-use instances keep their buckets but the category-mapping bug is fixed (working status `not_started`→`in_progress`). Non-destructive + idempotent; `seed.mjs` default updated.
**Why / alternatives:** *Next Action as columns* — the PRD puts it on the base; it's hot and a free-text variant has no edge home. *Project status keep-vs-replace* — resolved with Tyler: new users get the generic PRD states, existing users keep their buckets (mapping fixed); `NOT EXISTS project items` + `@> ongoing` guards discriminate without clobbering a customized schema. *`archived`* — deferred to Brandon's `items.archived_at` axis (PJ7), not forked.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-record-base.mts` 18/18 on Neon; `verify-statuses`/`verify-items`/`verify-project`/`verify-views` regress green; tsc/eslint/`next build` clean. Migration 0035 applied. (Fixed a pre-existing dev-DB drift: the project type's `property_schema` had been emptied — restored repo/liveurl/stack per 0031.)
**Affects:** `src/db/schema.ts`, `drizzle/0035_overrated_warpath.sql`, `src/lib/items.ts`, `src/lib/item-input.ts`, `src/lib/status.ts`, `scripts/seed.mjs`, `scripts/verify-record-base.mts`.

### PJ3 (2026-06-29) — widget registry + composition layers + home-scoped queries
**Decision:** New pure, client-safe `src/lib/widgets.ts` — the `WidgetDefinition` catalog (PRD §6, 14 widgets: overview/status/tasks/notes/meetings/milestones/relatedRecords/links/people/mindmap/nextAction/progress/recentActivity/timeline) with `kind`/`requires`/`cardinality`/`scope`/`options`/`recordQuery`, plus **Layer-1 derived availability**: `availableWidgets(type)` returns the WHOLE catalog for every type by construction (every `requires` key is satisfiable — universal base properties + universal containment + global log/relations), so a new Type inherits the catalog with zero widget authoring. New pure `src/lib/composition.ts` — Layer-2 (per-type default) + Layer-3 (per-record) shapes (`Composition`/`RecordWidget`, reusing the dashboard grid cell), tolerant `parseComposition`, `reconcileComposition` (drop removed widgets), `resolveComposition` overlay (record → type → generated, the `resolveLayout` pattern), the default **Project** composition (PRD §8 header strip + center + thin Tasks rail) with Digest-on, and gear helpers (`addableWidgets`/`isWidgetEnabled`); disable = `hidden:true` (hide-not-delete). `ViewFilter` gains **`relatedHome`** + **`relatedRole`** — a containment refinement of `relatedTo` (directional child→parent home edge) so a record-scoped Tasks/Notes widget surfaces what LIVES on the record, not everything related; additive, existing `relatedTo` behavior unchanged when unset. The `resolveRecordWidgets` rendering fan-out is deferred to PJ4 (where the canvas consumes it).
**Why / alternatives:** *Catalog as code, not a DB table* — mirrors the module registry; the catalog is code-owned and the gear reads it. *Availability derived, not curated* — the PRD's Layer 1; the explicit `SATISFIABLE` set is the one place a future type-capability gate would live. *Composition parse tolerant + overlay* — matches `canvas-layout.ts`/`dashboards.ts` so a malformed blob degrades to the default, never errors. *relatedHome directional* — "what lives here" is the child→parent home edge, distinct from the direction-blind `relatedTo`.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-widget-catalog.mts` 22/22 on Neon (availability is whole-catalog for any type incl. an unknown one; record-only vs both-scope widgets; default composition incl. §8 + Digest; tolerant parse/dedupe/reconcile/overlay precedence; live home-scoped + role-scoped queries return only contained children). `verify-views`/`verify-dashboards`/`verify-project`/`verify-list-lenses`/`verify-embedded-views` regress green; tsc/eslint/`next build` clean. No migration.
**Affects:** new `src/lib/widgets.ts` + `src/lib/composition.ts`, `src/lib/views.ts` (`ViewFilter` + `viewWhere` + parse), `scripts/verify-widget-catalog.mts`.

### PJ4 (2026-06-29) — widget canvas shell + gear (project page is widget-composed)
**Decision:** A `widget-home` capability (registered in `coreModule`, canvasId `widgets`) routes a type's records through the new `WidgetCanvas`; `module-wiring.tsx` maps `widgets` → `WidgetCanvas`; migration 0036 + `seed.mjs` set the `project` type's `capability='widget-home'` (so `canvasIdForType` resolves it via the existing ADR-051 SPIKE capability seam — any type adopts it in PJ10, zero new routing). New server `src/lib/record-widgets.ts` `resolveRecordWidgets(ownerId, record, composition)` — DashboardView's per-widget fan-out generalized to record scope: each collection/relation widget binds `relatedTo = record.id` (home-scoped + role-scoped for contained collections via PJ3's `relatedHome`/`relatedRole`; people are direction-blind), derived/property widgets read the base + activity log; Progress is indeterminate at zero tasks (never 0%). `WidgetCanvas` (server) resolves the composition (record → type → generated §8 default), fans out, renders the title (`ItemEditor`) + each widget in its saved lg grid position; bodies = Overview (editable body), Status pill, home-scoped collection lists, Next Action, Progress bar, Recent Activity. `WidgetGear` (client) is the "Customize" surface — section 1 (which-widgets: enable/disable = hide-not-delete, the first edit lazily materializes the full resolved composition onto `items.composition`; reset = composition null). `types.defaultWidgets` exposed raw on `TypeDefinition`.
**Why / alternatives:** *Capability seam over adding project to coreModule.types* — keeps project a normal DB type, opt-in, and generalizes to PJ10. *Render in saved positions (no RGL drag yet)* — defer-by-hiding: the §8 layout reads right via a 12-col grid; interactive drag-arrange is a follow-up, not v1-blocking. *Tasks/Notes read-only here* — editable bodies are PJ5; PJ4 is the shell.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-widget-canvas.mts` 17/17 on Neon (project routes to widgets; born with the §8 defaults; fan-out is home-scoped — Tasks widget shows the contained task, not an unrelated one; disable hides + keeps the item + re-enable restores; reset clears; Next Action + Recent Activity read base/log). `verify-types`/`verify-canvas-seam`/`verify-bespoke-capability`/`verify-project` regress green; fixed a stale `verify-module-registry` assertion (task has its own canvas since ADR-108). tsc/eslint/`next build` clean. Migration 0036 applied. In-browser eyeball deferred.
**Affects:** `src/lib/modules.ts` (capability), `src/lib/module-wiring.tsx` (canvas map), `src/lib/types.ts` (defaultWidgets), `drizzle/0036_project_widget_home.sql` + journal, `scripts/seed.mjs`, new `src/lib/record-widgets.ts` + `src/components/canvas/WidgetCanvas.tsx` + `WidgetGear.tsx`, `scripts/verify-widget-canvas.mts`.

### PJ5 (2026-06-29) — editable collection widgets + milestone type
**Decision:** New `milestone` system type (migration 0037 + seed): a polymorphic collection item with NO done-state — date = `due_date`, upcoming/passed derived from the clock, `status_mode='none'`, hidden + out of quick capture; attaches to ANY type via a home edge. Next Action auto-advance (`items.ts` done-block + `advanceNextActionIfPinned`): completing the home parent's pinned task advances `next_action_task_id` to the next open contained task (ordered by creation) else clears it — a direct owner-scoped write (no `updateItem` recursion). `POST /api/records/[id]/contain` — the one write path behind the editable widgets (create + home-contain; tasks role "project", else "contains"). Three client widget bodies: `TasksWidget` (add / check-off / pin-as-Next-Action), `NotesWidget` (scratch capture bar → untitled note on blur/Enter, then clears — PRD §6 one-surface-two-states), `MilestonesWidget` (add label+date, derived passed/upcoming badge), wired into `WidgetCanvas`.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-record-widgets.mts` 11/11 on Neon (milestone type props; polymorphic attach to a non-project parent; no done-state; pin auto-advance incl. a non-pinned completion leaving the pin alone; milestone fan-out). `verify-items`/`verify-recurrence`/`verify-record-base`/`verify-widget-canvas`/`verify-activity-log` regress green; tsc/eslint/`next build` clean. Migration 0037. In-browser eyeball deferred.
**Affects:** `drizzle/0037_milestone_type.sql` + journal, `scripts/seed.mjs`, `src/lib/items.ts` (auto-advance), new `src/app/api/records/[id]/contain/route.ts` + `src/components/canvas/widgets/{Tasks,Notes,Milestones}Widget.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/WidgetCanvas.tsx`.

### PJ6 (2026-06-29) — derived lenses → the usable project page
**Decision:** Progress is hierarchical (PRD §6): a leaf task is 0/1, a parent's fraction is the average of its task-children's fractions (recursive over the `parent_id` subtree via `listSubtree`), and the bar is the average of the top-level contained tasks' fractions; `flat` weighting stays done/total. Zero tasks → indeterminate (null, never 0%); 100% suggests Done but the project is never auto-forced. Deep-compute is capped (200 top-level tasks) so a large forest can't fan out unbounded. Next Action + Recent Activity bodies were wired in PJ4. **This reaches the PRD "shippable project page" milestone (end of phase 2): a project is born with default widgets, arrangeable via the gear, Tasks/Notes editable, milestones + derived lenses live.**
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-derived-widgets.mts` 10/10 on Neon (indeterminate-at-zero; hierarchical 0.5 vs flat 0 on a half-done subtree; 3-level recursion; 100% not auto-forced; Next Action title + activity lines). `verify-widget-canvas`/`verify-record-widgets`/`verify-subtasks` regress green; tsc/eslint/`next build` clean. No migration.
**Affects:** `src/lib/record-widgets.ts` (hierarchical progress + `nodeFraction`/`rootFraction`), `scripts/verify-derived-widgets.mts`.

### PJ7 (2026-06-29) — Digest / check-ins behavior (push-first)
**Decision:** The Digest is a behavior, not a widget (PRD §7) — it pings about projects gone quiet (staleness) or with a milestone coming up; deterministic, no model (Principle 3). Pure `src/lib/digest/compose.ts`: digestStatus (staleness wins over upcoming; no-activity-ever = dont nag; a recent review resets the clock), composeDigest (the PRD payload from Recent Activity + Milestones + Next Action), daysUntil. `src/lib/digest/notify.ts` runDigestNotify selects project items whose resolved composition has behaviors.digest.enabled, computes staleness (derived lastActivityAt/lastReviewedAt) + upcoming contained milestones, composes, pushes via the existing sendToOwner/WebPushSender, dedups one ping per staleness window (a properties.notify.digestNotifiedAt stamp, the prepNotifiedAt pattern). /api/machine/notify-digest cron + a daily vercel.json entry. activity.ts gains lastActivityAt. The review-resets-clock loop is already first-class (PJ1 checkin_reviewed → derived last_reviewed_at).
**Why / alternatives:** Push-first, email deferred — push is built + reachable; outbound email is not built, so it is a flagged fast-follow behind a future MailSender seam (the compose/select logic is channel-agnostic; reverses the PRD §7 email-first guess). No new notifications table — origin/main already ships the notifications table (ADR-129/130); a duplicate on the stale local base would be throwaway, so PJ7 only pushes + stamps and reuses that table at integration (a known reconciliation). Staleness over a dumb timer — the activity log makes quiet the smart trigger.
**Verification:** scripts/verify-digest.mts 16/16 on Neon — pure status/payload/daysUntil + live (under a THROWAWAY owner so real projects are untouched): fresh-doesnt-ping, stale-pings, dedup, upcoming-milestone-pings, recent-review-resets. verify-activity-log/verify-push/verify-containment regress green; tsc/eslint/next build clean. In-browser (a real push landing) deferred.
**Affects:** new src/lib/digest/{compose,notify}.ts, src/lib/activity.ts (lastActivityAt), new src/app/api/machine/notify-digest/route.ts, vercel.json, scripts/verify-digest.mts.

### PJ8 (2026-06-29) — Overview weave (two-zone Head/Story)
**Decision:** The Overview is one markdown body in two zones (PRD §6): the Head (evergreen, overwritten) and the Story (accreting, a readable post-mortem). New `src/lib/overview/weave.ts`: splitHeadStory/appendToStory (a "## Story" section, the Head untouched), buildStorySkeleton (dated bullets from activity, oldest-first), gatherUnwoven (events since the last weave), weaveStory (append + version + emit overview_woven), proposeStoryUpdate. GET/POST `/api/records/[id]/weave` (propose the editable skeleton, accept the edited lines). updateItem auto-snapshots the body change so each weave is versioned; overview_woven advances the derived last_woven_at (activity.ts gains lastWovenAt). Principle 3 / ADR-087: deterministic parts in-app; the optional prose polish (skeleton → narrative) is a Claude-over-MCP step, NOT an in-app LLM call (no new dependency); pure-auto narration rejected.
**Verification:** scripts/verify-overview-weave.mts 14/14 on Neon (pure split/append/skeleton; live propose-gathers-only-post-weave, weave appends + keeps Head + advances clock + snapshots a revision). Regressions green; tsc/eslint/build clean. The in-widget editing UI is a follow-up.
**Affects:** new src/lib/overview/weave.ts, src/lib/activity.ts (lastWovenAt), new src/app/api/records/[id]/weave/route.ts, scripts/verify-overview-weave.mts.

### PJ9 (2026-06-29) — containment up (Pursuit + Related Records + roll-up)
**Decision:** Pursuit is a widget-composed Type one scope up (PRD §1) — contains Projects via home edges the same way a Project contains tasks; not special-cased (carries widget-home, is a tracked subject). pursuit type (migration 0038 + seed). Roll-up in record-widgets.ts: a record that contains projects shows Progress = average of its projects fractions (done = number complete, total = number of projects), Recent Activity = the union of its own + its projects logs (new activity.listActivityForSubjects), Next Action = the first contained project next step when the record has none. A plain project (contains tasks, not projects) is unaffected. Related Records honors the type-filter option + the home flag. isTrackedSubjectType now includes pursuit.
**Verification:** scripts/verify-pursuit-rollup.mts 10/10 on Neon (routing; containment; type-filtered Related Records; Progress avg; activity union; Next Action roll-up). Regressions green; tsc/eslint/build clean. Migration 0038.
**Affects:** drizzle/0038_pursuit_type.sql + journal, scripts/seed.mjs, src/lib/activity.ts, src/lib/composition.ts, src/lib/record-widgets.ts, scripts/verify-pursuit-rollup.mts.

### PJ10 (2026-06-29) — universal per-type homepages (verified)
**Decision:** The widget-composed homepage is a capability ANY type can adopt in Build, not Project-only (Tyler scope expansion). It fell out of the model: PJ4 registered widget-home as an attachable capability + Layer-1 availability is universal, so the existing ADR-051 capability seam already lets a user attach "Widget homepage" to any type → it routes to the widget canvas, inherits the whole catalog with zero widget authoring, and gets a generated default composition (an authored types.default_widgets wins when present). No new code.
**Verification:** scripts/verify-type-homepage.mts 6/6 on Neon (widget-home is attachable; an arbitrary type routes to widgets + inherits the full catalog + gets a default; an authored Layer-2 default is honored). The acceptance criterion "a new Type needs zero widget authoring" is met. Follow-up: a visual Build "Design homepage" editor for default_widgets.
**Affects:** scripts/verify-type-homepage.mts (verification only).

### PJ11 (2026-06-29) — Mindmap + Timeline widgets
**Decision:** Timeline (derived): a read-only overlay of the record Meetings + Milestones by date, shown together without merging their data (PRD §6) — fan-out queries contained events + milestones, the body renders a dated kind-tagged list. Mindmap (collection, cardinality one): surfaces the record contained mindmap(s) linking to the existing MindmapCanvas, via the generic collection path (the mindmap module is reused, not reimplemented). v2 node-promotion (graph node → task/note/milestone) is explicitly deferred.
**Verification:** scripts/verify-graph-widgets.mts 3/3 on Neon (timeline overlays + date-sorts a meeting + milestone; mindmap widget lists the contained mindmap). Regressions green; tsc/eslint/build clean.
**Affects:** src/lib/record-widgets.ts (timeline fan-out), src/components/canvas/WidgetCanvas.tsx (timeline body), scripts/verify-graph-widgets.mts.

## ADR-139: Live item tokens — `{{item.*}}` in the canonical body, resolved at render time
**Date:** 2026-07-02
**Status:** accepted (Brandon; **Tyler ack pending** — flagged in `COLLAB.md`). **CORE** — extends the canonical body format (the `{format, text}` contract): a markdown body may now carry *live tokens* that are derived from the item's current state, not literal text. First slice (LT1) of the plan in `explorations/live-item-tokens.md`.
**Context:** Brandon (2026-07-02) wants a body that pulls in the item's own facts and its relations so he never edits the same thing twice: a paper whose printed/exported body carries the due date from its property; a `[Title]`-style token echoing the item title; a note that lists its related people. The 2026-06-20 templates redesign (ADR-093) already covers the *apply-time* half (bake `{{today}}`/`{{ask:}}` once when a template stamps an item). What's new is the *render-time* half: tokens that stay in the stored markdown and re-resolve every time the body is rendered. That's a body-format extension, not a templates feature — templates inherit it for free because the apply resolver leaves unknown tokens intact, so a prototype's live tokens survive the clone.
**Decision:**
1. **Two resolution times, kept separate.** Apply-time vars (`template-vars.ts`, baked once) and live tokens (`item-tokens.ts`, resolved per render) are distinct namespaces and distinct code. A live token is always `{{item.*}}`, `{{parent.*}}`, `{{item.children}}`, or `{{item.related.<key>}}`; anything else (including apply-time vars) passes through the live resolver untouched. This is what makes the two layers compose on one body.
2. **Grammar (the contract).** Scalars `{{item.title|status|type|url|priority}}`; dates `{{item.due|scheduled|created|meeting}}` with `:iso/long/short/us/day` formats and `±Nd/w/m/y` arithmetic; `{{item.props.<key>}}` (a `YYYY-MM-DD` value gets date treatment, else plain text); lists `{{item.children}}` and `{{item.related.<roleOrType>}}` (keyed by BOTH edge role and target type) that render comma-joined inline or as a real `ul`/`ol` list **only when the token is alone on its line**; `{{parent.*}}` for subtask bodies; `\{{…}}` escapes. Full table in the exploration doc.
3. **Pure resolver + DB context, mirroring the templates split.** `src/lib/item-tokens.ts` is pure/client-safe (the caller passes `todayYmd` + a plain context), so it's node-testable and can back a client preview later. `src/lib/item-tokens-service.ts` (`buildItemTokenContext`) does ONE owner-scoped, **body-free** read of the item + parent + children (authoring order) + outgoing relations — never another item's body (the list-query rule).
4. **Related/children ride the mention pipeline.** A list token emits `[@Title](ledgr://item/<id>)`, the exact mention-link shape (`mention-markdown.ts`). Callers resolve tokens **before** collecting `@`-mentions, so token-emitted links land in the mentions map and render type-aware (glyph + link), and flatten to plain names on print/share like any mention.
5. **Render-only; the token is the source of truth.** Resolution never writes the DB. It runs in `markdownToHtml`'s callers: `/items/[id]/print` (Save Offline), `/share/[token]`, and `/api/render-markdown` (the live Preview, which gained an optional `itemId`). **FTS strips tokens** (`markdownToText`) rather than indexing a resolved value that would silently go stale.
6. **Back-compat + additive.** A body with no live tokens renders byte-identical; chordpro (non-markdown) bodies are not token-resolved in v1; no schema change, no migration.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) bake live values into the body on save (rejected — defeats the whole "edit once" point and goes stale on rename/re-date); (b) resolve inside `markdownToHtml` with the token context passed through (rejected — the mentions map is built by the caller and must see post-resolution text, so callers own the ordering); (c) `[Title]` square-bracket syntax (rejected — collides with markdown link labels).
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-item-tokens.mts` 58/58 (pure grammar: every token kind, date math/format, inline vs block lists, escaping, unknown/apply-time passthrough; + live Neon: context fields, children order, owner-scoping of the item and of related targets, and `resolveItemBodyTokens` rewriting title + body). `verify-body-contract`/`verify-body-modes` green; tsc/eslint/`next build` clean.
**Affects:** src/lib/item-tokens.ts (new), src/lib/item-tokens-service.ts (new), src/lib/markdown-render.ts (unchanged — callers orchestrate), src/app/items/[id]/print/route.ts, src/app/share/[token]/route.ts, src/app/api/render-markdown/route.ts, src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownPreview.tsx + BodyEditor.tsx, scripts/verify-item-tokens.mts (new). Follow-ons (non-core): LT2 editor chips, TPL6 apply-time gaps, LT3 export/MCP parity — see `explorations/live-item-tokens.md`.

## ADR-140: `@`-mention linking in Quick Capture and the task-add card
**Date:** 2026-07-02
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-02). **Non-core** — creates ordinary `related` relations through the existing `POST /api/items/[id]/relations`; no schema, body-format, or MCP-contract change, so it ships solo. Builds the parked `explorations/quick-capture-at-mention.md` (post-v1.0 wish).
**Context:** the quick-capture modal had a separate, person-only "Relate to…" box that was easy to miss and failed silently (a best-effort `.catch(()=>{})` relate with no feedback). Brandon wanted the body editor's `@`-mention flow (already shipping: live cross-type search, `/type` narrowing, create-on-miss → a relation) brought to the capture *title* instead, and the extra box removed. The task-add card (`AddTaskCard`, used everywhere a task is created) had its own crude `@name`→assignee regex (preloaded 50 people, one-word match, stripped-on-save even when unmatched); he asked to unify the two `@` behaviors.
**Decision:**
1. **`@` in the capture title opens a live picker over ALL item types**, in both the universal capture card (`SimpleCapture`) and the shared `AddTaskCard`. Reuses the editor's search shape + the `/type` token (`parseTypeToken`/`loadTypes`) and glyphs (`mentionGlyphSvg`). The editor's popup is Tiptap-coupled and can't drop into a plain `<textarea>`, so the logic lives in a **headless hook** `useMentionTypeahead` + shared view pieces `mention-ui.tsx` (`MentionPopup`, `LinkedChips`, `useTypeGlyphs`), used by both surfaces.
2. **Consume-on-select, not strip-on-save.** Picking an item removes its `@query` span from the title *immediately* and adds a removable chip to a "Linked" row; only *resolved* mentions leave the text. An unresolved `@` (e.g. "email me @ 3pm") stays literal (the editor's leading-space guard is reused). This avoids the sentence-mangling and eat-unmatched-tokens bugs of the old strip-on-save task path.
3. **Role = `related`, never body-owned `mention`.** A capture-title link has no body to own it, so it's a plain manual edge (the universal related list, ADR-055/067) that survives on its own — using `mention` would risk a later body save diff-deleting it (`mentions.ts`).
4. **Task `@assignee` retired; `#project` kept.** With `@` now a generic link, the task card's old assign-by-`@` is gone (assignee is marginal in a single-user tool). `#project` stays as the destination shortcut (a different concept, not an association) with its mirror-highlight. The Assignee chip is kept as a labeled placeholder for a future dedicated picker (defer-by-hiding), config-hideable via Quick Add. `finalTitle` now strips only `#[\w-]+`.
5. **Popup anchored under the field** (not caret-following): a caret-pixel mirror hack isn't worth it (Principle 5), and under-field works on mobile. **Offline parity unchanged:** on a failed POST the item still enqueues to the outbox and lands in the Inbox; links are best-effort and skipped offline (no item id yet).
6. **Removed the separate person-only "Relate to…" box** from `CaptureModal`.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) strip `@tokens` on save (rejected — mangles sentences, eats unmatched `@`, no live feedback); (b) reuse the Tiptap mention extension in the textarea (rejected — ProseMirror-coupled); (c) keep `@`=assignee in tasks and pick a new syntax for generic links (rejected — Brandon chose one unified `@`); (d) role `mention` (rejected — body-owned, would be diff-deleted).
**Verification:** tsc + eslint clean; browser-verified in the dev-auth preview against live data — cross-type `@` search, `/person` narrowing (person-only results), the `@ ` literal guard (no popup), consume→chip, two-stage Escape (popup then modal), create-on-miss, and Add creating the item + a `related` edge (confirmed via `/api/items/[id]/related`); on the task path the NL-date mirror highlight ("tomorrow") coexists with the popup and a created task carried its `related` link.
**Affects:** src/components/capture/useMentionTypeahead.ts (new), src/components/capture/mention-ui.tsx (new), src/components/capture/MentionTitleField.tsx (new), src/components/capture/CaptureModal.tsx (person box removed, uses the field, relates chips), src/components/tasks/AddTaskCard.tsx (unified `@`, `@assignee` retired, `#project` kept). Resolves `explorations/quick-capture-at-mention.md`. Follow-ups (non-core): a dedicated assignee picker off the Assignee chip; the 6.14 wish to type `@` mid-body-canvas is already covered by the editor mention flow.

## ADR-141: The token layer — a semantic surface/ink/line vocabulary + a light-mode-ready neutral ramp
**Date:** 2026-07-03
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-03). **Non-core / solo** UI/UX work, but the token layer is a shared visual vocabulary Tyler's modules inherit, so it earns this ADR + a CLAUDE.md working-convention line + a 🟢 COLLAB heads-up (not a both-agree gate — no frozen-core surface is touched). Slice S1 of the unified UI/UX refresh (`explorations/ui-refresh.md`).
**Context:** `globals.css` defined four theme vars (`--background/--foreground/--accent/--ui-scale`) and everything else was hardcoded Tailwind neutrals — ~2,790 `neutral-*` usages across 234 files. That was both the light-mode blocker (no single place to flip) and why surfaces drifted apart visually (each component picked its own grays). Brandon wanted one design language across the four main surfaces and a future light mode that's a variable flip, not a 2,790-site rewrite.
**Decision:** two tiers in `globals.css`, both light-mode-ready, zero visual change in dark mode.
1. **Tier 1 — the neutral ramp as runtime variables.** Tailwind v4's `@theme inline` redefines `--color-neutral-50..950` to point at new `--n-*` CSS vars whose **dark values are Tailwind's own neutral oklch verbatim** — so every existing `bg-neutral-800`/`text-neutral-400`/`border-neutral-700` now resolves through a variable with *identical* output, and a future `.light` class flips the whole app by overriding `--n-*` once.
2. **Tier 2 — a semantic layer refreshed components style from directly:** `bg-surface-{0,1,2,3}`, `border-line`/`border-line-strong`, `text-ink`/`text-ink-muted`/`text-ink-subtle`/`text-ink-faint`, plus `rounded-card` (one unified 10px radius). Borders are one tone *quieter* than the old `border-neutral-800` (`--line`); hover/selection one tone *brighter* (`--surface-2`) — the swap that removes the "wireframe of gray boxes" feel. New/refreshed code adopts these; untouched code keeps its neutral classes (which still flip via tier 1). The `neutral-N → semantic` mapping guide is pinned as a comment block at the top of `globals.css`.
3. **A disciplined type scale** as opt-in `ui-*` classes (`ui-title` 24/600, `ui-section-label` 13/500/caps at ~60% ink, `ui-row` 14, `ui-meta` 12) + an 8px spacing-grid convention, replacing the ad-hoc `mt-5/mt-7/mt-9` mix.
4. **Badge caps** centralized in `src/lib/format-count.ts` (`badgeCount(n, cap=99)` → `"99+"`), replacing the inline `> 99 ? "99+"` checks in the nav.
5. **Light mode = mechanism only this pass.** `.light` overrides the ramp + semantic set + the CanvasSection skin vars; the *theme itself* is a later slice. A dev-only proof screen at `/dev/theme` (gated off in production) renders the same markup dark + light to prove the flip.
**Why / alternatives:** (a) A Tailwind config `theme.extend` mapping (rejected — the project is config-less Tailwind v4, CSS-first `@theme` is the idiom); (b) rewriting all 2,790 neutral usages to semantic tokens now (rejected — huge diff, high regression risk in a named fragile area, and unnecessary since tier 1 makes them flip for free); (c) shipping a full light theme now (rejected — Brandon deferred the theme; only the mechanism is in scope). `@theme inline` (not plain `@theme`) is deliberate: it makes utilities emit `var(--n-800)` directly so the runtime override on `.light` is all that's needed.
**Verification:** tsc + eslint clean; dev-auth preview at 1440px + 375px shows pixel-identical dark rendering (pure indirection); `/dev/theme` renders both panels correctly (semantic tokens AND raw neutral utilities flip, accent stays constant); unstyled-flash check — 5× hard-reload on `/`, `/tasks`, `/list/note` — a single deterministic stylesheet each time (runbook §6a, strict `cssChunking` intact).
**Affects:** src/app/globals.css (token layer, `.light`, type scale), src/app/dev/theme/page.tsx (new, dev proof), src/lib/format-count.ts (new), src/components/nav/NavGlyphs.tsx (uses `badgeCount`). Slice S1 of `explorations/ui-refresh.md`; later slices adopt the semantic classes as they refresh each surface.

## ADR-142: The mobile interaction standard — shared RowMenu + a global undo toast (row actions), extended by SwipeRow + the launcher
**Date:** 2026-07-03
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-03). **Non-core / solo** UI/UX work, but the row-interaction contract is a shared pattern Tyler's list surfaces inherit, so it earns this ADR + a CLAUDE.md working-convention line + a 🟢 COLLAB heads-up (not a both-agree gate). Slices S4 (RowMenu), S5 (SwipeRow), S6 (launcher) of the unified UI/UX refresh (`explorations/ui-refresh.md`); this entry lands with S4 and is extended as S5/S6 ship.
**Context:** every list row carried an always-visible "Trash" text button (`RowAction`), forced visible on touch (`max-sm:opacity-100`) since there's no hover on a phone. The audit found it ate row width and invited mis-taps, and there was no per-row home for the other common actions (complete, focus, schedule) outside the bespoke task surfaces. Brandon's settled decision: row actions move into gestures + a menu, with an undo toast as the safety net (soft-delete already makes a delete recoverable).
**Decision:**
1. **A shared `RowMenu`** (`src/components/lists/RowMenu.tsx`), opened by **right-click** (desktop) and **long-press** (touch, ~450ms, cancelled by a >10px move so scrolling passes through — the shipped kanban touch-drag timing). Actions: **Complete** + **Focus today** + **Schedule** (quick Today/Tomorrow/Next week/pick/clear) for task-like rows (`canComplete`), and **Move to Trash** for every row. Move-to-parent is deferred to the bulk bar (ADR-118) — it needs a target picker. Exposed as both a `useRowMenu(opts)` hook (returns `{handlers, menu}` to attach to any row element — `SubtaskExpandableRow` renders its own `<li>`, so it spreads these) and a thin `<RowMenu>` `<li>` wrapper for plain rows.
2. **The always-visible per-row Trash button is retired** on the refreshed surfaces (generic `/list/[type]`, `/notes`, `/links`); the row now shows only its content, and Trash lives in the menu. (`RowAction` stays for Trash/restore surfaces like the Trash page.)
3. **A global undo toast** (`src/components/ui/ActionToast.tsx`, mounted once in the root layout) driven by a `showToast(text, undo?)` window event. It lives OUTSIDE any list subtree, so it survives the `router.refresh()` that removes the acted-on row — the generalization of the Planner's "parent owns the toast" trick. Destructive/one-way actions (Trash, Complete) fire it with an Undo that re-hits the inverse endpoint (restore, re-toggle).
4. **S5 extends this with `SwipeRow`** (right = Complete, left = Schedule) and **S6 with the pull-up launcher**; both reuse this toast and the same non-destructive-by-default posture (Trash stays in the menu, never a swipe).
**Why / alternatives:** (a) a per-row toast (rejected — unmounts with the row on refresh before the user can click Undo); (b) keeping the visible Trash button (rejected — the audit's specific complaint); (c) a menu built on a dependency like Radix (rejected — Principle 5; a fixed-position popup + outside-click/Esc is enough); (d) putting Move in the menu now (deferred — needs a parent picker the bulk bar already provides).
**Verification:** tsc + eslint clean; dev-auth preview — right-click opens the menu (Trash-only on a person/note/link, full Complete/Focus/Schedule/Trash on a task), the Schedule submenu expands, the global toast renders on-screen with Undo + ✕ and survives refresh, and no visible Trash button remains on rows at 1440px or 375px. Long-press shares the verified `open()` path (synthetic TouchEvents are unreliable in the harness; the timing mirrors the shipped kanban long-press, so device-verify on merge).
**Affects:** src/components/lists/RowMenu.tsx (new), src/components/ui/ActionToast.tsx (new), src/app/layout.tsx (mounts the toast), src/components/subtasks/SubtaskExpandableRow.tsx (optional `menuOptions`), src/app/list/[type]/page.tsx + src/app/notes/page.tsx + src/app/links/page.tsx (RowMenu replaces the visible RowAction trash). Slices S4–S6 of `explorations/ui-refresh.md`.

## ADR-143: The mobile bar and the pull-up launcher are ONE surface (single-panel drawer)
**Date:** 2026-07-04
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-04). **Non-core / solo** UI/UX work; supersedes the two-element launcher of ADR-142/S6 + the S6a bar-swipe. 🟢 COLLAB heads-up only.
**Context:** the launcher was a separate full-bleed sheet that mounted on a swipe threshold and played a one-shot enter keyframe, while the bar was an independent floating pill. That produced the "two elements" feel, a bar/drawer width and icon mismatch, and two reproduced gesture bugs: (1) drag-down dismissal never reset the sheet's `dragY`, and since the component stayed mounted, the stale offset reappeared on the next open — the drawer stuck partially open; (2) `dragY` only updated on downward deltas and release ignored velocity, so swiping UP from that partial state read the stale value and snapped the drawer CLOSED.
**Decision:** one always-mounted, full-width, bottom-flush panel (`Launcher.tsx`): grip row + the bar row (rendered by NavShell, passed in as a prop) + the tile grid. Closed = the panel translated down by the grid's **measured** height (ResizeObserver; content-determined, no fixed vh), so only grip + bar show; the bar is literally the drawer's first row and can never diverge from it. The whole panel is draggable: a touch claims after ~8px of mostly-vertical slop (taps still navigate), tracks the finger 1:1 via direct DOM writes (no per-frame re-render), and on release snaps by velocity first (flick ≳0.4px/ms), else the halfway point. Every gesture reads the panel's LIVE transform, so a drag from any state (closed, mid-settle, open) resolves cleanly — no stuck-partway state is representable. The grid dedupes destinations already visible on the bar row; 5 columns. Scroll isolation is CSS `touch-action` (React root touch listeners are passive, so `preventDefault` is unreliable) + the html overflow lock while open. Backdrop is always mounted, opacity tracks drag progress, tap closes. `prefers-reduced-motion` drops the settle via `motion-safe:` classes. SSR pre-hydration closed state uses a calc() fallback matching the grip+bar height.
**Why / alternatives:** (a) keep two elements and just fix the drag state (rejected — the width/icon mismatch and threshold-then-animate open are structural); (b) a sheet library like vaul (rejected — Principle 5, and the gesture fits in ~120 lines); (c) height animation instead of transform (rejected once the bar went bottom-flush — transform is compositor-only); (d) fixed drawer height (rejected — Brandon's spec: height = contents).
**Verification:** tsc + eslint + next build clean; dev-auth preview at 375×812 with synthetic multi-task touch sequences — 1:1 finger tracking (dy 20/60/100/140 → ty 20/60/100/140), flick-up opens from 50px of travel, flick-down closes, slow release snaps by halfway, backdrop tap closes, the old repro (dismiss-by-drag then reopen) lands at exactly translateY(0), a down-then-up single gesture finishes OPEN, and a mid-settle grab freezes under the finger and resolves; `body[data-editing]` still hides the whole panel, the favorites popover still clears the bar, desktop chrome untouched. Found + fixed in review: the post-drag click-swallow flag now disarms on an 80ms timer, else it ate the next real tap.
**Affects:** src/components/nav/Launcher.tsx (rewritten as the panel), src/components/nav/NavShell.tsx (bar row passed into the panel; S6a swipe detection + the mobile floatingPill variant removed; launcher tiles deduped against the bar row), src/app/globals.css (sheet-enter/backdrop-enter keyframes removed — only the launcher used them).

## ADR-144: One People model on events — role unification, first-class groups, absence as an edge
**Date:** 2026-07-05
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-05 — design session + approved brief). Touches shared components and the relations *role vocabulary* (no tables/columns/enums change, so no `schema.md` edit), plus per-instance data. 🟢 COLLAB heads-up for Tyler: shared surfaces change behavior on events; roles/types are instance data, so an instance without a `group` type or `attending` field simply sees empty strata.
**Context:** an event's people rendered in THREE differently-named places — MeetingPrep "People" (ANY-role person edges), the "Attending" relation field (role `attending` only), and "Linked here → Person" (the complement of Attending). Root cause: template prototypes pre-related people with role `related` while the Attending field wrote `attending`. Separately, groups existed twice in two shapes (a heavily-used "Pastors" *tag* + an unused "Pastors" *person*; an "elders" person sitting inside Attending), and a live rule misfire was found in prod: the Timothy/Brandon check-in rule (attendeeEmail) claimed the All Pastors Meeting because Timothy attends it.
**Decision:**
1. **`attending` is THE attendance role** on event↔person edges, normalized event→person. Prototypes/pin write it (pin.ts); `scripts/backfill-attending-roles.mts` converts the 12 legacy `related` edges (backup-first, `--dry-run` supported).
2. **`absent` is an explicit edge** (event→person): "normally here, wasn't" renders as a struck-through OUT chip instead of a silent gap, and stays queryable ("what did Roger miss?"). Memory, not attendance-tracking — no dashboards.
3. **`group` is a first-class type** (a types-registry row, `scripts/setup-groups.mts`) with one `members` relation field → person. An event is FOR a group via role `group` (reads accept any confirmed role so tag-era edges count). Pastors/Elders/Staff tags retype to groups (their edges are generic rows and survive untouched); the group-impersonating person items are merged/trashed.
4. **One People card** (`EventPeopleCard`) is the only editor for these edges: For row (group chips), Here row (solid attending / struck OUT / dashed ghosts = roster + suggestions, one-tap ✓/✕, "✓ all here" bulk-confirm, 15 inline then "+N more"), "Also mentioned" line (mentions + loose `related` links, read-only). RelatedPanel claims every person/group on events; MarkdownCanvas hides person-target relation fields on events (the field *definition* stays for views/filters).
5. **The pull lens becomes presets**: "Show open tasks about: [⬡ group | anyone here | everyone here | custom…]" compiling to the unchanged `properties.taskPull` shape. With a group set and no stored rule, **the group is the default lens**; `@members:<groupId>` is a new additive seed sentinel ("anyone in Pastors"). Recent meetings follow the same idea (group-anchored when set).
6. **attendeeEmail rules only fire on small meetings** (≤3 emails incl. organizer) — fixes the misfire; group meetings match by series/title or a pinned group template.
**Why / alternatives:** group as person-subtype (rejected — formalizes the elders-as-person confusion; person surfaces would all need "is it really a person?" branches); groups stay tags (rejected — no roster, so expected-attendees and anyone-in-group can't exist); markdown-only attendance via a `{{attendees}}` template variable (rejected as source of truth — prose can record an absence but never surface one; kept as a possible TPL3-era snapshot extra).
**Verification:** tsc + eslint clean; verify-meeting-prep / verify-people-suggest / verify-task-pull / verify-event-template-apply all pass (fixtures updated to the attending role + new prep shape); both data scripts dry-run clean against prod (12 edges; 3 tag retypes + 2 person merges + 1 trash).
**Affects:** src/lib/events/people.ts (new), src/lib/events/task-pull{,-service}.ts (@members), src/lib/meetings/prep.ts (strata + presets + group-anchored recents), src/lib/templates/pin.ts (attending + group capture), src/lib/calendar/event-rules.ts (guard), src/components/events/{EventPeopleCard,TaskPullPresets}.tsx (new), src/components/events/TaskPullControl.tsx (member seeds), src/components/meetings/MeetingPrep.tsx (card composition; SuggestedPeople.tsx retired), src/components/relations/RelatedPanel.tsx (event claims), src/components/canvas/MarkdownCanvas.tsx (field hiding), src/app/api/events/[id]/attendance/route.ts (new), scripts/backfill-attending-roles.mts + scripts/setup-groups.mts (new).

**Phase 3 (BUILT 2026-07-05):** (a) the missed-meeting surface — `getMissedMeetings` in people.ts reads the recent PAST events an attendee was marked `absent` from, and prep surfaces them as a "Catch up on what they missed" section in 1:1 prep (auto-hides when no one here has a recent absence — the payoff of recording OUT). (b) `{{attendees}}`/`{{absentees}}`/`{{group}}` LIVE-token aliases (item-tokens.ts, normalized once in splitExpr; block-list regex + catalog updated) mapping to the attending/absent/group relation roles, so a meeting-note template resolves them to the CURRENT roster at render — NOT an apply-time snapshot (notes are usually templated before attendance is marked, and the People card is the source of truth; this reverses the ADR's tentative "snapshot extra" framing for that reason). Verified: verify-item-tokens (79/0, incl. aliases + `{{attendees:ul}}` block), verify-missed-meetings (new, 7/0), verify-meeting-prep still green; tsc + eslint + next build clean. Additional files: src/lib/item-tokens.ts, src/lib/editor/item-token-catalog.ts, scripts/verify-missed-meetings.mts (new). Nothing left deferred.

## ADR-145: Collapsible toggle block + collapsible headings in the markdown editor
**Date:** 2026-07-05
**Status:** accepted (Brandon + Tyler, 2026-07-05). 🟢 Extends the **canonical body format** (a core, both-agree item): the markdown dialect gains a `<details>` disclosure block. Tyler signed off before merge. No schema change — the two new settings ride the existing `users.settings` JSONB (parse-with-default, same posture as `aiMemoryEnabled`). Collapsible *headings* add no format change (view-only).
**Context:** the editor had no way to hide content — long sermon/meeting notes are one flat wall of text. Two related asks: a Notion-style collapsible "toggle" block, and foldable headings. The editor also had no `/` command menu (only `@` mentions and `{{` tokens), so there was no keyboard path to insert blocks.
**Decision:**
1. **Toggle block = a `<details>` disclosure**, three nodes (`toggle`/`toggleSummary`/`toggleContent`). Canonical markdown shape (blank lines are load-bearing so markdown-it renders the inner body while the `<details>`/`<summary>` shell passes through as raw HTML — the existing `html:true` render path, so print/share/export get a native disclosure for free). In-editor parse is a custom **block tokenizer** that claims the whole span before marked's html-block rule can split it at the inner blank line, rebuilding the subtree via the manager's `parseBlockChildren`/`parseInline`. The editing DOM is a `div` NodeView (a real `<details>` hides content from ProseMirror), chevron flips a persisted `open` attr.
2. **Collapsible headings = view-only fold.** Headings stay `# Heading` in the body (nothing serialized), so exports/FTS/render are untouched. A ProseMirror plugin hides the following blocks (until the next heading of level ≤ its own) with a `display:none` node decoration; the content stays in the doc, so copy/selection see it (⌘A grabs a folded section; copying just the heading line does not). `display:none` can strand a caret, so the plugin **auto-expands** any collapsed section the selection wanders into — and, on an explicit fold click, first moves the caret to the heading so the fold isn't self-vetoed.
3. **A `/` slash-command menu** (the first general command palette; hand-rolled over `@tiptap/suggestion` like the `{{` menu, no popup dep — Principle 5). Ships Heading 1/2/3 + Toggle; its own `PluginKey` (a second default-keyed Suggestion throws).
4. **Two settings, both default-on** (`collapsibleHeadingsEnabled`, `toggleBlocksEnabled`). The toggle node type is always registered so existing bodies parse; the settings only gate the *creation* affordances (toolbar button + `/toggle`) and the heading chevrons. The toolbar button is also individually hideable via the existing `editorToolbarHidden`.
**Why / alternatives:** `:::`/fenced container syntax for toggles (rejected — `<details>` is universally rendered incl. our server markdown-it, and needs no new render rule); the first-party `@tiptap/extension-details` (rejected — Pro-licensing uncertainty across versions, and a bespoke node keeps the markdown contract ours); persisting heading-fold state as a node attribute (rejected — can't serialize to markdown, and a fold is a view convenience, not content); a native `<details>` as the editing DOM (rejected — hides content from ProseMirror's selection/coords).
**Verification:** tsc + eslint clean; `scripts/verify-toggle-markdown.mts` (new, 13/0) covers the pure shape + a full MarkdownManager parse→serialize round-trip (caught a real bug: multi-paragraph bodies fused without the `\n\n` block separator). dev-auth browser pass on `/scratch/editor`: heading fold hides/restores its section, toggle inserts (toolbar + `/toggle`) and collapses, live serialize→re-parse round-trips summary/body/open, the `/` menu lists all four commands, and Settings → Editor features renders both switches. Also caught in-browser: a `PluginKey` collision with the `{{` suggestion (fixed). Not exercised: the settings-OFF path (avoided writing to prod settings; the gating is a traced boolean filter).
**Affects:** src/lib/editor/toggle-markdown.ts, src/components/markdown-editor/{toggle-extension,collapsible-headings,slash-suggestion}.ts (new); src/components/markdown-editor/{MarkdownEditor.tsx,toolbar-icons.tsx,markdown-editor.css} (register + toolbar button + settings load); src/lib/settings.ts (two booleans); src/components/settings/SettingsForm.tsx ("Editor features" section); scripts/verify-toggle-markdown.mts (new).
**Known limitation:** nested toggles don't round-trip (an inner `</details>` closes the outer via the lazy match) — uncommon shape; revisit only if needed.

## ADR-146: The Desk — a desktop-only multi-panel workspace
**Date:** 2026-07-06
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-06 — design approved in `plans/desk-multi-panel-workspace.html`). **Non-core / solo:** additive surface only.
