No schema, no `{format,text}` body-contract change, no MCP-contract change, no module-boundary or provider-interface change — so no both-agree needed. 🟢 COLLAB heads-up for Tyler: one new dependency, one new client wire format (localStorage + a `deskWorkspaces` key in the existing `users.settings` JSONB, parse-with-default like `navSlots`, no migration), and a note that `react-grid-layout` and `react-resizable-panels` now coexist (two libraries, two jobs — RGL owns dashboards/arrange grids, RRP owns only the Desk's docking tree).
**Context:** existing surfaces open one item at a time (page or intercept modal). There was no way to put a sermon draft beside its cross-refs, or a meeting note beside the person it's about — the Notion/Obsidian/VS-Code "workspace" idea. Wanted desktop-only (a phone can't usefully tile panels), additive (touch nothing that works), and durable (the arrangement should survive closing the app).
**Decision:** a new client-rendered route `/desk` where items, saved views, and (read-only) dashboards open in resizable, tabbed panels.
1. **Own the model, rent the renderer.** `src/lib/desk/layout.ts` is Ledgr's OWN versioned tree (leaf = a tabset, split = a binary row/col divider storing a **fraction** not pixels; tabs reference items/views/dashboards by uuid). Pure, unit-testable ops (split/close/move/focus/setFrac/sanitize). `react-resizable-panels@^2.1.9` (pinned classic `PanelGroup` API; the published `latest` 4.x is a rewritten API) only draws splits + drag-resize; we do NOT use its `autoSaveId` — the tree is the one persisted format, behind the `DeskShell` seam, so a future renderer swap touches one file and no stored data.
2. **One writer per item, enforced by a doc store** (`desk-doc-store.ts`), never by convention: the focused panel mounts the reused, untouched `ItemEditor` (the only editor); every other panel showing an item is a live read-only `MarkdownPreview` fed by the store. Two mounted editors on one item would both debounce-PATCH and clobber. Focus follows click; the pen moves, never duplicates. The existing debounce/PATCH/revisions save path is untouched — the only editor change is an additive optional `onLiveChange` read-only tap.
3. **Layout is app state, never in the URL.** Existing routes keep their deep-linkable URLs; the Desk arrangement lives in localStorage (`desk:layout`), like VS Code / Obsidian / Logos.
4. **A layout is never lost.** Anything that replaces the live layout (Open beside, load a workspace, restore) first snapshots the outgoing one into a per-device Recent ring (`desk:recent`, ~25, timestamped). Named workspaces are synced (`users.settings.deskWorkspaces`) and one click away.
5. **Reachable from anywhere.** The ADR-142 RowMenu and inline @mentions / item-links (editor + preview) gain "Open in Desk" (adds a tab) and "Open beside" (seeds a two-panel layout), sharing one `DeskSendMenu` + a seed-and-navigate helper; both desktop-gated (fine pointer, ≥640px).
6. **Desktop-only, gated at 640px** (`useIsDesktop`); below it `/desk` renders a plain list of open tabs. Registered in the destination picker only (no default-slot change; ADR-063 opt-in). Chrome styled from the ADR-141 semantic token layer; every bespoke control labeled/tooltipped.
7. **Views (S4) and dashboards (S5) in panels.** A thin body-free `GET /api/views/[id]/items` backs a compact view list (click a row → opens the item as a tab). Dashboards render read-only via a resolver extracted from `DashboardView` into `src/lib/dashboard-resolve.ts` (shared with the full page) + `GET /api/dashboards/[id]/resolved`; the panel renders the same RGL grid with `editMode=false` (drag/resize off — sidesteps the RGL edit-mode quirk), reviving JSON-serialized dates before formatting, with "Edit ↗" opening the full dashboard page.
**Why / alternatives:** a docking library like dockview (rejected for v1 — Principle 5: tabs/zones/persistence are ~small bespoke code, and renting only the splitter keeps the dependency tiny and swappable); serializing panels into the URL (rejected — a workspace isn't a deep link; app state matches the mental model and keeps existing URLs clean); letting each panel host its own editor (rejected — clobbering; the doc store makes one-writer structural); a drag-and-drop gesture for moving tabs (deferred — click-to-place zones ship first and share the `DropTarget` vocabulary a future drag would use); rendering dashboards editable in-panel (rejected — the RGL edit quirk + two-writers-on-one-dashboard; read-only + "edit on the full page" is simpler and safe).
**Verification:** `npm run lint` + `npm run build` clean on every slice. dev-auth preview (real data): 3-panel build via split, divider resize, reload-restore from `desk:layout`; same item in two panels — typing in the focused panel live-updates both read-only twins, network shows one GET + one PATCH stream (no clobber); zone move (center docks, edge splits, collapse + dedupe), Esc cancels with no tree change; Editing/Viewing pills track focus; save a named workspace (persists to settings), load it (restores + snapshots the outgoing to Recent), restore a Recent entry; Send-to-Desk from a list row and from a real @mention in both editor and preview (Open beside seeds current-left/target-right in place — fixed a same-route no-op where the mounted client ignored `router.push("/desk")`, now via a `DESK_LAYOUT_CHANGED` event); tab overflow arrows scroll a 14-tab strip; view panel renders body-free rows and opens an item on click; a dashboard renders static (no `dash-edit`, cursor auto, dates revived, no console errors) and the full `/dashboards/[id]` page still renders after the resolver extraction. Runbook §6a pass: normal + mobile item editor render, favorites popup opens (the `ItemEditor` tap is optional; save path untouched).
**Affects:** new — `src/lib/desk/{layout,persist,send}.ts`, `src/lib/dashboard-resolve.ts`, `src/components/desk/{DeskClient,DeskContext,DeskShell,DeskTabset,DeskItemPanel,DeskViewPanel,DeskDashboardPanel,DeskOpenPicker,DeskMoveOverlay,DeskWorkspacesMenu,DeskSendMenu}.tsx`, `src/components/desk/desk-doc-store.ts`, `src/app/desk/page.tsx`, `src/app/api/views/[id]/items/route.ts`, `src/app/api/dashboards/[id]/resolved/route.ts`; edited — `package.json` (react-resizable-panels), `src/lib/settings.ts` (`deskWorkspaces`), `src/lib/nav-slot-options.ts` (picker entry), `src/components/lists/RowMenu.tsx` + `src/components/markdown-editor/{ItemEditor,MarkdownEditor,MarkdownPreview}.tsx` (send-to-desk + `onLiveChange`), `src/components/dashboards/DashboardView.tsx` (thin wrapper over the extracted resolver), `src/app/layout.tsx` (global send popover mount).

## ADR-147: The Desk, round two — send-menu clarity, canvas sections as panel sub-tabs, in-panel details, and two fixes
**Date:** 2026-07-06
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-06, this session — design agreed in conversation; builds on ADR-146). **Non-core / solo:** additive Desk-surface polish. No schema, no `{format,text}` body-contract change (canvas sections are display over the existing body, ADR-095), no MCP-contract change, no module/provider change. One new read-only aggregation endpoint (`GET /api/items/[id]/details`) and additive optional fields on the localStorage layout tree (`section?` on item tabs, `title?` on view/dashboard tabs, per-tab `showDetails?`), all parse-with-default in `sanitizeLayout`. 🟢 COLLAB heads-up for Tyler: same client wire format, one additive endpoint.
**Context:** first daily use of the Desk (ADR-146) surfaced gaps. (a) A tabbed item (note / `tabs`-capability type, ADR-095) shows no tab UI in a panel — the writer gets the raw body, twins get flattened headings — so you can't read or edit a specific section, let alone put two sections side by side. (b) The full item chrome (custom properties, typed relations, "Linked here", Discover) is omitted from panels with no way to bring it back, which limits the Desk as a working surface (vs. pure reading). (c) "Open beside" from a list row opens beside the Desk's *last focused item* — an invisible, unrememberable anchor — so "beside what?" has no answer. (d) "Open in Desk" is vague. (e) tab-overflow scroll arrows don't appear until a reload/tab-switch. (f) view/dashboard tabs are labeled the literal word "View"/"Dashboard". (g) tab actions (close/move) require the panel's ⋯ menu and can't target an unfocused tab.
**Decision:**
1. **Canvas sections become the panel's sub-tabs, on one line (fixes a + the double-strip tension).** The item's sections (parsed from the live body) render in the panel's own tab strip as small chips *after* a larger item tab that anchors identity, the chips a single zero-gap unit so they read as one control. Only the active item's sections show; other item-tabs in the panel stay collapsed to their name. The content area renders just the active section: the focused (writer) panel drives the reused `TabbedBody`/`ItemEditor` with its internal strip hidden and its active index controlled by the chrome (edit one section, whole-body save path untouched); a read-only twin renders the sliced section via `MarkdownPreview`. Section selection is **per-panel view state** persisted on the item tab (`section?`), so two panels of the same item show different sections side by side (the "mount different tabs next to each other" case) while one-writer-per-body still holds (you edit the section in the focused panel; twins are read-only). Sections are **navigation-only in the Desk**; add/rename/delete/reorder stay on the full-page canvas (defer-by-hiding). Section identity persists by index with a title fallback, snapping to the first section if neither resolves (low-stakes: the strip re-derives from the live body each render). Editing two sections at once is out of scope (would need a block-level co-editing model).
2. **"Show details" in a panel, opt-in (fixes b).** A per-tab ⋯-menu toggle (off by default, persisted `showDetails?`) appends the item's properties + typed relations + "Linked here" below the body at full-canvas parity, via one new client `ItemDetails` component backed by a read-only `GET /api/items/[id]/details` (the existing chrome is a mix of client + server-fetched components — `RelationProperties` is a server component, `RelatedPanel` is server-fed — so one client component over one endpoint is cleaner than mounting the server pieces in the client Desk). Property/relation edits PATCH their own fields, not the body, so they don't touch the one-writer-per-body rule; details are editable only in the focused panel and read-only in twins.
3. **"Open beside" anchors the surface you can see (fixes c).** Invoked from a list/view/dashboard row, it seeds the layout with **the current view as the left column** and the clicked item to its right, and on repeat from the same view **appends a new column** (`[view | A | B]`) rather than rebuilding; the outgoing layout snapshots to Recent (ADR-146 pt 4, unchanged). The row's host surface is threaded down as an optional `DeskTab` (`viewTab`/`dashboardTab` carrying its name); a bare type list with no reusable view id falls back to opening the item alone (flagged, not a new tab kind for v1). Label is contextual: "Open beside this list/view/dashboard".
4. **"Open in Desk" → "Send to Desk" (fixes d).** Same additive behavior (adds a tab to the focused panel), clearer paper-to-desk metaphor.
5. **Tab strip fixes (e, f).** Scroll arrows recompute after paint and observe the inner tab row's growth (late-arriving async labels grow `scrollWidth` without resizing the observed box, so the old `ResizeObserver`-on-viewport never fired). View/dashboard tabs carry a denormalized `title?` captured at open time (the picker already has the name) and render it instead of the literal kind word.
6. **Right-click a tab for its own menu (fixes g).** The ⋯ menu's tab-scoped items (Open in full page / Move tab… / Close tab) extract into a shared component opened on a tab's `contextmenu`, targeting that specific tab id (the `closeTab`/`armMove` ops already take a tabId), without activating it or moving the pen — the panel's focus-on-mousedown is limited to the left button so a right-click no longer steals focus. Panel-scoped actions (Split, Close panel) stay in the ⋯ menu.
**Why / alternatives:** two strips stacked (panel tabs above, canvas tabs below) — rejected, merging onto one line keeps the Desk vibe and item identity prominent; a rigid per-panel section "pin" — dropped for plain per-panel active-section view state (simpler, and repeat-navigation is free); moving a lone section to another panel as a first-class op — rejected (a section isn't a layout node; opening the same item in a second panel and selecting the section is the same result with zero data duplication); mounting the server-side chrome components directly in the client Desk — rejected for one client `ItemDetails` + endpoint; "Open beside" replacing vs. appending — appends on repeat from the same anchor (matches the collect-columns mental model), still non-destructive via Recent.
**Affects:** new — `src/components/desk/ItemDetails.tsx` (client), `src/app/api/items/[id]/details/route.ts`; edited — `src/lib/desk/layout.ts` (`section?` on item tabs, `title?` on view/dashboard tabs, `showDetails?`, an append-column op, `sanitizeLayout` parse-with-default), `src/lib/desk/send.ts` + `src/components/desk/DeskSendMenu.tsx` (rename, host-anchored Open beside, contextual label), `src/components/lists/RowMenu.tsx` + the list/view/dashboard host pages (thread the host `DeskTab`), `src/components/desk/DeskTabset.tsx` (sub-tab chips, tab context menu, left-button focus guard, real view/dashboard labels, arrow recompute), `src/components/desk/DeskItemPanel.tsx` + `desk-doc-store.ts` (item `type` in `DocState`, section-aware writer/twin render, details), `src/components/desk/DeskContext.tsx` + `DeskOpenPicker.tsx` (carry names into view/dashboard tabs), `src/components/markdown-editor/TabbedBody.tsx` (controlled active index + hideable strip), `src/lib/editor/canvas-tabs.ts` (a slice-one-section helper).
**Verification (planned):** per-slice `npm run lint` + `npm run build` clean; dev-auth preview on prod data — a tabbed note shows section chips as one unit, two panels of it show different sections live as you type in the focused one; "Show details" reveals properties/relations/backlinks and edits save from the focused panel; "Open beside" from a list opens `[list | item]` and appends a column on repeat, old layout in Recent; "Send to Desk" adds a tab; overflow arrows appear without a reload as labels load; view/dashboard tabs show their real names; right-clicking an unfocused tab opens its menu without moving the pen. Runbook §6a re-check (editor render, favorites popup, styling load).

## ADR-148: `link_to_line` — an MCP tool for deep links to a body line
**Date:** 2026-07-06
**Status:** accepted (Brandon + Tyler agreed, 2026-07-06). **CORE (both-agree + ADR):** adds a tool to the machine/MCP API contract; Tyler signed off before merge (CLAUDE.md "Building together"). One new read/write MCP tool, no schema change, no body-format change (reuses the ADR-090 `^id` anchor verbatim).
**Context:** the in-app "copy link to this line" (ADR-090 block anchors — a trailing `^id` marker on a line, deep-linked as `/items/{id}#^{id}`) was **client-only**: it lived in the markdown editor toolbar (`ensureAnchorAtSelection`), so a Claude/MCP agent could read a body (and already *see* the `^id` markers `get_item` returns) but could neither mint an anchor on an un-anchored line nor build the URL — the MCP layer had no app-origin concept at all. Brandon wanted an agent to drop direct line-links into chats and other docs.
**Decision:** add one MCP tool, `link_to_line(id, {line | lineText | blockRef})`, that returns `{ url, blockRef, line, lineText, created }`. It resolves the target line three ways in precedence order — an existing `blockRef` you already saw (pure read), a 1-based `line` number (as `get_item` returns the body), or a `lineText` snippet (matched against the line with its anchor **and** leading list/checkbox marker stripped, fenced-code lines skipped; errors on no-match or ambiguity, steering to `line`). If the line already has an anchor it reuses the id (so repeat calls are idempotent and return the same link); otherwise it mints a `uniqueBlockId`, appends ` ^id` to that line, and saves via the same owner-scoped `updateItem` the app uses (snapshotting a revision). Blank lines and lines inside fenced code blocks are refused (a marker there can't be stripped from the human render). Base URL is `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` (same env the Todoist sync uses), so links resolve on prod/local. The anchor logic moved to two **pure, server-safe** helpers in `src/lib/editor/block-anchor.ts` (`findLineByText`, `ensureAnchorOnLine`) that mirror the existing fence-aware stripping and are covered by `scripts/verify-block-anchor.mts`.
**Why / alternatives:** **no AI-provenance marker** on agent-created anchors (Brandon chose "skip it"): an anchor is neutral infrastructure — it points to a line regardless of who created it, and behaves identically to a human-clicked one; flavoring the `^id` would change the canonical body/anchor format (itself core) and complicate the human-render stripping for a marginal signal (the write is already captured in `revisions` if provenance is ever needed). Rejected: folding per-line links into `get_item`'s output (noisy for a whole body, and still can't anchor un-anchored lines); a read-only tool that only builds URLs for already-anchored lines (most lines aren't anchored, defeating the point). Reused the ADR-090 anchor format unchanged rather than inventing a second line-address scheme.
**Affects:** new — `link_to_line` tool in `src/lib/mcp/tools/items.ts`; `findLineByText` + `ensureAnchorOnLine` in `src/lib/editor/block-anchor.ts`; edited — `scripts/verify-block-anchor.mts` (coverage for both new helpers).
**Verification:** `npx tsx scripts/verify-block-anchor.mts` green (reuse-vs-mint, blank/fence/out-of-range refusals, marker-normalized + fence-skipping text match, ambiguity/not-found); `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on the changed files. Live MCP round-trip (mint on a fresh line, reuse on repeat, follow the URL to confirm the scroll-and-flash) pending after Tyler sign-off + deploy.

## ADR-149: Passage hub, lighter — a reference dimension, not 31K verse items (amends ADR-060)
**Date:** 2026-07-06 (proposed as ADR-134; renumbered)
**Status:** **accepted.** CORE (both-agree + ADR) — it touches the relations/association substrate, the mention→relations contract, and the machine surfaces that resolve links. **Brandon + Tyler agreed 2026-07-06** (Tyler via Telegram: the OneDrive backup was the real hit, not the SQL; verses are "literally just a lookup reference," so a lightweight per-verse code beats a row carrying all the item machinery — "you can't write to a specific verse anymore, but we wouldn't do that anyway"). Amends ADR-060, which is kept for the record. Build is module-level and minimal-first (decision pt 6). **Numbering note:** proposed on the `passage-hub-lite-adr-134` branch as ADR-134, but 134 is the cross-device edit guard on main (cited by number in `src/lib/body.ts`), and 135–142 filled in after Tyler's review, so this was logged as ADR-143; but main went on to use 143–148 (mobile-bar launcher through link_to_line) before this merged, so it is logged as **ADR-149** (next free slot). The branch was rebased onto current main before build (Tyler's review pt 1, now actioned). Branch name kept as-is.
**Context:** ADR-060 settled *that* the Bible is the relational hub and *that* references auto-wire; it modeled that as **book→chapter→verse with the verse as an item** (~31,102 verse rows + ~1,189 chapters + 66 books). Brandon's commentary-library import forced a re-examination. **The row count is NOT the reason to change it** — ~31K rows is trivial for Postgres, and the export/browse noise is fixable with an exclusion flag. Two harder problems are the reason:
1. **Owner-scoping.** `items` is *the* owner-scoped table and the schema's first rule is "owner-scope every query." A Bible verse is fixed, shared, read-only reference data, not the owner's authored/editable/soft-deletable/exportable content. Putting it in `items` forces a bad choice: duplicate the whole canon per owner (absurd, and Tyler seeds his own on the shared schema), or carve a non-owner-scoped exception into the one table that must never have one. Every future query then either leaks 31K verses or must remember a third exclusion predicate (beside `deletedAt`/`is_template`) forever.
2. **Migration is one-directional.** Once the commentary library is imported (a large edge set), the storage choice is expensive to reverse. **A reference dimension → verse-items is clean and deterministic (fan any range out into per-verse edges anytime); verse-items → reference dimension is lossy** (you can't reliably reconstruct "this was 8:1–10" from ten separate verse edges). So the information-richer model must be chosen *before* the import, not after. (Weighed across five lenses — perf, maintainability, UX, conceptual integrity, ops/durability — the 2026-07-06 review. The lenses that favored verse-items did so for cheaper up-front reuse; that reuse is undercut by the owner-scope mismatch and the lossy escape hatch.)
**Decision.**
1. **A passage is a reference dimension, not an item.** The Bible is a fixed external ontology (identical for every owner), so it is *not* stored in `items`. Restates the principle: "everything you **author** is an item; a passage is a reference *target*." Verse-atomic item rows (ADR-060 pts 1 & 3) are dropped. This keeps `items` meaning exactly "the owner's content" and keeps the owner-scope invariant unbroken.
2. **Canon = tiny static data.** Not a verse table — a book list + a verses-per-chapter count array (66 books, 1,189 chapters, a few KB), enough to parse, validate ("does Romans have a ch. 17?"), and generate the browse UI. Read-only and shared, so it can't be corrupted by a stray edit/bulk-op and it packages trivially for the local-first build.
3. **Reference = a computed integer + range.** A pure deterministic resolver (the RefTagger parser ADR-060 already called for) maps `"Rom 8:5"` / `"Romans 8.5"` / `"Rom. 8:5–9"` → a canonical id `book·1_000_000 + chapter·1_000 + verse` (Rom 8:5 = `45_008_005`). A passage is a range `[startRef, endRef]`; a single verse is the degenerate range where start == end. **Build the resolver first** — both this model and the verse-item fallback need it, so it is the no-regret starting point that keeps the storage decision reversible in the safe direction.
4. **Links live in a purpose-built `passage_refs` edge table**, not `items` and not `relations`: `{ source_item_id → items.id, start_ref int, end_ref int, role }`, interval-indexed (a GiST/int-range index for true overlap at scale; a plain b-tree is fine at library size). "What touches Romans 8:5" = `start ≤ 45008005 AND end ≥ 45008005`; "what overlaps 8:1–10" = `startA ≤ endB AND startB ≤ endA`. Framed as **a new "passage" mention/relation kind whose values are canon references** — the symmetric analog of ADR-067 storing typed relation fields as `relations` edges. Ranges are stored as one edge (not fanned out to per-verse edges), so a range is a first-class object and no information is lost.
5. **A passage "page" is a virtual view, not a row.** The browse surface (Books→chapters→verses, or a single searchable list) is generated from the static canon; a passage page runs one overlap query against `passage_refs` and lists the items that reference it (commentary chunks, notes, sermons). This same query IS the passage's backlinks. Nothing is seeded, trashed, or exported.
6. **Build it minimally — the durable core now, the registry later.** Ship (a) the resolver + canon data + the `passage_refs` table, and (b) the *one* integration that delivers the value: `@/ref` insertion in the editor + the Related panel showing passage links + the passage page. **Defer** generalizing the relate-button and the other candidate sources into a full linkable-provider registry, and the user-configurable scope label, until they're actually wanted. This answers the maintainability objection: don't build a provider *registry* for a population of one; build the specialized reference index and the seam where it earns its place, and extend only on demand. (The eventual registry would future-proof other non-item linkables — Strong's numbers, dates, an external-directory person — but that is a later YAGNI call.)
**Why / alternatives:** *Verses as items (ADR-060), the strongest alternative* — rejected on owner-scoping (a shared, read-only ontology doesn't belong in the owner-scoped `items` table) and on the lossy migration direction, NOT on row count (rows are cheap). Its one real advantage — reusing the item machinery "for free" — is partly illusory (you pay it back in a permanent exclusion discipline) and is recovered where it matters by wiring the Related panel + `@/ref` (pt 6). *A "system-owned" non-owner-scoped verse-item variant* — rejected: it dodges per-user duplication but bakes a null/sentinel owner and cross-owner relations into the hottest, most-invariant table. *Lazy materialization of verse-items* — rejected: near-total commentary coverage materializes almost everything anyway. *Passage as a value/property on the source only (no edge table)* — rejected: JSONB interval-overlap isn't index-friendly, and "what references this passage" is the core query. *Loosen `relations.target_id` to point at non-items* — rejected: pollutes the item↔item relations invariant; a typed `passage_refs` table keeps relations clean and gives indexable integer intervals.
**Cost to weigh (named for Tyler):** the minimal build still touches the mention→relations contract (a sibling edge-writer/resolver alongside `syncMentionRelations`/`resolveMentions`) and adds a second, specialized linking substrate beside `relations` — hence core. That is the honest price for keeping `items` clean and the migration direction safe.
**Affects (when built, module-level):** a small static canon dataset + a pure passage-ref resolver (first); a new `passage_refs` table + migration + interval index; siblings of `mentions.ts` (`syncPassageRefs`/`resolvePassageRefs`) + the `@/ref` path in `mention-suggestion.ts`; the Related-panel/backlink union; a generated passage browser + passage-page route. Deferred: the full linkable-provider registry (relate picker + other sources), the settings-configurable scope label, and an optional read-only `bible_text` lookup (per translation) if verse text is ever shown — still not items. **Supersedes ADR-060 pts 1 & 3 and its "verse atomic / range = per-verse edges" model; keeps ADR-060's intent (the Bible is the relational hub; references auto-wire deterministically, no AI at runtime).**

**Tyler's review (2026-07-06) — agreed; conditions recorded on top of the acceptance.** Confirming from my side what the Telegram thread settled: I'm in on the reference-dimension model, and minimal-first (pt 6) is the right way to ship it. The clincher for me: we never author *onto* a verse (journals, sermons, and small-group questions are the items; a verse is only ever their target), and verse-level lookup survives fully (Rom 8:1 and Ps 1:5 each resolve to an exact integer; ranges come out cleaner than per-verse fan-out). A few things to fold in:
1. **Renumber + rebase. ✅ ACTIONED (2026-07-06):** "134" is taken on main (the cross-device edit guard, cited by number in `src/lib/body.ts`) and 135–142 filled in after this review, so the ADR is logged as **ADR-149** (143–148 filled on main before this merged; 139 was suggested first, then 143, both taken), and the branch was rebased onto current main before build. Branch name `passage-hub-lite-adr-134` kept as-is.
2. **First extensions after the minimal core (my two asks, on record so they aren't lost):** (a) **keep the ADR-060 auto-tagger** — the deterministic plain-prose scanner that catches refs I type into journals/sermons without hand-tagging — but its edges land **suggested + confirm** and it gets its **own edge role** so the on-save body sync (`syncPassageRefs`, the passage sibling of `syncMentionRelations`) never deletes a tagger-written row; and (b) **the sermon Primary Passage field** — labeled primary-text + cross-reference slots, which is exactly where the deferred registry has to reach **ADR-067 typed relation fields** (`RelationField`/`outgoingRelationsByRole`). Minimal-first is right; these are the next slices, not the first cut.
3. **When the registry does land, it is more than the relate-picker:** **search / the ⌘K palette** and the **MCP tools** also need the passage provider, or passages aren't findable from search and Claude can't read/write passage links (the commentary library leans on the MCP path).
4. **`@/ref` scope-token parsing is net-new** (PR #125 added type glyphs/labels, not scoping), and create-on-miss must be suppressed for the passage scope (you can't "create" a verse).
5. **Pin the canon:** 66-book Protestant, English (KJV-style) versification, with the resolver normalizing translation-specific differences (Hebrew psalm superscriptions, 3 John 14/15), so the integer encoding never shifts under us.
6. **`passage_refs` shape:** `source_item_id` FK `ON DELETE CASCADE`; owner-scope through the join to `items` (as `relations` does) and filter `deleted_at` on the passage-page query; the `ledgr://passage/` URI grammar (dots vs colons, ranges, whole chapters/books) deserves a paragraph since it is now a canonical-body-format concern (core); and name the book → chapter containment choice (`parent_id` vs the ADR-111/138 home-edge model) plus chapter ordering.
7. **Import slice (not this ADR):** check Neon free-tier headroom before industrializing (30-40 volumes ≈ 150-300MB with `body_text` + the tsvector, against a ~0.5GB tier and the ~$0 target), skip revision snapshots on import writes, and flip the faithfulness check to exact string-equality by having the AI emit only boundary offsets + titles + ref locations into the deterministic markdown (the material must be quotable).

## ADR-150: `attach_file` — an MCP tool to add an image or file to an item
**Date:** 2026-07-07
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-07 — Tyler agreed on the MCP-contract addition; gate cleared at `/ship`). **CORE (both-agree + ADR):** adds a tool to the machine/MCP API contract (CLAUDE.md "Building together"). Purely additive: one new write MCP tool, no schema change, no body-format change (reuses the standard `![alt](url)` image markdown and R2 attachment machinery verbatim).
**Context:** the MCP surface let an AI write an item's `bodyMarkdown` but gave it **no way to add an image or file**. The whole upload path is browser-only: `POST /api/attachments` reserves a metadata row + returns a **presigned R2 PUT URL**, then the browser PUTs the bytes and drops the returned public CDN URL into the body as `![alt](url)` (`ItemEditor.uploadImage`). An MCP client (Claude) can't perform an arbitrary signed PUT, and even if it could, it has no way to obtain the presigned URL — so an AI could reference an image only if it somehow already had a public URL, and could never attach a file at all. Brandon asked for the AI to be able to add images (and files) into a note.
**Decision:** add one MCP tool, `attach_file(itemId, {sourceUrl | dataBase64}, filename?, contentType?, alt?, embedInBody?=true)`, returning `{ id, itemId, filename, contentType, sizeBytes, publicUrl, embedded }`. The bytes arrive **server-side**, two ways: `sourceUrl` (an http/https URL Ledgr fetches — the natural path for an AI that has a link) or `dataBase64` (bare base64 or a `data:` URI — for generated/pasted content). The server writes the bytes with the storage provider's `putObject` (not presign), so no browser is in the loop. By default it then embeds a reference in the item's markdown body — `![alt](url)` for an image content type, `[filename](url)` for anything else — appended with a blank-line separator; `embedInBody:false` attaches without touching the body. `filename`/`contentType` are inferred from the response (`Content-Disposition`, URL path, `Content-Type`) or the `data:` URI when omitted.
Storage-side, `createAttachment`'s validation was refactored into a shared private `reserveAttachment` (owner-scoped live-item check, per-file cap, ~10GB quota, row insert), and a new `createAttachmentFromBytes` reuses it then `putObject`s — so the MCP path **cannot drift** from the in-app presign path on quota/cap/owner scoping (same discipline as every other MCP tool being a thin wrapper over the app libs). A `sourceUrl` fetch is guarded: http/https only, and capped at 50 MB buffered (the per-file/quota caps still apply on top). The pure glue — base64/`data:` decode, `Content-Disposition` parsing, image detection, embed-markdown building — lives as exported node-testable functions (the `image-markdown.ts` discipline) covered by `scripts/verify-mcp-attach.mts`.

**Addendum (2026-07-07, same session): the presigned-PUT path for LOCAL/LARGE files.** `attach_file`'s base64 door rides the bytes inside the tool call, which bloats the model's context and is impractical past a few MB, and it can't help a local file the AI can't read into base64. So two companion tools expose the browser presign handshake to a capable agent: **`create_upload_url(itemId, filename, contentType, sizeBytes)`** reserves the row via the existing `createAttachment` and returns `{ attachmentId, uploadUrl, publicUrl, storageKey, contentType, next }`; the agent PUTs the local bytes **straight to R2** at `uploadUrl` (Content-Type must match the signature), so bytes never pass through the tool call or the app server and size stops mattering. **`embed_attachment(itemId, publicUrl, alt?, kind?)`** then adds the reference to the body after a successful PUT (image-vs-file inferred from the URL extension unless `kind` forces it). Both `attach_file`'s auto-embed and `embed_attachment` share one `appendReferenceToBody` (safe blank-line append through the owner-scoped `updateItem`, never a blind body replace). This is the same handshake `POST /api/machine/attachments` already exposes over REST (the migration path); the two MCP tools make it usable from an agent that can perform an HTTP PUT (Claude Code via curl/fetch), not a chat client that can't PUT. Caveat recorded: a pure chat client that only *sees* a dragged-in image (no byte access, no PUT capability) still can't use either door — that's a client-capability limit, not a Ledgr gap.
**Why / alternatives:** *sourceUrl + base64 both, server-side write* chosen because an AI can't use a presigned URL — the value is Ledgr taking the bytes. **sourceUrl is the workhorse** (an AI usually has a link, not raw bytes); base64 covers small generated/pasted content. Rejected: *exposing the presigned-URL flow over MCP* (the AI can't PUT, so it's useless to it); *a base64-only tool* (forces the model to inline megabytes it rarely has, and it can't base64 an image it merely "sees"); *not embedding in the body* (then every call needs a follow-up `update_item` to make the file visible — `embedInBody:true` makes "add this diagram to the note" one call, with an opt-out). SSRF exposure is bounded by this being a single-user, token-gated surface acting only on the owner's own data, plus the scheme + size guards; a full allow-list was judged overkill for one authenticated owner.
**Affects:** new — `attach_file`, `create_upload_url`, `embed_attachment` in `src/lib/mcp/tools/attachments.ts`, registered in `src/lib/mcp/tools/index.ts`; `createAttachmentFromBytes` + `reserveAttachment` refactor in `src/lib/attachments.ts`; a mention in the MCP `INSTRUCTIONS` (`src/lib/mcp/server.ts`); `scripts/verify-mcp-attach.mts`. No migration, no client change.
**Verification:** `npx tsx scripts/verify-mcp-attach.mts` green (base64 + `data:` decode, disposition parsing incl. RFC 5987, image detection, image-vs-file embed markdown, bracket escaping); `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on the changed files. Live MCP round-trip (attach a real image by URL, confirm the R2 object + the body embed renders) pending after Tyler sign-off + deploy — needs R2 configured.
## ADR-151: Timezone is a per-owner setting resolved at request time (replacing the build-time env constant)
**Date:** 2026-07-07
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-07). **Non-core / solo** — additive to the existing `users.settings` jsonb blob (no schema migration, same posture as every other setting) and it doesn't touch the frozen data model, body format, module boundary, provider interfaces, or MCP contract. Fulfills the "becomes a per-user setting" note that `today.ts` / `.env.example` had carried since ADR-008.
**Context:** Brandon reported every time in the app was an hour off. Root cause: the app's timezone was a build-time constant, `APP_TIMEZONE = process.env.LEDGR_TIMEZONE || "America/New_York"`, imported into ~15 files (many as module-level `Intl.DateTimeFormat` constants). His instance ran on the `America/New_York` default while he lives in Central, so every meeting/timestamp rendered an hour ahead (a 14:00Z meeting shows 10 AM Eastern vs 9 AM Central). The value wasn't editable from the UI (no setting existed) and — being server-side — his travel to Eastern was a red herring; nothing about it re-tuned the display.
**Decision:**
1. **`settings.timezone: string \| null`** on the existing `users.settings` blob (`null` = follow the server default). Validated in `parseSettings` via `isValidTimezone` (asks `Intl` to build a formatter; a `RangeError` rejects a bad string). Additive, no migration.
2. **`today.ts` becomes the resolver.** `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` = the env fallback (`LEDGR_TIMEZONE` else `America/New_York`); `APP_TIMEZONE` kept as an alias so nothing regresses. `getAppTimezone(ownerId)` (React `cache()`-memoized) resolves setting → env → default and is used by server components/routes/crons. A process-cached `appTimezoneSync()` (primed each request by the root layout via `primeAppTimezone`) backs the sync, owner-less helpers (`appTodayYmd`, a couple of SQL-filter builders) — correct because the instance is single-owner, so the cached value is always this one owner's zone; it only lags in the cold-start window before the first resolve (falls back to the env default, self-healing).
3. **Threaded the resolved zone through every display + day-boundary site.** Server components resolve `getAppTimezone` (or derive from an already-loaded `settings`) and build their `Intl` formatters per-request (memoized by zone); pure helpers (`event-format`, `item-tokens`, `templates`, `export`, `search`) take a `tz` param. The one client-reachable renderer, `ViewRenderer`, gets a `tz` prop (defaulting to `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE`), and the deep client dashboard-widget path reads it from a new global `TimezoneProvider` context (provided once in the root layout). Calendar-day fields (due/scheduled/note_date, UTC-midnight per ADR-008/110) stay formatted in UTC — unchanged.
4. **UI:** a Timezone control in User Settings — a full IANA `<select>` (`Intl.supportedValuesOf`, ~418 zones) with an "Automatic (server default)" option and a "Use this device's timezone" button; changing it `router.refresh()`es so server-rendered times update immediately.
**Why / alternatives:** (a) a pure module-global runtime value read synchronously everywhere (rejected for the *display* path — client components can't read server module state, and RSC renders layout/page concurrently so a layout-seeded global isn't reliably fresh within the first request; kept only as the `appTimezoneSync` best-effort for owner-less sync helpers where a near-midnight cold-start edge is acceptable); (b) full prop-drilling into the client widget tree (rejected — 4–5 hops through `RglInner`/`WidgetFrame`; a context is idiomatic and matches the existing providers); (c) leaving it an env var and just correcting the default to Central (rejected — Brandon asked for it to be user-configurable, and a redeploy-to-change knob isn't that). The env fallback is retained so a not-yet-threaded or owner-less path degrades to the old behavior, never to UTC.
**Known follow-up (non-core):** the meeting-time *input* (`FieldStrip` `datetime-local`) still interprets a typed wall-clock in the *browser's* zone, not the setting, so entering times on a device whose zone differs from the setting can store a shifted instant. Consistent when device zone == setting (the normal case); flagged for a later pass.
**Verification:** `next build` compiles clean (all routes, no type/lint errors); the client `TimezoneProvider`→`today.ts` import tree-shakes (no server code in the client bundle, same pattern `ViewRenderer` already used); confirmed the fix directly — a 14:00Z instant renders 10 AM under `America/New_York` and 9 AM under `America/Chicago`, `isValidTimezone` accepts `America/Chicago` and rejects `Bogus/Nowhere`. Device-verify the Settings picker + `router.refresh` live on merge.
**Affects:** src/lib/settings.ts (field + `isValidTimezone`), src/lib/today.ts (`DEFAULT_TIMEZONE`/`getAppTimezone`/`appTimezoneSync`/`primeAppTimezone`), src/components/providers/TimezoneProvider.tsx (new), src/app/layout.tsx (resolve + prime + provide), src/components/settings/SettingsForm.tsx + src/app/settings/page.tsx (the control), src/components/views/ViewRenderer.tsx (`tz` prop), and the threaded surfaces: src/app/page.tsx, /list/[type], /tasks, /planner, /views/[id], /changelog, /notes, /links, /api/search, src/lib/{event-format,calendar/feed,views,recurrence-service,export/engine,templates,item-tokens-service,push/notify}.ts, src/components/{lists/ViewLensBody,dashboards/WidgetBody,events/EventTimeline,calendar/CalendarFeed,canvas/widgets/MeetingsWidget,meetings/MeetingPrep}.tsx.

## ADR-152: Service worker v7 — restore the missing `return` in the fetch handler's navigate branch (fixes double `respondWith`)
**Date:** 2026-07-09
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-07-09). **Near-core (the SW/PWA layer) but a pure correctness bug fix, not a design change** — no change to the caching model, the pinned-cache seam, push, or any provider interface, so it deploys under ordinary production care rather than a fresh both-agree gate. Flagged to Tyler in COLLAB.md.
**Context:** Opening or reloading a note by direct URL (and notification taps) intermittently failed in prod with `The FetchEvent for "…/items/<id>" resulted in a network error response` and `sw.js:147 Uncaught InvalidStateError: Failed to execute 'respondWith' on 'FetchEvent': respondWith() was already called`. It surfaced against freshly imported notes (NSX → Ledgr migration) but the note bodies are schema-valid and the failure reproduces app-wide — it is not note data. The deployed worker was `VERSION = "v6"` (confirmed by fetching the live `/sw.js`).
**Decision:** v6's `fetch` handler has four intended-mutually-exclusive branches — cross-origin (R2), `/_next/static/`, navigations, and a catch-all — each doing `event.respondWith(...)` then `return`. The **navigate** branch was missing its `return`, so a navigation request called `respondWith()`, fell through, and hit the catch-all's `respondWith()` a second time on the same event → `InvalidStateError`, aborting the navigation into a network-error response. It only fires for `request.mode === "navigate"` (hard open / reload / notification tap), which is why soft in-app navigation was unaffected and it looked note-specific. v7 adds the one missing `return` after the navigate branch so the four branches are exclusive again. Bumping `VERSION` `v6`→`v7` also drops stale shell caches and reclaims clients on `activate`, so installed PWAs pick up the fixed worker on next load.
**Why / alternatives:** a hard reload / SW unregister only masks it until v6 re-registers (the registration is client-side), so it is not durable — the fix has to ship. A plain `return` (vs. reworking the branches into `if/else if`) matches the other three branches and the file's existing shape, keeping the diff to one line + the version bump. No behavior change beyond restoring branch exclusivity; the caching model (ADR-016) is untouched.
**Verification:** confirmed the deployed prod `/sw.js` served `VERSION = "v6"` with no `return` after the navigate branch and the catch-all `respondWith(` at the reported `sw.js:147`; the v7 edit restores the `return` so every branch ends in `respondWith()` + `return`. Reproduces only on navigation-mode requests. Post-deploy, confirm a hard-open of an item URL resolves (no `InvalidStateError` in console) and `/sw.js` reports `v7`.
**Affects:** public/sw.js.

## ADR-153: Live time tokens `{{now.*}}` + the `{{` picker on the title (extends ADR-139)
**Date:** 2026-07-10
**Status:** accepted. **Non-core / solo** — an additive vocabulary extension to the live item-token layer, in the spirit of the already-shipped LT2 (the `{{` insert menu) and TPL6 tokens. It builds on the **core** ADR-139 (live `{{item.*}}`/`{{parent.*}}` tokens), which is accepted but whose Tyler-ack is still pending per COLLAB.md; this addition touches no frozen surface (data model, body `{format,text}` contract, module boundary, provider interfaces, MCP contract), only the render-time resolver's recognized token set and one editor affordance, so it moves solo.
**Context:** Two gaps in the live-token feature. (1) The render-time resolver (`item-tokens.ts`) had no "current date" token — an author who wanted "today, always current" had nothing, because the only `{{today}}` in the system is the template **apply-time** variable (`template-vars.ts`) that BAKES ONCE when a template is applied, not a value that stays live. Brandon's call: keep the baking `{{today}}` exactly as-is and add a **distinctly-named live variant** so the two never collide. (2) The `{{` autocomplete popup existed only in the TipTap body editor, not in the item **title** (a plain `<textarea>`), even though titles resolve live tokens at render.
**Decision:**
1. **Grammar — a `{{now.*}}` family, live.** `{{now}}` and `{{now.today}}` = the current date; `{{now.tomorrow}}`, `{{now.yesterday}}`, `{{now.nextweek}}` (= today+7d); weekday words `{{now.sunday}}`…`{{now.saturday}}` (the coming weekday, incl. today) and `{{now.next<weekday>}}` (next week's). Each accepts the same `±Nd/w/m/y` offsets and `:iso/long/short/us/day` format suffixes as the existing item date tokens (e.g. `{{now.today+7d:long}}` → "July 17, 2026"; default → "Jun 20, 2026"). Weekday words defer to the shared `parseNaturalDate` (identical semantics to the apply-time weekday vars). All of it resolves against `ctx.todayYmd` (the owner's timezone-aware "today", ADR-151) — **never `Date.now()`** — so it re-resolves every render and never shifts across a timezone.
2. **Keep BOTH variants (the crux).** Apply-time `{{today}}`/`{{tomorrow}}`/… (`template-vars.ts`) are left untouched and still **bake** at template apply; live `{{now.*}}` (`item-tokens.ts`) **re-resolves** at every render. They don't collide at runtime because they act at different stages: a template's `{{today}}` is baked to concrete text at apply, so the live resolver never sees a token; a hand-typed `{{now.today}}` stays a token and resolves live. The live resolver's recognition predicates (`isLiveTokenExpr`/`hasItemTokens`/`scanItemTokens`, unified behind one `isLiveBase`) deliberately do **not** claim the bare `{{today}}` vocabulary, so apply-time baking is fully preserved (regression-tested).
3. **`{{` picker on plain text fields.** A new dependency-free hook `useTokenAutocomplete` (`src/components/markdown-editor/useTokenAutocomplete.tsx`) brings the same menu to any `<textarea>`/`<input>`: it detects the `{{query` trigger before the caret, filters the **shared** catalog (`item-token-catalog.ts` — no duplicated token list), supports arrow/enter/tab/escape, inserts the closed `{{token}}` and places the caret after it, and reuses the existing `.ledgr-token-*` popup CSS. IME-safe (pauses during composition) and Escape-dismiss-aware. Wired onto the item title in `ItemEditor`, ahead of the title's Enter-to-focus-body handler. New catalog rows (a "Now" group) surface the live tokens in both the body and title menus.
**Scope note — templates:** templates are authored in the normal item canvas (the hidden prototype opens at `/items/:id`; `NewTemplateForm` only collects name+type), so the title fix + the pre-existing body popup cover template editing. There is no separate template-string input to wire.
**Why / alternatives:** (a) repurposing the apply-time `{{today}}` to be live (rejected — it would break template baking, which Brandon wants kept); (b) a bare `{{today.live}}`-style suffix on the existing word (rejected — muddier than a clean `now.` namespace); (c) a full mirror-div caret-tracked popup position (rejected for now — the title is a short growing textarea, so anchoring the menu at the field's bottom-left is robust and dependency-light; the hook can gain caret coords later without changing its API).
**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on the changed files; `scripts/verify-item-tokens.mts` = 105 passed, 0 failed, including new cases proving `{{now.*}}` resolves to the current date, offsets/formats work, weekday words land on the right weekday on/after today, the token re-resolves when "today" moves, and apply-time `{{today}}`/`{{today+7d}}` still pass through the live resolver untouched. The title picker's in-browser behavior (menu placement, IME, Enter routing) wants a human eyeball on merge.
**Affects:** src/lib/item-tokens.ts (the `{{now.*}}` resolver + unified `isLiveBase` recognition), src/lib/editor/item-token-catalog.ts ("Now" group), src/components/markdown-editor/useTokenAutocomplete.tsx (new), src/components/markdown-editor/ItemEditor.tsx (title wiring), scripts/verify-item-tokens.mts (cases).

## ADR-154: The `{{` picker distinguishes "bakes on apply" from "live"; Preview is a first-class body mode (slice 7)
**Date:** 2026-07-10
**Status:** accepted. **Non-core / solo** — a picker-UX + editor-affordance change over the same additive token layer as ADR-153; touches no frozen surface (data model, body `{format,text}` contract, module boundary, provider interfaces, MCP contract). The resolvers themselves are unchanged.
**Context:** After ADR-153 the `{{` picker offered ONLY the live catalog (`{{item.*}}`/`{{parent.*}}`/`{{now.*}}`). So an author typing `{{today}}` in a template title was offered just the live `{{now.today}}`, which does **not** bake — the reported confusion between the two same-syntax families. Brandon chose the scoped fix: keep the editor showing raw tokens (no resolved-value chips), just make the picker teach the difference and offer the baking tokens, and make Preview (which already resolves live tokens) easy to reach.
**Decision:**
1. **Two labeled families in one shared catalog.** `TokenOption` gains an optional `kind: "live" | "bake"` (default live). A new **"Bakes on apply"** group adds the apply-time template vars — `{{today}}`, `{{tomorrow}}`, `{{yesterday}}`, `{{today+7d}}` (offset), `{{sunday}}` (this coming weekday) and `{{nextSunday}}` (next week's) — each hinted "…baked once", sitting adjacent to the live "Now" group (whose labels keep their "(live)" suffix). Because both plain-text (`useTokenAutocomplete`) and TipTap (`token-suggestion`) pickers render group headers straight off the shared catalog, both surfaces gain the group with no per-picker code. Inserting a bake option inserts the literal `{{today}}` (not `{{now.today}}`).
2. **Always-show, not template-gated.** The bake group shows in every editor, not only when editing a template's prototype. Gating to templates was considered and declined: the prototype is a normal item and template-awareness isn't reachable at the picker without threading a flag through the whole canvas chain and reconfiguring the statically-registered TipTap extension — cost out of proportion to the benefit. The per-row "baked once when a template is applied" hint carries the caveat instead (a bake token is simply inert literal text in a non-template note).
3. **Preview is a third body mode on normal notes.** `BodyEditor`'s normal-note mode row gains a Preview (eye) button beside Rich/Source, titled "Preview — tokens resolve here". Preview already existed (and resolves live tokens via `/api/render-markdown` with `itemId`) but was reachable only as the large-note default; now any note can flip to it to see resolved values. The large-note reading/source banner and the S5 collapse toggle are untouched.
**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on changed files; `scripts/verify-item-tokens.mts` = 111 passed, 0 failed (new cases: bake tokens are in the catalog, are NOT live tokens, ARE recognized apply-time vars, and a `{{today}}` query surfaces both a bake and a live option); `scripts/verify-template-vars.mts` still 63/0 (baking preserved). The picker's grouped popup and the Preview button want a human eyeball in-browser on merge.
**Affects:** src/lib/editor/item-token-catalog.ts (`kind` + "Bakes on apply" group), src/components/markdown-editor/BodyEditor.tsx (Preview mode button), scripts/verify-item-tokens.mts (cases).

## ADR-156: Search ranking weights recency with a power-law multiplier (strong for @/quick, mild for full search)
**Date:** 2026-07-10
**Status:** accepted (solo build). **Borderline-core — flag for Tyler:** this reweights the ORDER BY of the FTS query but keeps *the FTS approach itself* unchanged (still `websearch_to_tsquery` + the generated tsvector + `ts_rank`); it's ranking/UX tuning, not a change to the search mechanism, the schema, or any frozen contract. If we read "the FTS approach" (core list) to include result ordering, this wants Tyler's nod before merge; otherwise it's solo. No new columns, no new deps, no migration.
**Context:** Recency was only a *final tiebreak* in every search path (`ts_rank desc, updated_at desc` in `searchItemsQuery`; `…similarity desc, updated_at desc` in `listItemsQuery`). Relevance scores effectively never tie, so recency never fired — the reported "recency isn't weighted" feeling. Brandon: for the @ typeahead and quick search he's usually reaching for something worked on recently; for a deliberate full search, less so. He wanted a smooth curve (no hard cutoff) that's steep near term but keeps a fat tail (a 1-year-old item still ranks above a 2-year-old one).
**Decision:**
1. **Recency as a multiplier on relevance, not a sort key.** New `src/lib/recency.ts` exposes `recencyMultiplier(w)` → the SQL factor `1 + W / (1 + age_days / H)`, `age_days = days since GREATEST(created_at, updated_at)`. The FTS order becomes `ts_rank × multiplier desc` and the @ order becomes `similarity × multiplier desc`, each with `updated_at desc` kept as the final tiebreak. Modulating (× similarity) rather than replacing it means a short exact-ish match ("Roger Knowlton", high similarity) keeps its lead over a long freshly-typed task ("Roger Knowlton's email …", low similarity) — recency only reorders *close* matches.
2. **Power-law, not exponential — on purpose.** A power-law keeps a fat tail (1yr ≈ 1.074×, 2yr ≈ 1.038× at strong); an exponential would flatten both to ~1.0 past a few H, losing the ordering Brandon asked for.
3. **Two presets, per surface.** `RECENCY_STRONG = {w:2, h:14}` for the @ typeahead (`listItemsQuery`, always) and quick search (command palette passes `?recency=strong`); `RECENCY_MILD = {w:0.5, h:30}` as the `/api/search` default (the full search page). Signal is created-or-updated, whichever is newer; **no `lastOpenedAt`** — an open-tracking column was considered and deferred (it'd be a core schema change + a write per open). Relation-recency ("recently linked to") likewise considered and dropped (per-row subquery for a small effect); both noted as upgrade paths in `recency.ts`.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-recency.mts` = 20/0 (bounded, monotonic, `1wk ≫ 6mo`, `1yr > 2yr` fat tail, strong > mild everywhere, and the @ guarantee: short-exact beats long-fresh while recency still breaks close ties). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on changed files. Live in-browser eyeball on real data wanted before ship (the constants are tuned by feel).
**Affects:** src/lib/recency.ts (new), src/lib/search.ts (FTS order + `recency` opt), src/lib/items.ts (@/list order), src/app/api/search/route.ts (`?recency=strong`), src/components/search/CommandPalette.tsx (passes the flag), scripts/verify-recency.mts (new).

## ADR-157: Bespoke-first item canvases — a shared longform document canvas for prose types (note, link, journal, …)
**Date:** 2026-07-10
**Status:** accepted (solo build). **Not a core-model change:** everything here rides the *existing* canvas seam (ADR-041) — a new `canvasId` + component in `module-wiring.tsx`, a new attachable *capability* in the ADR-042 catalog, and a new faint chrome element — none of which changes how a type declares a canvas, the grid-layout schema, or any frozen contract, so it's module-internal / UI (move-fast-solo). Flagged for Tyler in COLLAB because it changes the default rendering of shared core types (`note`, `link`) his instance also runs.
**Context:** A design critique of the item canvas (impeccable, snapshot in `.impeccable/critique/`) asked why a task gets a hand-crafted two-pane rail (ADR-108) while every other type falls to the default `MarkdownCanvas` — a ~14-section vertical stack. Brandon chose **bespoke-first** (Principle 6) over teaching the grid customizer (ADR-069) to express a rail (rejected as over-engineering). A first pass built a two-pane note rail, but Brandon's own iteration reframed it: a side rail steals width from prose, and *most* of the stacked-canvas types (note, link, journal, prayer, logos_note, email, transcript, media, teaching — ~2,500 items) are **longform** — they want a document shape, not per-type hand-built canvases.
**Decision:**
1. **One shared `LongformCanvas` (`canvasId: "longform"`), not N per-type canvases.** A document layout: the markdown body runs the full reading column; the item's metadata sits in one intentional **byline** under the title — a clickable URL chip (link), the date, tags/relation fields inline, custom scalars beneath — rendered through `ItemEditor`'s own `fields` slot so it aligns with title and body (the earlier standalone-wrapper version drifted / double-padded). System fields (type/created/updated) are **chrome, not content**: faint, right-aligned on the `ItemCanvas` breadcrumb row (all canvases; full-page — the modal-chrome copy is a follow-up).
2. **Rollout via the two existing mechanisms.** Core types point at it by `canvasId` (`note`, `link` — retiring the bespoke `LinkCanvas`, whose URL chip is now the byline chip). User prose types attach a new pickable **`longform` capability** (`canvasId: "longform"`), resolved via `typeDef.capability`. The capability's canvas **enables tabs itself**, so a type wanting both a document layout and tabs (journal, teaching) attaches only `longform` — the single-capability slot can't also hold `tabs`.
3. **Customizer stays the per-type override.** A saved `canvasLayout` (or `?arrange=1`) still delegates to the default canvas's draggable grid: `if (arrange || savedLayout) return <MarkdownCanvas {...} />`. (Precedence "bespoke wins unless re-customized" is achieved for now by clearing a stale pre-existing layout once; a durable marker is a noted follow-up.)
4. **FieldStrip gains a `flush` option** (drop its built-in column padding) so it composes inside the byline without double-indenting.
**Rollout state:** dev seeded (`types.capability = "longform"` on journal, prayer, logos_note, email, transcript, media, sermon; note/link by code). **Prod not touched** — attach "Longform document" per type in Build → Types, or run a one-shot seed, once shipped.
**Verification:** `verify-canvas-seam`, `verify-module-registry`, `verify-tasks-seam`, `verify-canvas-layout`, `verify-bespoke-capability` all pass (seam scripts updated: `note`/`link` → `longform`). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. In-browser (dev-auth): note, URL-bearing link, prayer, logos_note all render clean (200, panels firing). NOTE: worktree HMR is unreliable (Turbopack infers the main-repo root) — the dev server must be restarted to see edits.
**Affects:** src/components/canvas/LongformCanvas.tsx (new, was NoteCanvas), LinkCanvas.tsx (deleted), FieldStrip.tsx (`flush`), ItemCanvas.tsx (chrome timestamps), src/lib/module-wiring.tsx (`longform` wire), src/lib/modules.ts (note/link canvasId + `longform` capability), scripts/verify-canvas-seam.mts + verify-module-registry.mts. Follow-ups: modal-chrome timestamps; the "re-customized" precedence marker; **structured** bespoke types next — event (meeting panels) then person (relations-forward).

## ADR-158: Bespoke event/meeting canvas — a two-pane notes + sticky, collapsible meeting rail
**Date:** 2026-07-10
**Status:** accepted (solo build). **Not a core-model change:** rides the same canvas seam (ADR-041/157) — a new `canvasId: "event"` + component in `module-wiring.tsx` — plus a small reusable addition to the shared `CanvasSection` (a `defaultOpen` collapsible mode). No change to how a type declares a canvas, the body contract, the grid schema, or any frozen contract. Module-internal / UI (move-fast-solo); flagged for Tyler in COLLAB since it changes the default rendering of the shared core `event` type.
**Context:** The next bespoke type after the longform prose family (ADR-157). The event is the heaviest, densest type (~1,400 items) and neither the longform byline nor the task rail fits: a meeting carries big interactive sub-panels (the ADR-144 People card, the ADR-094 rule-pulled Open-tasks panel with presets/lens/multi-select, Transcripts, Notes). Shaped with Brandon over three mockups (two-pane vs People-band-stack vs before/during/after tabs). He picked two-pane but flagged the real risk — long meeting notes lose vertical room to a side rail — and resolved it: make the rail **float** (sticky + independently scrolling) so its context (People, and Open tasks doubling as an agenda) stays in view while scrolling a long note, and make it **collapsible** so it can be dismissed to give notes full width.
**Decision:**
1. **`EventCanvas` (`canvasId: "event"`), a two-pane shape.** Left: title + a compact **meeting byline** (the `meetingAt` "When" field via `FieldStrip`, the date Brandon wanted hoisted up) + the notes/agenda body, with `[ ]` lines promotable to tasks (block anchors, ADR-090). Right: the whole `MeetingPrep` panel (People card → Open tasks → Catch-up → Recent meetings) rendered `bare`, in a **sticky, independently-scrolling** `<aside>` (`lg:sticky lg:top-4 lg:self-start lg:max-h-[calc(100vh-1.5rem)] lg:overflow-y-auto`, hairline `border-l`). Rail sections get hairline dividers via a child selector so `bare` sections still read as a list.
2. **The boundary is a draggable resizer with a sticky collapse chevron** (`EventTwoPane` client wrapper). Brandon's iteration: the first cut put a "Hide panel" text button above the grid, which scrolled out of view and didn't help truncation. Replaced with (a) **drag-to-resize** — the pane boundary is a `role="separator"` you drag to set the rail width (clamped 280–620px), which gives long task titles and the rule label room; and (b) a **sticky chevron ON the boundary** (like the nav's collapse), so it stays reachable while scrolling and collapses the rail (→ the whole right-edge gutter becomes a set-off, full-height click target — surface-1 + hairline, brightening to surface-2 on hover, with a sticky "‹" chevron — a big, obvious reopen affordance, not a lone chevron; Brandon). Both width and open/closed persist per browser in `localStorage`; the drag persists a closure-local `latest` (not the render-lagged ref) so the saved width is exact. Collapsing gives the notes full width; on mobile the rail always stacks (resize/collapse are desktop affordances).
3. **Rarely-opened panels collapse by default** (Brandon: transcript access is rare). Transcripts and Notes render full-width below the two-pane, **collapsed even when non-empty**, via a new `CanvasSection defaultOpen` mode (renders the section as a native `<details>`; the header becomes the `<summary>` with a rotating caret; honors `prefers-reduced-motion`). Properties (scalar + non-person relations — person relations stay on the People card, ADR-144), Linked-here, Discover, and the utilities footer follow, full-width.
4. **Reorder = the existing customizer, no new system.** Brandon chose the whole-page grid customizer as the rail-reorder escape hatch over a second rail-scoped drag-reorder (over-engineering). So `if (arrange || savedLayout) return <MarkdownCanvas {...} />` stays — bespoke by default, grid on `?arrange=1` — exactly like Task/Longform.
**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. In-browser (dev-auth, worktree): a real meeting (Strategic Half-Day) renders 200, hydrated — two-pane confirmed, byline "When" field, rail People card + Open tasks (43, lens/presets/multi-select) + Recent meetings, rail **scrolls independently** while the notes column stays put, Hide/Show toggle works, Transcripts/Notes collapsed and expand on click. (Worktree HMR unreliable — restart the dev server to see edits.)
6. **The two-pane splits on CONTAINER width, so the bespoke layout works in the modal too.** First cut used viewport `lg:` breakpoints, which ignore the `@modal` peek's actual (narrower) width — so the modal crammed (main ~400px, long titles colliding with the collapse chevron) and a stop-gap that fell the modal back to `MarkdownCanvas` was wrong: Brandon views items in the modal *most of the time*, and wants the bespoke rail-forward layout (less MD-canvas emphasis) there. Fixed with **container queries** (`@container` + `@min-[640px]:`, Tailwind v4): `CanvasTwoPane` splits into two columns when its own container is ≥640px and stacks (main, then rail under a hairline) when narrower — so a roomy modal peek shows the dual column, a tight modal or phone sheet stacks, and the full page always splits. The inner drag-resize is disabled in the modal (`resizable={variant === "page"}` on event; task is always collapse-only) so it never clashes with the modal peek's own outer resize handle. (Class literals are written out in full — Tailwind's scanner can't see interpolated variants.)
5. **Generalized to a shared `CanvasTwoPane`, adopted by tasks (collapse-only).** The two-pane wrapper is type-agnostic (only `main`/`rail` nodes), so it was renamed `EventTwoPane` → `CanvasTwoPane` with a `storageKey` (each type remembers its own width + collapsed state) and a `resizable` flag. TaskCanvas swapped its static `grid … 340px` + `<aside>` for `<CanvasTwoPane storageKey="task" resizable={false} defaultWidth={340}>` — tasks get the collapsible gutter but **not** drag-resize (Brandon's call: the compact task rail rarely needs widening; `task-rail-width` is never persisted). Event stays `resizable`. The collapsed gutter is the whole set-off, full-height strip (surface-1 → surface-2 on hover), a big reopen target rather than a lone chevron.
**Affects:** src/components/canvas/EventCanvas.tsx (new), CanvasTwoPane.tsx (new — shared resizable/collapsible two-pane; used by event + task), TaskCanvas.tsx (adopts CanvasTwoPane, collapse-only), CanvasSection.tsx (`defaultOpen`), src/components/meetings/MeetingPrep.tsx (rule chip truncates + hover-title), MeetingNotes.tsx + MeetingTranscripts.tsx (`collapsed`), src/lib/module-wiring.tsx (`event` wire), src/lib/modules.ts (event canvasId), src/app/globals.css (collapsible summary CSS), scripts/verify-canvas-seam.mts + verify-module-registry.mts (event → own canvas). MarkdownCanvas keeps its event branches as the grid/arrange fallback. Deferred: **per-row task-title wrap** in the rail (an *option* Brandon floated) — leaned on drag-resize instead since wrapping touches the shared `ViewRenderer`/list rows everywhere; revisit if resize proves insufficient. Follow-ups (carried from ADR-157): modal-chrome timestamps; the durable "re-customized" precedence marker; then **person** (relations-forward) next. Prod: no data change — the canvas resolves by type key, live on deploy.

## ADR-159: Editor loads the body via `setContent`, not the constructor `content` path (fixes the standalone-inline-image `contentMatchAt` crash)
**Date:** 2026-07-10
**Status:** accepted
**Context:** Opening certain notes threw `Called contentMatchAt on a node with invalid content` and the editor never mounted — the item opens in an intercepting-route modal (`@modal/(.)items/[id]`), so the failed mount drops the user back on the list they clicked from ("opens, then falls back to the list"). It correlated with images and surfaced en masse on the NSX note import (~262 of the 265 imported image-notes were at risk; large notes escaped only because they open in read-only reading mode above `LARGE_BODY_THRESHOLD`). Root cause: `LedgrImage` is `inline: true`, and a **standalone image in its own block** (an image alone on a line, not the sole node — extremely common in screen-clip/web-clip notes) parses to a **bare `image` child of the doc**, which is schema-invalid (an inline node must live in a textblock). `MarkdownEditor` passed `content: initialMarkdown` + `contentType: "markdown"` to `useEditor`, so this parse happened **in the editor constructor, before every extension's markdown hooks are wired**, and produced the invalid doc. The editor never runs `doc.check()` on load, so the first plugin `appendTransaction` (StarterKit's `TrailingNode`) is the first thing to touch it and throws — killing the mount. Not bad data: the stored bodies are the repaired/validated import bodies, and `doc.check()` (what the import's `prep-import-bodies.mts` validated against) does **not** run plugin `appendTransactions`, so it structurally could not catch this.
**Decision:** Construct the editor **empty** (`content: ""`) and load the body in the existing post-mount effect via `editor.commands.setContent(initialMarkdown, { contentType: "markdown", emitUpdate: false })` (the same effect that already handled "reload from saved"). `setContent` on the ready editor parses markdown correctly — it wraps a standalone inline image in a paragraph — so the doc is valid and no `appendTransaction` ever sees invalid content. An empty initial doc is valid, so the mount re-serialize can't crash before the load runs. The effect then sets `lastEmitted` to the canonical serialization so the load isn't mistaken for a user edit (the "viewing marks edited" guard is preserved). Content preserved and still rich (image renders); the body on disk is untouched — each load repairs in memory.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected changing `LedgrImage` to a block node / `group: "inline block"` — that's a canonical-schema change (both-agree + ADR, and risks the view/round-trip). Rejected a defensive `enableContentCheck` + post-mount repair — a transaction (the mount re-serialize) fires and crashes *before* a post-mount effect can run, and `onContentError` fires mid-construction when `editor.state` doesn't yet exist, so it can't `setContent` there. Rejected re-patching the ~255 stored bodies — the defect is in the editor load path, not the data, so an editor fix needs no prod data write and also covers the remaining ~5,500 unimported notes and any future body with a standalone image. This is a load-path fix only: **no schema, no canonical-body-format, no MCP/API-contract change**, hence non-core.
**Verification:** Reproduced the exact crash live in prod (`All in One Modules`, `City Lab - session 3`) — console `contentMatchAt … at appendTransaction`. Headless harness with the live extension set + load path: the constructor path crashes, the `setContent` path yields a valid doc with the image wrapped in a paragraph; a sweep over **all 1,364 imported notes = 188 crashed before the fix, 0 after** (the 8 "image not rendered" are code-fenced notes, where the image is intentional literal text). `eslint` + `tsc --noEmit` clean. Post-deploy, confirm one image note (e.g. `City Lab - session 3`) opens with its image and a plain note still edits/saves.
**Affects:** src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.tsx (empty `content`, the loader effect + baseline). Verify script: scripts/verify-editor-load.mts.

## ADR-160: Browser-minted API tokens (MCP + web clipper), per-purpose signing secrets
**Date:** 2026-07-11
**Status:** accepted (CORE — machine/MCP auth contract; Tyler agreed 2026-07-11)
**Context:** Getting an API token meant the `scripts/make-token.mjs` CLI + pasting a hash into `LEDGR_API_TOKENS` + a redeploy (ADR-004's "the secret in env IS the credential, no DB row"). Brandon wanted to mint a token from the web app the way most apps do — one for the durable MCP connection, one for the "Save from the web" clipper — and wanted the two independently revocable so rotating the clipper never kills MCP.
**Decision:** Mint tokens in-browser by reusing the OAuth shim's stateless signed-blob primitive (ADR-117), **no DB table, no redeploy to mint.** A minted token is an `access`-kind signed token (same format as the OAuth flow's), with two deliberately **separate signing secrets** so each purpose has its own kill switch:
1. **MCP token** — scope `mcp`, signed with the existing `LEDGR_OAUTH_SECRET`, 10-year TTL. The existing `verifyAccessToken` on `/api/mcp` accepts it **with no route change**. Durable; paste into Claude Code/Desktop config (no refresh path, hence the long TTL).
2. **Clipper token** — scope `api`, signed with a **new** `LEDGR_CLIPPER_SECRET`. Verified by a new `verifyClipperToken`; the four `api`-scope routes now call a combined `verifyApiToken` = static `LEDGR_API_TOKENS` token **or** minted clipper token, so both credential paths coexist (the same additive pattern `/api/mcp` already uses).
- **Minting is additive:** a new token never invalidates an old one (same secret signs both). The only revocation is rotating a purpose's secret (env change + redeploy), which kills every token of that purpose at once. The UI states this at each mint and warns on each rotate: rotating `LEDGR_OAUTH_SECRET` signs out the phone/web connector *and* every minted MCP token; rotating `LEDGR_CLIPPER_SECRET` kills every clipper token but leaves MCP untouched.
- The AI & MCP page gets a Generate-MCP-token button (CLI kept as a fallback note); User Settings → Save from the web gets a Generate-clipper-token button that loads straight into the bookmarklet (paste still works for CLI/static tokens). Both buttons are owner-gated server actions that refuse to mint until the purpose's secret is set.
**Why / alternatives:** Chose stateless-signed (the ADR-004/117 model) over a `api_tokens` DB table. A table would give per-token listing + individual revocation ("how web apps work" in full), but it's a `schema.md` change, makes the pure/sync `verifyMachineToken` async across ~20 routes, and Brandon explicitly picked mint-only. The cost accepted: no list of active tokens, and revocation is coarse (rotate-the-secret kills all of that purpose). The **per-purpose secret split** is what buys back the one separation Brandon actually needed (clipper rotatable without touching MCP). Rejected a third secret for MCP-vs-phone separation as unneeded (MCP is "durable / rarely revoked"). Rejected a narrower `capture` scope for the clipper token (single-user; the owner's own `api` token is fine).
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-minted-tokens.mts` (roundtrip; wrong-secret rejection = the per-purpose kill switch holds; scope enforcement; tamper + expiry rejection). `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` clean. In-browser: mint on the AI & MCP page and against `/api/mcp`; mint a clipper token and POST `/api/machine/capture`.
**Affects:** src/lib/auth/oauth.ts (key-parameterized sign/verify; `signMcpToken`/`signClipperToken`/`verifyClipperToken`/`verifyApiToken`/`clipperConfigured`), src/lib/auth/mint-actions.ts (new, owner-gated server actions), src/components/build/TokenMinter.tsx (new), src/app/build/claude/page.tsx (mint button + revoke warning + status), src/components/build/ClipperSetup.tsx + src/components/settings/WebClipper.tsx + src/app/settings/page.tsx (clipper minting), src/app/api/machine/{capture,items,relations,attachments}/route.ts (`verifyApiToken`), .env.example (`LEDGR_CLIPPER_SECRET`), runbook.md §3. New secret is additive — deploying without `LEDGR_CLIPPER_SECRET` set just disables the clipper Generate button; nothing existing breaks.

## ADR-161: Editor color palette retuned for the dark canvas — bright text colors, rgba highlight washes, underline inherits color
**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Status:** accepted (CORE — the color encoding is part of the canonical body-format contract; Tyler agreed 2026-07-16)
**Context:** The 9-color editor palette in `src/lib/colors.ts` started as BlockNote's COLORS_DEFAULT (Notion's), tuned for a white page. On Ledgr's dark canvas (`#191919`) that showed three ways: several text colors lacked contrast, there was no true green (`green` was `#4d6461`, a gray-teal), and the highlight backgrounds were ~95%-lightness pastels that all composited toward white — every highlight read the same. Separately, an underline over colored text painted in the default color, not the text's color.
**Decision:** Retune the one table (names unchanged — they're the stable contract):
- **Text colors** → bright, saturated hex readable on dark (Tailwind-400 family), including a true green `#4ade80` and a cherry red `#f23a4a` (Brandon approved by eye).
- **Highlights** → `rgba()` washes (~0.42 alpha) instead of near-white hex. An alpha wash reads as a distinct saturated color over `#191919` **and** degrades to a soft pastel over white, so one value works in both modes — a future light mode needs no highlight table (text colors can't do this trick; a light mode would need a second text table, deferred). Highlights already round-trip via the `hl-*` class, so the background value is free to change without breaking parse; the class-stripped fallback reverse-lookup now matches the full color value (hex **or** rgba, whitespace-normalized) rather than hex-only.
- **Underline** → bump the `textColor` mark's Tiptap `priority` to 120 so it renders **outside** underline/strike (rank 1, just inside link); those decoration elements then inherit the color span's `color` as `currentColor`.
- **Migration** → `scripts/backfill-editor-colors.mts` rewrites old inline values → new in stored `items.body.text` (dry-run + JSON backup first). Required because a text color round-trips via exact hex: an un-migrated old-hex span no longer maps to a palette name and gets stripped to plain text on the next rich edit (confirmed live in the scratch editor). `revisions` left as historical snapshots.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected a full user-facing color picker — it would force arbitrary-hex round-trip (a core body-format change) and persisted per-user palette config, heavy machinery for a single owner's one-time preference; changing the shared table + a backfill delivers the actual outcome. Kept the names/`hl-*` classes stable so exported documents and the parse side don't shift.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-tiptap-markdown.mts` (color round-trip, class + style decode), `verify-body-contract.mts`, `verify-body-modes.mts` all pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean; migration replacement logic self-checked (hex→hex, hex→rgba, case-insensitive, `hl-*` preserved, longer hex tokens untouched); mark-nesting confirmed headlessly via schema rank; live in `/scratch/editor`: cherry red `rgb(242,58,74)`, true green `rgb(74,222,128)`, and a colored+underlined word rendering `<span style="color:…"><u>…</u></span>` with the underline's `text-decoration-color` matching the text.
