**Affects:** src/lib/colors.ts (palette values + hex-or-rgba reverse lookup), src/components/markdown-editor/extensions.ts (`TextColor` `priority: 120`), scripts/backfill-editor-colors.mts (new). Prod bodies need the backfill run as a deliberate step (dry-run against `.env.production.local` first).

## ADR-162: Live editing context — a Notion-style AI note-editing loop (active_context row + get_active_context/edit_item_body MCP tools)
**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Status:** accepted (CORE — new `schema.md` table + machine/MCP contract; Tyler agreed 2026-07-16). Additive and off-by-default, so Tyler's instance is untouched until he opts in. (Renumbered from ADR-161 → ADR-162 on merge: origin/main took 161 for the editor-palette retune.)
**Context:** Brandon wanted Notion's live AI-editing feel inside Ledgr: an assistant that always has the open note as context ("help me sharpen this"), is highlight-aware ("rework this sentence"), acts on "go ahead and make that change," and stays in sync while he also edits directly with keyboard and mouse. The tracing found Ledgr already had most of the machinery — MCP `get_item`/`update_item`, the tiptap autosave with a cross-device 409 guard, and the ADR-134 refresh-on-focus version check — so the gap was small and specific: the assistant didn't know *which* note was open or what was selected, manual edits didn't reach the DB fast enough to critique, and the refocus check only offered a manual reload.
**Decision:** A four-part, opt-in feature behind `settings.liveContextEnabled` (default off, mirrors AI Memory's gating, ADR-137):
1. **`active_context` table** — one upserted row per owner (owner_id unique) holding the open item id, a fallback title, the current selection text, and staleness stamps. Ephemeral UI state, explicitly **not** user content (rule 2): out of `items`, never exported/searched/revisioned. Device-clobbering is intended (last-writer-wins) — Brandon called the context "in the moment." Written by the open canvas via `POST /api/active-context` (Clerk-authed); an `ActiveContextTracker` reports the item on mount and a debounced text selection, and clears on close.
2. **Two MCP tools** — `get_active_context` (resolves "this note"/"this sentence" to the open item, returning its **freshly re-read** body + selection) and `edit_item_body` (a unique-match find/replace, the safe surgical alternative to whole-body `update_item` when the owner is co-editing). Gated + surfaced by a connect-time instruction addendum, both like the memory tools.
3. **Flush-on-hide** — `ItemEditor` now flushes pending edits on `visibilitychange → hidden` (tab-switch to Claude), not just `pagehide`, so "what do you think of this draft?" reflects the latest keystrokes. Because that flush advances `knownVersion`, it also clears the `localSaveSinceSync` flag (new `clearLocalSave`) so a subsequent external edit (Claude over MCP) isn't misattributed as the owner's own and swallowed.
4. **Auto-swap-when-clean** — the ADR-134 refocus check now, on a genuine external change, silently `location.reload()`s when the editor is clean (new `hasPendingEdits` dirty-check registry) and only shows the "Updated elsewhere" banner when the owner has unsaved work to protect. This makes Claude's edits appear on tab-return with no click.
- **The prompt as a seeded item, not a loose skill file.** Brandon's "somewhere in the middle": the canonical tuned instructions live in the repo (`note-editing-prompt.ts`, kept in lockstep with the tools), and enabling the feature seeds them as an editable `type=prompt` item ("Note Editing Partner") — his existing "use my X prompt" muscle memory (memory 1c069e09). Editable like any item; a settings "Revert to default" re-writes it from the constant. Falls back to `type=note` where no `prompt` type exists (Tyler/fresh instances).
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected export→local-editor→sync-back (violates the one-way-export principle, rule 1), a bespoke Chrome extension (Claude-in-Chrome already exists), and editing in an external MD/Obsidian vault (forks the source of truth, drops properties/relations/revisions). Chose the Claude-app-as-sidebar + server-tracked active context because it needs no new runtime, fits the ~$0 target (rides the existing MCP + subscription, no API metering), and works from mobile. Chose a dedicated table over stashing context in `users.settings` (high-frequency selection writes would thrash the whole settings blob and race other writes). Chose a stateless "re-read every turn" tool over having the assistant remember the note (a remembered id goes stale the instant the owner switches notes). Chose surgical `edit_item_body` over whole-body `update_item` so live co-editing can't clobber concurrent manual edits.
**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit` clean on all new/changed files; `eslint` clean. Migration generated then hand-trimmed to a single-purpose `active_context` create (this repo hand-authors migrations; the drizzle meta snapshots are stale past 0040, so a raw `generate` re-emits 0041–0046 — dropped the polluted snapshot, kept the clean SQL + journal entry, matching 0046). **Not yet applied** (additive; `npm run db:migrate` before enabling) and **not yet browser-smoke-tested end-to-end** (needs the migration applied + a connected MCP client). Left to exercise: enable the setting, open a note, confirm the tracker row + `get_active_context` over MCP + an `edit_item_body` round-trip + auto-swap on return.
**Affects:** src/db/schema.ts (`active_context`) + drizzle/0047_ordinary_maverick.sql; src/lib/active-context.ts (new), src/lib/note-editing-prompt.ts (new); src/app/api/active-context/route.ts + prompt/route.ts (new); src/components/canvas/ActiveContextTracker.tsx (new) + ItemCanvas.tsx (mount, gated); src/components/markdown-editor/ItemEditor.tsx (flush-on-hide, clearLocalSave, dirty-check) + src/lib/save-status.ts (`clearLocalSave`/`registerDirtyCheck`/`hasPendingEdits`) + src/components/canvas/SaveStatusIndicator.tsx (auto-swap); src/lib/mcp/tools/context.ts (new) + tools/index.ts (register + gate) + server.ts (instruction addendum); src/lib/settings.ts (`liveContextEnabled`, `noteEditingPromptItemId`) + src/app/api/settings/route.ts (seed on enable) + src/components/settings/SettingsForm.tsx + NoteEditingPromptActions.tsx (new). All additive and off by default.

## ADR-163: Sort views and list-tab lenses by task priority (urgency added to the sort/lens field set)
**Date:** 2026-07-19
**Status:** accepted (touches the view-engine `SORT_FIELDS` / MCP `create_view` sort contract — additive only, no schema change; other types unaffected). Flag for Tyler as a heads-up, not a blocker: a new allowed enum value that defaults nowhere.
**Context:** Brandon filed a task ("Can't create lenses for the 'Task' view and can't sort by task priority") with a screenshot of the New View builder whose Sort-by dropdown offered only date fields + title, no priority. Root cause: `urgency` (the task priority P1–P6 column, ADR-096) was never a sortable field. The same gap hid it from the Build → Types "List tabs" lens editor, and the builder's Priority filter was still stale — it listed the retired 4-level `low/normal/high/critical` enum and saved `Number("high")` = `NaN`, so the urgency filter silently did nothing.
**Decision:** Make priority a first-class ordering everywhere urgency already appears (task/any):
1. **Engine** — add `"urgency"` to `views.ts` `SORT_FIELDS` + `SORT_COLUMNS`; it rides the generic `asc/desc nulls last` path, so ascending = P1 first with unset (≈P6) last. `parseSort` and MCP `create_view` accept it for free (the tool description now lists it).
2. **ViewBuilder** — `sortFieldsFor` offers "priority" for task/any; picking it defaults Direction to asc and relabels the two options "highest first (P1→P6)" / "lowest first". Also fixed the stale Priority *filter*: it now lists P1–P6 (numeric values), so the filter actually applies.
3. **Lenses** — add `"urgency"` to `list-lenses.ts` `LENS_FIELDS` (validation whitelist) and a "Priority" preset to `ListTabsEditor`, filtered to `typeKey === "task"` so notes/links/etc. never see a meaningless all-null sort. Not added to the generic `defaultLenses` strip — offered only where the type has it.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected exposing urgency as a generic lens field for all types (it's the task-only column; other types would sort by all-nulls). Rejected treating priority as a custom property sort (it's a built-in column, not in any `propertySchema`). Kept it additive to the existing sort machinery rather than a bespoke priority path.
**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; `verify-views.mts` and `verify-list-lenses.mts` both ALL PASS against live Neon; a throwaway `viewItemsQuery(..., {field:"urgency",dir:"asc"})` emits `order by "items"."urgency" asc nulls last`. Browser smoke of the builder form was blocked by the preview browser hanging on Clerk auth (form never hydrated); engine + settings round-trip are covered by the verify scripts.
**Affects:** src/lib/views.ts (`SORT_FIELDS`, `SORT_COLUMNS`), src/lib/list-lenses.ts (`LENS_FIELDS`), src/lib/mcp/tools/views.ts (sort description), src/components/views/ViewBuilder.tsx (sort + priority filter), src/components/build/ListTabsEditor.tsx (Priority preset, task-gated). Additive; no migration.

## ADR-164: Filter/sort a view by ANY property, plus an AND/OR rules layer (`filter.where`, property sort)
**Date:** 2026-07-19
**Status:** accepted (CORE — extends the view-definition shape and the MCP `create_view` contract; Tyler agreed 2026-07-19). Fully additive and back-compat: every stored view is unchanged, no schema/migration. Scope decided with Brandon: **one combinator** per view (flat all-AND or all-OR), not a nested tree; nesting can be a later additive step.
**Context:** Brandon asked to filter and sort by any property of any type (custom fields included), and to express basic rules like "tagged A AND B" or "tagged A OR B, sorted by X". The engine already had two of the pieces latent: property sort existed in the list-tab lens layer (`{ field:'property', propertyKey, numeric }` with a numeric cast + nulls-last) but wasn't exposed to saved views, and property *filtering* existed but only for `select`/`multi_select` equality, silently AND-ed. Text/number/date/checkbox/relation filtering and any OR logic were absent. Two storage shapes matter: scalar properties live in `items.properties` jsonb; relation fields (Tags/People/Project…) are `relations` edges keyed by `role`, so "tagged X" is a relation condition, not a jsonb one.
**Decision:** Three additive extensions, sharing one new client-safe vocab module (`src/lib/view-where.ts`):
1. **Sort by any property.** `parseSort` widened from `ViewSort` to `ListSort`, so a saved view (and dashboard-widget `sortOverride`) can carry `{ field:'property', propertyKey, numeric }`; the query engine already honored it. ViewBuilder's Sort-by control gains a "Properties" optgroup (text/number/date/select/checkbox).
2. **Filter by any property, with kind-appropriate operators.** `opsForKind()` maps each property kind to its operators — text/url: contains/eq/neq/set/empty; number: eq/neq/gt/lt/gte/lte/set/empty (numeric cast); date: on/before/after/set/empty (ISO text compare, ADR-008); checkbox: checked/unchecked; select: anyOf/noneOf; multi_select: anyOf/allOf/noneOf.
3. **AND/OR rules — `filter.where`.** A single-combinator `WhereGroup { combinator:'and'|'or', conditions[] }` where each condition's `subject` is `property` | `relation` (with `key`) | `priority` | `status`. `buildWhereSql` folds it into one parenthesized clause, AND-ed with the view's existing scalar filters (they scope; the rules refine — so `type=task AND (tagged A OR tagged B)`). Relation conditions are directional `exists` subqueries on `relations` (source = item, role = field key): anyOf = one `target_id in (…)`, allOf = one exists per id AND-ed, noneOf = `not exists`. All owner-scoped, body-free, and containment/relation ops stay index-friendly.
- **UI:** a new `RuleBuilder` component (advanced-filter section in the ViewBuilder), one combinator toggle over condition rows (field ▸ operator ▸ value); relation values are picked from a lazy `/api/items?type=…` fetch, select/priority/status values from fixed option lists. Rules clear on a type change (their keys are type-specific) and stale conditions are dropped on save.
- **MCP:** parseViewInput already routes `filter.where` + property `sort` through the shared parsers, so `create_view` gains both for free (tool description updated).
**Why / alternatives:** Chose one combinator over a nested tree (covers every example Brandon gave; Notion itself hides nesting as advanced) — nesting stays a clean later addition since `WhereGroup.conditions` could later hold sub-groups. Chose to widen `parseSort` to the existing `ListSort` rather than invent a second sort field (the engine already spoke `ListSort`). Chose directional relation matching (source = item) to mirror how relation *fields* author their edges, not the both-directions `relatedTo` scope filter. Kept everything additive/back-compat so no view migration and Tyler's instance is untouched until he pulls.
**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` clean. New `scripts/verify-view-rules.mts` — 20 assertions ALL PASS against live Neon: numeric property sort (asc, nulls last), text contains / date after / number gt / set / empty operators, AND vs OR combinator, priority anyOf, and relation any/all/none/set/empty, plus the combined query carrying `owner_id` and selecting no body. `verify-views.mts` + `verify-list-lenses.mts` still ALL PASS (no regression from the parseSort widening). Browser smoke of the RuleBuilder UI was blocked by the sandbox preview hanging on Clerk auth (same limitation as ADR-162); the builder is a controlled component that emits exactly the `parseWhere`-validated shape the engine tests cover.
**Affects:** src/lib/view-where.ts (new: WhereGroup/WhereCondition/ops/parseWhere), src/lib/views.ts (`ViewFilter.where`, `buildWhereSql` + condition builders, `parseSort`→`ListSort`, `ViewDefinition/ViewInput.sort`), src/lib/dashboard-widgets.ts (sortOverride → ListSort), src/components/dashboards/WidgetSettingsPopover.tsx (spread sort), src/components/views/RuleBuilder.tsx (new), src/components/views/ViewBuilder.tsx (property sort + RuleBuilder mount), src/lib/mcp/tools/views.ts (description). No schema, no migration.

## ADR-165: Desk shows every panel as a live editor (source + followers), superseding the one-mounted-editor rule
**Date:** 2026-07-20
**Status:** accepted (relaxes ADR-146's "only the focused panel mounts an editor")
**Context:** In the Desk, only the focused ("writer") panel mounted the real editor; every other panel showing the same item rendered a read-only `MarkdownPreview` fed by the doc store. Two problems Brandon hit: (1) a preview twin **flashed white** on each live update — `MarkdownPreview` dropped to a "Rendering…" placeholder whenever its text changed while the new server render was in flight; (2) clicking a preview panel to edit swapped the whole body subtree (preview → freshly-mounted editor), which **reformatted** the content (editor line-spacing/chrome differs from the rendered preview), **reset the scroll to the top**, and **couldn't place the caret between the exact characters clicked** (the preview DOM and the editor DOM don't map 1:1). Brandon's insight: since there is one physical keyboard, only one panel can ever be typed into at a time, so two mounted editors on one item can't actually race a save — the structural "one editor" guard was stricter than physics requires.
**Decision:** Every Desk panel that shows an item mounts the **same** `ItemEditor` (editable, toolbar on), keyed by item id so moving the pen between panels is a prop flip, never a remount. The focused panel is the **source** (drives edits, publishes to the doc store, saves). Every other panel is a **follower** (`follower` prop): it applies the source's live title/body in place via the editor's existing `setContent(emitUpdate:false)` path and never publishes or saves. Because the editors are identical and always mounted, there is no preview↔editor swap: no flash, no reformat, and a click lands the caret natively between the exact characters (verified: click at viewport y=558 → caret at y=550). Follower body updates are trailing-debounced 300ms (the old preview cadence) so a fast typist doesn't re-parse+setContent into every mirror per keystroke.
**Save-handoff safety (ADR-134):** followers pin their save baseline to the mirrored content and flush any pending save the instant they become a follower, so handing the pen back and forth between panels never trips the cross-device 409 guard. Verified end-to-end against live Neon: typed in panel A → appeared in B; clicked into B → B took over, typed → both synced, **no conflict banner**, server body persisted correctly.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected keeping the preview and only smoothing the swap (reading-first shell + scroll/caret compensation, the first attempt this session): it still swapped DOM representations, so the caret was only ever *near* the click and the chrome shift was visible. Rejected an editable=false read-only Tiptap for followers: flipping editable on click doesn't retroactively seat the caret at the click. Two identical always-editable editors is the only shape that makes the transition physically seamless. The reading-first machinery added mid-session (LazyMarkdownEditor caret-at-coords + height-hold, `autoEditAt` threading) is left dormant (nothing sets `readingFirst` in the Desk now) rather than ripped out — it's inert (defer-by-hiding) and improves the genuine reading-first path if ever enabled.
**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit` clean. Live browser test against production Neon on a throwaway scratch note (created + soft-deleted after): two panels, one-click handoff, pixel-perfect caret, live source→follower sync in place (no flash/remount), clean save with no false 409, body round-tripped to the server. `MarkdownPreview` also hardened independently (module-level rendered-HTML cache keyed by content + retain-last-HTML-while-rerendering) so its other uses (large-doc preview, the Rich/Source/Preview toggle) never flash either.
**Affects:** src/components/desk/DeskItemPanel.tsx (always render ItemEditor, `follower={!writer}`, dropped the MarkdownPreview twin + reading-first/autoEditAt Desk wiring), src/components/markdown-editor/ItemEditor.tsx (`follower` prop: title/baseline mirror + flush-on-become-follower), src/components/markdown-editor/BodyEditor.tsx + TabbedBody.tsx (follower re-seed of the mounted child, debounced), src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownPreview.tsx (HTML cache + retain-stale, general flash fix), src/components/markdown-editor/{LazyMarkdownEditor,MarkdownEditor}.tsx (dormant reading-first caret/height improvements). No schema, no migration.

## ADR-166: The Planner becomes an app-wide scheduling surface — a placement layer, a range rule (`end_at` + `withEnd` date props), and Timeline as a third mode
**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Status:** accepted (CORE — adds `items.end_at`, a `withEnd` field on the date `PropertyDef`, and a placement contract the renderers + eventually MCP/the builder emit; Brandon confirmed Tyler approves as the work lands, per the "core is frozen behind agreement" rule). Additive and back-compat: the column is nullable, `withEnd` defaults off, no data reshaped. Built across slices; this ADR is written up front with the foundation (slice 2) and the renderer slices follow.
**Context:** The Planner (ADR-131) is a tasks-only tool: it hardcodes, inside `PlannerTimeGrid`, which date field a drop writes (`scheduledDate`/`dueDate`) and where time lives (`properties.scheduledTime`). Events place by `meeting_at` (a real instant) and fall to a static read-only grid; nothing else dated can be dragged at all. Brandon's pivot (2026-07-23): stop treating this as a task widget and make it a Ledgr-wide feature — **any** item with date fields renders on Month / Multi-day / a new Timeline, whatever is writable can be dragged, whatever has a start and an end can be resized, and an item missing a capability just drops that affordance rather than disappearing (so a work-log-by-`note_date` or a created-date review still shows, read-only). This also settled the long-open "duration vs end" question and "Multi-day is just a zoom of the timeline" observation.
**Decision:** Four parts.
1. **A placement layer (`src/lib/placement.ts`), the new cross-cutting seam.** `resolvePlacement(item, spec, tz)` turns any storage shape into one normalized `{ start, end, can:{move,resizeStart,resizeEnd} }` (anchors are `{ymd, minutes|null}`); `buildPatch(item, spec, tz, next)` turns a drag back into a PATCH body. Renderers consume placements and never read a date field directly, so a new field shape is added here alone. A `PlacementSpec` is `{ start: DateRef, end?: DateRef }` where `DateRef = {field: BuiltinDate} | {prop: key}`; it lives in `views.display` (jsonb) beside the calendar mode. The layer encodes both what renderers must not know — how each field stores time (calendar-day UTC-midnight vs zoned instant vs floating `scheduledTime` block) — and which edits are legal (read-only `created`/`updated` can't move; a single anchor can't resize until it gains an end).
2. **The range rule: any date field may carry an optional end; duration is always derived.** The "6 of one" equivalence only holds *within a day*; it breaks for multi-day spans (an end *date* is meaningful, "2,880 minutes" is not), for date-only items (duration has nothing to attach to), and for zoned instants across DST. So start + optional end is canonical. Realized two ways: a new **`items.end_at`** (timestamptz, nullable) pairing with `meeting_at` for events; and a **`withEnd`** flag on a `date` `PropertyDef` whose end value is a sibling ISO scalar at **`properties[key + "__end"]`** (`placement.END_SUFFIX`). The sibling-scalar choice keeps the start at `properties[key]` a plain ISO scalar, so every existing filter/sort/query path (ADR-008 lexical compare) is untouched, and the pairing is declared once on the property (no manual "which field is the end" wiring — Brandon's explicit call). A task keeps `scheduledTime {start, durationMinutes}` as its intra-day block; placement.ts converts that block into a start/end pair for display and writes the duration back on resize.
3. **`meeting_at`/`end_at` writes compose the zoned instant.** A drag on an event writes a full instant (via `zonedInstant`, the DST-correct guess-and-correct in the new client-safe `src/lib/zone.ts`), never a UTC-midnight day, so time-of-day survives every move; task writes stay day + floating time. Both rules live in `buildPatch` only.
4. **Timeline is a third `CalendarMode`; Multi-day converges into it (renderer slices).** `month | timegrid | timeline` — a `views.display` value, not a new `view_layout` enum, so no migration and no clash (the mode string, the event lens `kind:"timeline"`, and the record widget `id:"timeline"` are independent namespaces). The Timeline is one horizontal zoomable axis (Hour→5-Year); at fine zoom it does the Multi-day job, so `PlannerTimeGrid` retires by defer-by-hiding (unrouted, recoverable) once the Timeline lands.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected bolting a `meeting_at` branch beside the `scheduledDate` branch inside `PlannerTimeGrid` — that deepens the exact hardcoding that made the tool tasks-only. Rejected storing event duration in `properties.scheduledTime` (the earlier lazy idea): it duplicates "when" across a zoned instant and a floating block and can't express a multi-day or date-only span; `end_at` is the honest model and Brandon chose architecture over ADR-avoidance. Rejected a new date-property *kind* for ranges (would fork every kind-aware code path); a `withEnd` flag on the existing `date` kind with a sibling key is additive and leaves the query engine alone. Extracted the pure zone helpers out of the DB-importing `today.ts` into `zone.ts` so the client renderers can compose instants without pulling the DB into the bundle (today.ts re-exports them, so nothing else changed).
**Verification (slice 2 / foundation):** `tsc --noEmit` clean. New `scripts/verify-placement.mts` — 27 assertions ALL PASS: task day (all-day chip, movable, not resizable), task time-block (bar, resize writes duration), event `meeting_at`+`end_at` (both-edge resize, move round-trips through a DST-aware instant preserving time-of-day and day), custom date prop + `__end` range (read + write both keys), read-only `created_at` anchor (shown, no move/resize), unscheduled → rail, and rail-clear. Migration `0048` applied to the dev Neon branch (trimmed to the single `ADD COLUMN "end_at"` — the autogen diff was polluted by pre-existing stale drizzle meta snapshots on main that re-emit already-applied 0041/0042/0046 objects; see next_steps note).
**Affects (slice 2):** src/lib/placement.ts (new — the seam + tests), src/lib/zone.ts (new — pure zone conversions extracted from today.ts), src/lib/today.ts (imports/re-exports from zone.ts), src/db/schema.ts + drizzle/0048 (`items.end_at`), src/lib/items.ts (listColumns select), src/components/views/ViewRenderer.tsx (`ViewItem` gains `endAt`/`noteDate`), src/lib/{dashboard-resolve,related-views,view-render}.ts (ViewItem constructors), src/lib/item-input.ts + item-mutations.ts (accept/patch `endAt`), src/lib/types.ts (`PropertyDef.withEnd` + tolerant parse), scripts/verify-placement.mts. Renderer slices (PlannerTimeline, mode toggle, Month/Multi-day refit, scroll-bug fix, builder controls, lens relabel) follow and will extend this entry's Affects.
**Verification (slice 4 / Timeline writable):** `applyTimelineDrag` (span-preserving move + front/back edge resize, snap- and precision-aware) added to timeline-geometry.ts; verify-timeline-geometry.mts extended to 37 assertions ALL PASS (`tsc` clean on changed files; 3 pre-existing errors in verify-placement.mts noted separately). Live (dev preview, 200-item tasks planner): move → one `scheduledDate` PATCH + optimistic reposition; back-edge resize of a scheduled→due bar → `dueDate` moves, start held; drop-to-rail → both dates cleared; rail→axis → `scheduledDate` set to drop day; no console errors.
**Affects (slice 4):** src/lib/timeline-geometry.ts (`applyTimelineDrag` + `GAnchor`/`TimelineDragKind`, `shiftAnchor`/`units`/`fromUnits` helpers), src/components/planner/PlannerTimeline.tsx (pointer-driven move/resize/rail-drop/rail-schedule via placement.buildPatch, optimistic override + undo toast, edge auto-scroll; imports buildPatch/Anchor), scripts/verify-timeline-geometry.mts.
**Verification (slice 5 / Month refit + meetingAt gate + Multi-day retired):** verify-placement.mts extended (timed-task-no-due chip + move preserves block + no spurious dueDate); `tsc`/`eslint` clean on changed files. Live: Month task move → one PATCH keeping `scheduledTime {10:30,90}`, dueDate untouched; day-number open → Timeline centered off-today; a temp meetingAt calendar view mounted the interactive planner (was static grid).
**Placement-seam correction (slice 5):** the intra-day scheduledTime block-end is now derived ONLY when the spec declares no end field (so deriveSpec's scheduled→due pairing can't let a block masquerade as a dueDate write), and `buildPatch`'s scheduledDate write preserves the existing block duration on a plain move (resets to default only when there's no prior block). This closes a slice-4-exposed path where dragging a timed, due-less task set dueDate to its scheduled day.
**Affects (slice 5):** src/lib/placement.ts (shared `deriveSpec` + block-derivation guard + duration-preserving write; type-only view imports), src/components/planner/PlannerMonth.tsx (placement-based bucketing/drag/undo via buildPatch, `can.move` gate, display+tz props), src/components/planner/PlannerCalendar.tsx (Multi-day segment retired/unrouted-but-recoverable, `openDay`→timeline+`focusDay`, hint text, pass display+tz to Month), src/components/planner/PlannerTimeline.tsx (import shared `deriveSpec`, `focusDay` centering), src/components/views/ViewRenderer.tsx (calendar branch routes `meetingAt` to the interactive planner), scripts/verify-placement.mts.
**Verification (slice 6 / builder controls + chip polish):** `tsc`/`eslint` clean on changed files; both verify scripts still pass. Live: at Year zoom Timeline chips render as 16px dots with overflowing labels and pack by true extent (6 lanes vs a ~13-lane smear); a calendar view's builder edit page renders the Default-view + Timeline-zoom controls initialized from stored `display`, and create round-trips `display:{mode,zoom}`.
**Affects (slice 6):** src/components/planner/PlannerTimeline.tsx (coarse-zoom dot + overflow-label packing: `DOT_W`/`COARSE_PPD`, true-extent lane packing), src/components/views/ViewBuilder.tsx (calendar-display section: Default view mode + Timeline zoom → `display` payload), src/lib/list-lenses.ts + src/components/build/ListTabsEditor.tsx (event lens label "Timeline"→"Agenda"; `kind` unchanged). **Deferred follow-ups (documented in next_steps):** event-canvas `end_at` field, `withEnd` date-property toggle in the type editor, an explicit start/end field picker, and type-aware month quick-create on non-task calendars.

## ADR-167: The table of contents is container-relative and can be pinned open as a per-item sidebar (extends ADR-114)
**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Status:** accepted (not core — one component's positioning + a UI affordance; the only shared-surface touch is an additive `users.settings.tocPinnedItems` and one `[data-toc-scope]` CSS rule). Additive and back-compat: no schema change, no migration, an absent settings key means "nothing pinned."
**Context:** Brandon reported the outline missing in the Desk (2026-07-27). Root cause: `FloatingToc` is mounted in exactly one place, `ItemCanvas`, and the Desk bypasses it entirely (`DeskTabset → DeskItemPanel → ItemEditor`). But mounting it there would have failed anyway: the component positioned itself `fixed` against the *viewport* (`fixed top-1/2 right-4`, plus a `fixed bottom-24` button), so N Desk panels would have stacked N rails on one screen edge, each pointing at a different document. The same viewport assumption also forced `variant:"modal"` to show the phone bottom-sheet inside a 52rem-wide peek panel, where a rail would obviously be better. Brandon also asked for a third presentation: hover or click the outline to reveal it, with a pin at the top of the list that turns it into a sidebar.
**Decision:** Four parts.
1. **Container-relative, not viewport-relative.** The outline renders as a `sticky top-[var(--nav-pt,0px)] z-30 h-0` layer that must be the **first child** of its `[data-toc-scope]`. One pattern pins correctly against whatever actually scrolls — the window on the full page, the peek's scroll body in the modal, each Desk panel's own `overflow-auto` div — with no coordinate math and no per-host special-casing. First-child is load-bearing: a sticky box only pins while its containing block is in view, so mounted after the content it would sit stranded at the bottom. Any future host of a body editor now inherits correct positioning by marking a scope.
2. **Presentation comes from the measured container, not a media query.** A `ResizeObserver` on the scope yields `showRail = w >= 560` and `canPin = w >= 640 && visibleHeight >= 600`. This retires the `variant: "page" | "modal"` prop. The height clause is what encodes Brandon's "no pin on mobile, yes on tablet": width alone can't express it, because a landscape phone is *wider* than a portrait tablet.
3. **Three states.** Collapsed marks rail → flyout (CSS hover, plus a click/tap-held `open` state since hover is unreachable on touch, closed by Esc or outside click) → pinned sidebar, docked right (never mirrored to a left nav), drag-resizable 12–24rem via the same pointer-capture handle `Modal.tsx` uses for the peek. Pinned sets `--toc-pin-w` on the scope and `globals.css` turns that one variable into the content's `padding-right`, so the rail's width and the room made for it cannot drift. The sidebar is positioned `right: -width`, because that same padding also shrinks the sticky layer's content box — `right: 0` parks it a full width *inside* the gutter it just opened and overlaps the prose. Deliberately no transition on the padding: easing it would reflow the whole ProseMirror document every frame.
4. **The pin is remembered PER ITEM, in owner settings.** `users.settings.tocPinnedItems: string[]`, the same shape and parser as `favorites` (`parseFavorites` generalized to `parseItemIdList(raw, cap)`), written through the existing generic `PATCH /api/settings` — no bespoke endpoint. A stored pin is only *honoured* where `canPin` holds, so a note pinned at the desk opens as the bottom sheet on a phone.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected `items.properties.tocPinned`, the obvious home: every write to `items` bumps `updated_at` via the schema's `$onUpdate`, so pinning an outline would restamp the note as edited and push it up the recently-updated lists. Pinning is a reading preference *about* an item, not a change *to* it — the same reasoning ADR-114 used to keep `tocByType` out of the (instance-global) `types` row. Rejected a per-device `localStorage` pin: Brandon's framing ("I'd always want that toc pinned on that note") makes it a property of the note, which should follow it to the tablet. Width stays per device (`ledgr:toc-width`) because that *is* about the screen. Rejected per-type pinning as a Build setting — a larger slice, and worth seeing whether it's wanted after living with per-item. Known ceiling (marked `ponytail:` in settings.ts): the id list is rewritten whole on each toggle, fine for dozens, wrong at thousands.
**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, and `next build` all clean. Verified live against the dev server on a 39-heading note: Desk panel shows the rail (scope = the panel's own scroll div, sticky, `--nav-pt` zeroed); hover expands the flyout; pin docks a 240px sidebar with the prose reflowed clear (overlap −188px, was +52px before the `right: -width` fix); pin survives a reload; synthetic PointerEvents resize 240→320→clamped 384 (max) and 192 (min) with padding tracking at every width and no overlap; a split Desk shows **two independent pinned outlines**, and opening a different note in one panel gives it its own 13 headings, unpinned, while the first keeps its 39 pinned; shrinking panels to 398px drops both to the sheet and stops honouring the stored pin; a 1000×420 landscape-phone shape shows the rail but withholds the pin; the full page honours a pin set from the Desk and holds position through a 1500px scroll with active-heading tracking following; the **peek panel now gets the rail it never had**; unpin clears the sidebar, the padding, and the settings entry. No console or server errors.
**Affects:** src/components/canvas/FloatingToc.tsx (rewritten: sticky container-relative layer, ResizeObserver breakpoints, click-to-open, pin toggle + monochrome stroke pin icon, resizable pinned sidebar; dropped the `variant`/`navPosition` props), src/lib/settings.ts (`tocPinnedItems` + `TOC_PINNED_HARD_CAP`; `parseFavorites` → `parseItemIdList(raw, cap)`), src/app/globals.css (`[data-toc-scope] { padding-right: var(--toc-pin-w, 0px) }`), src/components/canvas/ItemCanvas.tsx (mount moved to the top of the scope, new props), src/components/desk/DeskItemPanel.tsx (scope marker + `--nav-pt: 0` + the mount), src/components/desk/DeskContext.tsx + DeskClient.tsx + src/app/desk/page.tsx (carry `tocByType` + `tocPinnedItems` into the client shell), src/components/build/TocSettingsEditor.tsx (stale description copy). No schema, no migration.

## ADR-167a: Live editing context works in the Desk — one reporter for the surface, and a clear that can't outrun a handoff
**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Status:** accepted (not core — wires an existing feature into an existing surface; the one shared-behavior change is that `clearActiveContext` gained an optional item guard, which is additive and back-compat). No schema change, no migration.
**Context:** Brandon reported (2026-07-27) that the live editing context (ADR-162) — the row Claude reads over MCP to answer "this note" / "this sentence" — reports nothing while he works in the Desk. Same root cause as ADR-167: `ActiveContextTracker` is mounted only by `ItemCanvas`, and the Desk bypasses it. His framing pointed straight at the design: "even if multiple items are open on Desk, only one item can be the active item I'm editing at a time."
**Decision:** Three parts.
1. **One tracker for the whole surface, not one per panel.** `DeskActiveContext` (new) mounts a single `ActiveContextTracker` in `DeskClient`, pointed at the focused panel's active item tab (focus-follows-click already guarantees exactly one). A view/dashboard tab focused, or an empty panel, unmounts it and clears the row.
2. **Selections are scoped to the panel holding the pen.** The tracker gained an optional `scopeSelector`, resolved *fresh on every selection change* rather than cached at mount; the Desk passes `[data-desk-focused] [data-toc-scope]` (`DeskTabset` marks the focused panel). A single mounted tracker whose scope re-resolves means moving the pen is a prop change, not a remount. Without this, a highlight in a follower panel would be reported as the focused note's selection — attributing one note's text to another.
3. **A clear can no longer outrun a handoff.** The old tracker DELETEd in the same effect cleanup that preceded the next item's POST, so the two raced; whoever's DB write landed last won, and a lost race blanked the context. Latent and rare for page-to-page navigation, but Desk focus switching would have fired it constantly. Fixed at both ends: teardown moved to its own mount-only effect (so re-pointing to another item is POST-only, never DELETE-then-POST), and the DELETE now carries `?itemId=`, with `clearActiveContext(ownerId, onlyItemId?)` deleting only when the row still points at that item — so a straggler matches nothing instead of wiping fresh context.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected mounting the tracker inside `DeskItemPanel` gated on `writer`, which is the obvious placement and gets scoping free via `closest("[data-toc-scope]")`: every focus switch would unmount one tracker and mount another, turning the DELETE/POST race from rare into routine. Rejected letting the Desk tracker run unscoped (accepting any document selection) on the theory that focus-follows-click keeps selection and focus together — mostly true, but it silently mis-attributes text between notes when it isn't, and the fix was one prop. Rejected a server-side sequence number to order the writes: the item guard gets the same protection with no new state.
**Known gap:** `ItemCanvas` suppresses the tracker for a template prototype (`!item.isTemplate`); the Desk doc store doesn't carry `isTemplate`, so a template opened in a Desk panel does report context. Harmless (it's still a real item Claude can read) and not worth a store field until templates are routinely edited in the Desk.
**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `next build` clean. Verified live against the dev Neon branch with `liveContextEnabled` temporarily flipped **directly in the DB** — deliberately not through `PATCH /api/settings`, whose enable path also seeds a "Note Editing Partner" prompt *item*, which is a content write and not something a test should make. Confirmed end to end: the Desk reports the focused panel's item; moving the pen to the other panel re-points the row (and the row *survives* the handoff, proving the race fix); a highlight in the focused panel is captured verbatim; the same highlight made in the **unfocused** panel is rejected and clears the selection rather than attributing another note's text; the full-page canvas still reports after the tracker rewrite (no regression); and navigating away from any item clears the row. Flag restored to `false` afterward.
**Affects:** src/components/desk/DeskActiveContext.tsx (new — the single reporter, resolves the focused panel's active item), src/components/canvas/ActiveContextTracker.tsx (optional `scopeSelector` resolved per selection; lifecycle split so teardown is mount-only; DELETE carries `?itemId=`), src/lib/active-context.ts (`clearActiveContext` item guard), src/app/api/active-context/route.ts (DELETE reads `?itemId=`), src/components/desk/DeskTabset.tsx (`data-desk-focused`), src/components/desk/DeskClient.tsx + src/app/desk/page.tsx (`liveContextEnabled` threaded, reporter mounted).

## ADR-168: The item page's chrome row is sticky, and `--item-chrome-h` is the one offset every sticky layer in the canvas stacks under
**Date:** 2026-07-28
**Status:** accepted (not core — one row's positioning plus a CSS-variable convention local to `[data-toc-scope]`). No schema change, no migration, no API change.
**Context:** On the full item page, the row under the breadcrumb is the item's *only* trash / ⋯ / word-count chrome, and scrolling a long note took it off screen (Brandon, 2026-07-28) — so acting on the item meant scrolling back to the top. The modal doesn't have the problem: its own header carries those actions above the scrolling body. Making the row sticky is a two-line change on its own, but the canvas already has two other sticky layers that pin at `var(--nav-pt)` — the body editor's formatting/mode bar (z-30) and, since ADR-167, the outline (z-40) — and all three pinning at the same offset means they pile up on each other.
**Decision:** The chrome row goes `sm:sticky` at `var(--nav-pt)` with z-35 (above the editor bar so its ⋯ menu opens over it, below the outline and the app's overlays), and `ItemCanvas` publishes its height as **`--item-chrome-h` on the `[data-toc-scope]` element**. The editor bar and the outline pin at `calc(var(--nav-pt) + var(--item-chrome-h))`, so they stack under the row instead of sliding over it. The variable is set *only* when the sticky row actually renders (full page, non-template), so it falls back to `0px` in the modal, in a Desk panel, and on mobile — every other host keeps its current offsets with no per-host branching. The row gets a fixed `h-[var(--item-chrome-h)]` rather than padding: the box must be exactly as tall as the offset the others pin below, or a strip of content scrolls through the gap between them.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected measuring the row at runtime and writing the height back as a variable — a ResizeObserver and a state write for a row whose height is a design constant. Rejected hardcoding the offset into each of the three consumers: that's the same number in three files, and the next sticky layer added to the canvas silently gets it wrong. Rejected making the row sticky on mobile too (a phone's vertical space is the scarce thing, and the actions are already in the ⋯ menu). One trap worth recording: **the JS side can't read these variables with `getPropertyValue` + `parseFloat`.** Custom properties hold their authored token, so `--nav-pt` reads as `"3.5rem"` → `3.5`px — a pre-existing bug in `FloatingToc`'s jump offset, latent because the outline scrolled *close enough*. `stickyTopOf()` now reads the sticky layer's own computed `top`, which is a used length in px and therefore correct whatever the `calc()` sums and whichever breakpoint applies.
**Also in this commit (two narrow-container overflow fixes, same session's WIP):** `CustomProperties`' inputs and `RelationField`'s typeahead input + dropdown gained `max-w-full`, and the typeahead's positioning anchor moved from the input to the whole field (the only box with a known width). The task rail scrolls on `overflow-y`, which makes `overflow-x` `auto` too, so a few px of horizontal spill from a `w-56`/`w-64` control showed up as a scrollbar that shifted the rail's labels out of view.
**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `next build` all clean. Geometry confirmed live against the dev server via computed styles: on the item page the chrome row resolves to `height: 52.8px` (3rem at this root font size) and the outline's sticky layer resolves to `top: 52.8px` — i.e. it pins exactly at the row's bottom edge, with z-order 35 < 40 as intended; `--nav-pt` was `0px` for this nav position, so the sum was exercised on the `--item-chrome-h` term. **Not visually confirmed:** the Browser pane was not displayed this session, so the page never composited frames (screenshots time out, every `getBoundingClientRect().height` reads 0, and the lazy editor's IntersectionObserver never fires). The scroll-through behavior is therefore verified by construction and by the resolved offsets, not by eye.
**Affects:** src/components/canvas/ItemCanvas.tsx (sticky chrome row, publishes `--item-chrome-h`), src/components/canvas/FloatingToc.tsx (sticky top includes the new term at `sm`+; `stickyTopOf()` replaces the two `parseFloat(getPropertyValue(...))` reads), src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.tsx + BodyEditor.tsx (sticky tops include the new term), src/components/build/CustomProperties.tsx + src/components/relations/RelationField.tsx (the overflow fixes).


## ADR-169: Date pickers commit on confirm, never on the browser's first `change`
**Date:** 2026-07-28
**Status:** accepted (not core — one shared UI control and its call sites). No schema change, no migration, no API change.
**Context:** Brandon reported (2026-07-28) that scheduling a task from the Inbox was unusable: click the calendar chip, click the date field, and the moment you navigate the browser's own calendar to a different month, a date you never picked is saved and the popup closes. The Inbox chip's "Pick" field wrote on the first change event (`onChange` → PATCH → `setDateOpen(false)`), and a native date input fires a value change *while* the user is still moving around inside the picker — so the first month change was read as a final answer. The native picker is browser chrome (synthesized clicks pass through it to the page), so the exact emission cannot be reproduced from automation; the pattern is the bug regardless of which browser emits it.
**Decision:** A new `src/components/ui/DateInput.tsx` holds the picked value as a **draft** and commits only on an explicit "Set" (or Enter). It re-adopts the stored value when that changes underneath it (the adjust-during-render pattern `SchedulePopover` uses), and its Set button `preventDefault`s mousedown so focus never leaves the input — a surface that exits on the input's blur can't unmount before the click lands. Swapped in at every date field that wrote on first change *and* dismissed itself: the Inbox chip (`InboxTaskControls`), the shared row menu (`RowMenu`), the rail's Schedule/Due popovers (`DayField`), the subtask date (`SubtaskSchedule`), and the quick-add card (`AddTaskCard`). The Today / Tomorrow / +1 wk / Clear shortcuts are untouched and stay one click.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected listening for the DOM `change` event instead of React's `onChange` (which is `input`): it assumes a browser fires only one of the two while navigating, which is exactly the unverifiable part. Rejected debouncing the write — month-scrolling still commits a wrong date if the user stops there. Rejected building an in-app month grid: much more code than the bug is worth, and the native picker is the right rung. The draft + apply shape is not new here — `BulkActionBar`'s date field already worked this way, and this makes it the standard.
**Left alone deliberately:** inline *field* editors that write on change but stay on screen (`FieldStrip`, `CustomProperties`, `RelatedRow`). A stray value there is visible in place and re-pickable; they don't vanish on write. If one of them starts closing something, it needs `DateInput` too.
**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit` clean. Verified live against the dev server by replaying exactly what the native picker does — setting the input's value and dispatching `input` — on all four reworked surfaces: none fires a PATCH, all keep their popup open, and the Set button appears. Confirmed the commit path still works end to end (Inbox chip Sep 15 → chip and DB update, popup closes; quick-add card chip → Aug 20; subtask → "Oct 7 +98d" with the relative offset recalculated, proving the blur-vs-click race is handled), and that clicking away still leaves the subtask's edit mode. The Inbox popup widened `w-40` → `w-52` and both "Pick" rows wrap, so Set sits inside the panel.
**Affects:** src/components/ui/DateInput.tsx (new), src/components/inbox/InboxTaskControls.tsx, src/components/lists/RowMenu.tsx, src/components/canvas/rail/DayField.tsx, src/components/subtasks/SubtaskSchedule.tsx, src/components/tasks/AddTaskCard.tsx.


## ADR-170: Comments on the body are CriticMarkup in the markdown itself, not a side table
**Date:** 2026-07-28
**Status:** accepted — **CORE** (the canonical body format and its extended dialect). Both-agree: Brandon proposed 2026-07-28, Tyler cleared it the same day. No schema change, no migration, no API change.
**Context:** Brandon wants to comment on a span of an item's body: select text, leave a note to self, see it in the margin like Word/Notion or behind an inline icon like Logos, hover the note to light up the text it points at, hide or show comments on export. Explicitly non-conversational (no replies, no threads) and explicitly portable: a comment should still work, or fail gracefully, when the exported `.md` is opened in another editor or in Notepad.
**Decision:** Comments live **in the canonical body markdown** as **CriticMarkup**: `{==anchored text==}{>>the note<<}` for a ranged comment, `{>>the note<<}` alone for a point comment. One new pure module, `src/lib/editor/comment-markdown.ts`, sits in the existing render chain next to `stripBlockAnchors`/`flattenTabs` with the two ends the pipeline needs: `renderComments()` expands a comment into two **adjacent sibling** spans (`.cmt` around the anchored text, `.cmt-note` right after it), and `stripComments()` drops the markers and the note while keeping the author's prose. Adjacency is the mechanism: it lets CSS pair the two with `+`/`:has()` and lets the tap handler find the note with `nextElementSibling`, so a comment needs no id, no counter, and no state anywhere.
`markdownToHtml`'s new third argument picks the end. It defaults to **render**, so the in-app read view shows comments and `markdownToText` indexes them (searching your own notes is the point). The print/PDF/pinned-offline/share document and the paper `.docx` export pass **false**, so a private note never reaches a reader; the owner can opt a print back in with `?comments=1`. A share link cannot opt in at all yet.
**Why in-body, not a `comments` table:** a table keyed to the existing `^id` line anchors is a smaller diff and it loses data. Anchors drift as the body is edited, and `restoreRevision` restores the body while knowing nothing about a side table, so every comment on the item would silently orphan. Because the CriticMarkup anchor **is** the text it points at, it cannot drift, and revisions, the weekly backup, and the OneDrive export cover comments for free. It also fails the portability requirement outright: comments would be invisible in the exported `.md`. The cost accepted in exchange: comments are in the body, therefore always exported and always searchable. A note that stays out of the export would be a different feature (the confidential tier ADR-075 already declined).
**Why CriticMarkup rather than our own spelling:** the syntax is the wire format. Once notes carry it and those notes have been exported, changing it means a migration over live production bodies, so we take the established spelling (iA Writer, Marked 2, Ulysses, Obsidian plugins) and get legible degradation in other editors for free. `{==`/`{>>` collide with nothing already in the dialect: live item tokens are `{{item.*}}` (ADR-139), block anchors are a trailing `^id` (ADR-090), canvas tabs are an HTML comment (ADR-095), colors are `<span>`/`<mark>`, and Pandoc attribute spans are `{.class}`.
**Deliberately not implemented:** CriticMarkup's `{++insert++}`, `{--delete--}`, `{~~a~>b~~}`. That trio is collaborative redlining; these are notes to self. A bare `{==highlight==}` with no comment after it is also not ours (Ledgr highlights are `<mark>`), so it stays literal text. No replies, no resolve (delete is resolve), no author or avatar (one user), no timestamps (in-body markdown has no metadata slot; an optional date prefix is the upgrade path if it's ever wanted).
**The visual contract:** a **comment owns the underline channel, a highlight owns the fill channel.** That is what lets a commented phrase sit inside a yellow highlight and still read as two separate things, and it is why `.cmt` must never take a permanent background. Hover borrows a soft fill for as long as you hover, coupled in both directions with `.cmt:hover` and `.cmt:has(+ .cmt-note:hover)` — no JavaScript. At ≥1024px the note floats into a right gutter as a Word/Notion-style card; `float` + `clear: right` stacks cards automatically and never overlaps them, which is the whole reason to use floats instead of absolute positioning plus a JS layout pass, and `.ledgr-prose:has(.cmt-note)` means the gutter is only reserved when the body actually has a comment. Below that, and on paper, the note renders as a bracketed italic **inline** aside: a block-level note inside a paragraph splits the sentence it belongs to and orphans the rest of the line into what looks like a new paragraph (caught in a live print render, 2026-07-28).
**Mentions inside comments count.** `syncMentionRelations` reads the raw body and cannot tell a comment from prose, so `{>>ask [@Roger](ledgr://item/…)<<}` creates a real relation. Deliberate: doing nothing is both the lazy answer and the true one.
**Known ceilings (marked `ponytail:` in the code):** the parser is fence-aware but not inline-code-aware, so a literal `{>>x<<}` inside single backticks is rewritten — the same limitation `stripBlockAnchors` already has, asserted in the test so it's pinned rather than surprising. A comment is single-line by design, which is also what keeps an unclosed `{>>` from running away and swallowing the document. The gutter breakpoint is viewport-width, not container-width, so a narrow Desk panel on a wide screen still gets a gutter; wrap it in `@container` once `.ledgr-prose`'s host declares `container-type`.
**Phasing, and one finding that mattered:** phase 1 (parser + read render + print/share/docx off) and phase 2 (margin cards, pins, hover) are read-only. They render comments in preview mode and the print document, but preview is gated on `isLargeBody` (ADR-125), so an ordinary note opens in the Tiptap rich editor, where the raw CriticMarkup showed as literal text. **Phase 3 was therefore required for the feature to exist in daily use, not optional polish**, and it shipped in the same branch.
**Phase 3 (the editor):** `src/components/markdown-editor/comment-mark.ts` holds a `comment` mark whose `renderMarkdown` emits the CriticMarkup pair and whose inline `markdownTokenizer` reclaims it (the same reclaim-before-Link shape TextColor/Highlight use, so nested `**bold**`/`*emphasis*` inside an anchored range survives a rich⇌source flip). The note rides as a string ATTRIBUTE, not editable inline content: a comment holding rich content would need a nested editor instance for a note to self, so instead it's markdown text in one textarea that renders rich wherever the body renders. A sibling `CommentCards` extension decorates each comment-marked run with a widget that is literally the same `.cmt-note` element `renderComments()` emits, so the editor reuses the read view's stylesheet (gutter card, hover coupling, pin) instead of growing a second one.
**The mark stays OUT of `HTML_WRAPPED_MARKS`** (extensions.ts). That set un-escapes text inside marks that emit raw inline HTML; this one emits CriticMarkup, so its content is genuinely markdown and genuinely needs the serializer's normal escaping. Adding it there "for consistency" would break bold inside commented text.
**Clicks are handled at the DOM level, not with ProseMirror's `handleClick`** (which was tried first and silently never matched). The mark is `inclusive: false` and the card is a widget sitting at the run's END, so a position lookup there finds no mark. Instead: a click on the underlined text reads the note off the span's own `data-note` and resolves its position with `posAtDOM`; the card carries its run's start and note in the event it fires. Save/Delete then `setTextSelection(at).extendMarkRange("comment")`, which is what makes an edit rewrite the whole comment rather than a fragment — relying on the caret alone did not work, because focus has moved to the note's textarea in between.
**The editor UI reuses the hyperlink editor's shape, not a popover:** a textarea row below the toolbar (⌘/Ctrl+Enter saves, Escape cancels, Delete removes the comment and keeps the text). Nothing to position, and mobile behaves identically to desktop. The toolbar button sits in the color/highlight cluster, gated by `showTb("comment")` and disabled without a selection unless the caret is already in a comment.
**One editor-only imperfection, accepted:** ProseMirror splits a mark across text nodes, so an anchor containing `**bold**` renders as several `.cmt` spans while the read view always emits exactly one. The note lands after the last fragment, so the pin is keyed to `.cmt:has(+ .cmt-note)` (one pin, not three — caught live), but card-hover lights up only that tail fragment. The read view is unaffected.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-comment-markdown.mts` (37 assertions, run `npx tsx scripts/verify-comment-markdown.mts`) covers both forms, the unclaimed forms left literal, the no-runaway-match guarantee, fenced code untouched, the inline-code ceiling, formatting and mention links surviving inside a note, and the three chain outcomes (rendered in the read view, present in the FTS text, absent with stray-brace-free prose on print). `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean; `verify-print` and `verify-block-anchor` still pass.
Confirmed live on the dev server. Read paths: `/items/<id>/print` carries zero comment markup and zero stray braces outside code fences while keeping the prose, `?comments=1` renders every note with bold inside, and preview at desktop width stacks four margin cards in the gutter with **no overlap** (measured geometry: identical left edge and width, strictly increasing tops). Editor: a seeded body's CriticMarkup parses into marks and cards; **three rich⇌source flips are byte-identical at 543 chars with zero backslashes**, including a comment inside `<mark class="hl-yellow">` and an anchor containing `*emphasis*` (the escape trap, avoided); creating a comment from the toolbar over a live selection writes the exact expected `{==…==}{>>…<<}`; clicking the underlined text opens the row on that comment's note and saving rewrites only that comment; Delete removes the comment and keeps the annotated sentence intact.
**No unit test for the editor half:** the mark and its decoration are exercised through a real Tiptap instance, and standing one up headlessly would mean adding a test framework for one file (Principle 5). The round-trip is the thing that can silently rot, and that is what was verified in the browser; the pure parser underneath it has the assertion suite.
**Affects:** src/lib/editor/comment-markdown.ts (new), src/components/markdown-editor/comment-mark.ts (new), scripts/verify-comment-markdown.mts (new), src/lib/markdown-render.ts (`prepare()` extracted, third arg on `markdownToHtml`), src/lib/print-html.ts (`comments` opt, `CMT_CSS`), src/app/items/[id]/print/route.ts (`?comments=1`), src/app/share/[token]/route.ts (never opts in), src/lib/papers/msm-docx.ts (strips), src/components/markdown-editor/markdown-editor.css (the `.cmt*` rules), src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownPreview.tsx (delegated tap-to-open), src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.tsx (registration, toolbar button, comment editor row, click wiring), src/components/markdown-editor/toolbar-icons.tsx (the speech-bubble icon + `comment` in TOOLBAR_ITEMS).


## ADR-171: The machine/MCP contract carries all 8 dashboard widget kinds, not 4
**Date:** 2026-07-29
**Status:** accepted, **CORE** (the machine/MCP API contract). Both-agree: Brandon proposed 2026-07-29, Tyler agreed. No schema change, no migration, no UI change.
**Context:** `add_widget` advertised only the ADR-064/065 base kinds (view, stat, action, text). The three dashboard-canvas kinds (tree, embed, container, ADR-111) plus image were deliberately pinned out of the MCP enum because the machine contract is frozen-core, so a widget vocabulary that had grown to eight in the app was still four over MCP. Brandon wants to assemble activity dashboards (a Home board, a planning board, an organizing board) by asking an agent for them instead of hand-building each tile, and the archetypes he described need exactly the kinds that were withheld: a nested outline, an embedded item, a tabbed group.
**Decision:** `add_widget` (and the inline `widgets` array on `create_dashboard`) now accept every kind in `WIDGET_KINDS`. The MCP tool file imports that contract instead of keeping its own pinned copy, gains an `itemId` input property for `embed`, and documents each kind's `settings` shape in the tool description and in the shaping guide (which also gains one worked "Home" board recipe: create the views, create the dashboard, then add a view widget, a stat on the same view, a second view widget, and a quick-capture action).
**Nothing else changed.** `parseWidget` was already whole-vocabulary: it requires a real uuid `viewId` for view/stat/tree, a real uuid `itemId` for embed, drops a nested container, and clamps the image fields. The handler needed no new validation, only the extra argument passed through and a widened error message.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected keeping the enum pinned and telling the owner to finish agent-built boards by hand: that leaves the interesting archetypes half-buildable and makes "ask for a board" a partial promise. Rejected a second tool for the canvas kinds: same parser, same table, same append, so a parallel tool would be pure duplication.
**This widening is one-way.** Once an agent-built dashboard stores a tree, embed, or container widget, the enum cannot shrink again without orphaning live widgets on a production dashboard. It is additive and the parsers already covered the whole vocabulary, which is why the gate was cheap to pass, but the direction only goes forward.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-mcp.mts` covers placing a tree (with a viewId), an embed (with a real itemId), a container whose settings carry two non-container children, and an image, reading the stored jsonb for the fields the serializer omits, plus two negative cases (an embed with no itemId and an embed with a bogus itemId are both rejected). Its stale always-on tool list also gained the four tools shipped since it was last touched (`link_to_line`, `attach_file`, `create_upload_url`, `embed_attachment`), which had been failing the tool-list assertion. ALL PASS; `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean.
**Affects:** src/lib/mcp/tools/dashboards.ts, src/lib/mcp/guide.ts, scripts/verify-mcp.mts.

## ADR-172: Fuzzy search is per-criterion confidence scoring, with dates that bend a curve instead of drawing a line
**Date:** 2026-07-29
**Status:** accepted, **not core** (a new page-level feature; no schema change, no migration, no change to the machine/MCP contract, and `src/lib/search.ts` is untouched). Brandon designed it interactively 2026-07-29 and approved the plan (`plans/fuzzy-search.html`).
**Context:** Existing search answers "find the rows containing these words." Brandon's actual problem is the opposite: "I half-remember it, and I can't recall the exact wording or the date, but I know several vague things about it." Every filter in the old search *excludes*, so a wrong guess about the type or the month silently hides the target. He asked for weighted guesses instead: stack up what you recall, say how sure you are about **each piece separately**, and let the ranking absorb the uncertainty. Explicitly no AI (Principle 3).
**Decision:** A fuzzy mode on the same `/search` page, behind a "Tune" toggle (defer-by-hiding, so the plain path is unchanged). Each criterion carries its own confidence from a three-stop vocabulary (`might` / `probably` / `sure`), and confidence means different things for two different classes of criteria:
- **Continuous (a date):** the dial sets the *sharpness exponent* of the falloff curve, `1 / (1 + (days_outside / softDays) ^ p)` with p ≈ 6 / 2.5 / 1. It is **never** a hard filter at any stop. Sure is a cliff just past the stated window, Might is a long tail, all three cross at half credit at the window edge (so the dial pivots around the owner's guess rather than moving it), and none ever reaches zero, so a strong text match can always overcome a wrong date.
- **Categorical (term, type, relation, tag):** there is no continuum between note and meeting, so there is no curve to bend. `sure` becomes a real `WHERE` filter (exactly today's behavior); the lower stops boost without excluding.
**Term expansion is layered and deterministic:** the owner's dictionary (wins) → a committed WordNet map → number-word twins ("4" ⇄ "four", "3rd" ⇄ "third"). Postgres FTS already stems, so no morphology is duplicated here. Disambiguation is not attempted per-word: WordNet cannot know which *sense* was meant, so wrong-sense noise is accepted and contained by ranking it below exact hits. The owner's own lever is typing several words, whose shared sense accumulates score.
**Loose dates are typed, not picked.** `parseFuzzyWhen` in `src/lib/nl-date.ts` is a third section beside the existing forward-looking task-capture grammar, which is left untouched. It returns a *range plus a softness*, never a point, because "within the last week" is a range while "about a month ago" is a plateau; three phrase shapes (`window` / `around` / `before`) collapse into that one return type, so the scorer needs only one formula. The plateau half-width is half the stated distance, so a vaguer phrase self-fuzzes ("6 months ago" gets ±90 days, "a week ago" gets ±3.5) with no extra dial. The owner picks which date is meant (created = "I made it", updated = "I worked on it", or any date-kind custom property).
**The whole thing is one SQL query** over indexes already maintained (`items_search_gin`, `items_type_idx`, `items_properties_gin`): a candidate gate of OR'd index-backed conditions, per-criterion signals normalized to 0..1 (term ranks by `max(...) over ()`, which is legal in a select list and ORDER BY, so no CTE), each times its weight, summed. The scoring shape is Discover's (ADR-127) with the owner holding the weights instead of a hardcoded table.
**The recency prior stands down when a date is given.** `RECENCY_MILD` still multiplies the score in the no-date case, but if the owner said "at least six months ago", boosting recent rows would contradict the thing they just asserted, so their statement wins.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected storing a numeric weight (a 1–10 scale, or `0.3` in the URL): the numbers are false precision nobody calibrates consistently, they freeze today's guess about what the value means, and they cannot express a sharpness exponent. Storing the *word* keeps the whole curve family retunable without invalidating a saved search. Rejected a POST body for the criteria list: a search worth finding twice is worth bookmarking, so it stays an extended GET (`term=teaching~sure`), with `~` rather than `:` because a tag value can legitimately contain a colon. Rejected a synonyms table (a schema change, therefore a core gate, for a feature that needs neither) and a runtime thesaurus API (a network call in every search, breaking determinism); a committed JSON is inert, diffable, and works offline. Rejected embeddings/AI reranking outright (Principle 3).
**Back-compat is deliberate and total.** `src/lib/search.ts` is not modified, so quick search, the command palette, the @ typeahead, and MCP `search_items` are bit-for-bit unaffected. A suffix-less `type=note` / `person=<uuid>` still means a hard filter, and a plain `q=` with no fuzzy params runs the old exact path. Fuzzy mode engages only when a `term=`/`tag=`/`when=` param or a `~` suffix is present. Not exposed over MCP for now (an agent can iterate exact `search_items` calls, which is the same job by other means).
**Any property can be a criterion, and the UI reaches three kinds of them.** Brandon asked for this during the design pass, and it decomposed into three cheap extensions rather than a separate feature: date-kind fields join the When source select, select/multi_select fields become repeatable tag rows, and relation-kind fields become a "linked as" role narrowing on the person criterion. All three are populated from the live type registry and deduped by property key across types (a criterion matches `items.properties[key]`, or a relation `role`, regardless of which type declares it), so two types sharing a "campus" field offer one row with the union of their options. **Deferred, by hiding not deleting:** number/text/checkbox/url property criteria — the `Criterion` union and the URL vocabulary already generalize to them, only the pickers are missing.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-search-deep.mts` (ALL PASS, 62 checks) covers expansion precedence, number twins, the phrase grammar, the curve's monotonicity and its never-zero floor, and the generated SQL (owner-scoped, body-free, and no date comparison in `WHERE` at any confidence). Live against the ~9k-item dev corpus: 83–178ms warm; a **Sure** date of "within the last week" still returns month-old term matches ranked down rather than dropped; a soft `type=meeting` leaves task/transcript/event hits in place; the dictionary takes effect with no redeploy; `created` vs `updated` genuinely diverge. `next build`, `tsc --noEmit` clean, and the 1.8MB WordNet map is confirmed present only in `.next/server`, never in a client chunk. Browser-verified on the dev-auth preview: the panel opens from Tune leaving the plain view untouched, a word row shows its live synonym count and returns ranked matches with why-chips, a tag row narrows correctly, and Roger + "linked as Attending" cuts 50 matches to 34 events he attended. The soft-criterion promise is visible in the list — with a tag at Might, an untagged event still appears, ranked below.
**Known ceilings (marked `ponytail:` in the code):** the confidence weights and exponents are tuned by feel, like `recency.ts`'s W and H, so expect one pass after living with it. There is no index on `items.updated_at`, so a date-only search at `might` degrades to a bounded scan-and-rank (`items_owner_updated_idx` is the upgrade). The score expression repeats in ORDER BY, so each `ts_rank` evaluates about twice per candidate row; ordering by the select alias is unavailable because Drizzle emits no SQL aliases, and a CTE is the fix if it ever needs to be faster.
**Affects:** src/lib/search-deep.ts, src/lib/synonyms.ts, src/data/synonyms.json, scripts/build-synonyms.mts, src/lib/nl-date.ts, src/app/api/search/route.ts, src/app/search/page.tsx, src/components/search/SearchClient.tsx, src/lib/settings.ts, src/components/settings/SettingsForm.tsx, scripts/verify-search-deep.mts.

**Follow-up (2026-07-30): the search PAGE was unreachable from the UI, so the nav's /search hijack is gone.** Brandon reported that the Search nav item opens quick search instead of the page. The cause was a hardcoded `href === "/search"` check in `NavShell.tsx` (5 sites) and `Launcher.tsx` (2 sites) that turned any slot pointing at `/search` into a command-palette button. Combined with `command-index.ts` deliberately omitting Search ("it *is* the palette") and the destination picker offering exactly one "Search" entry, there was **no route to `/search` from anywhere in the UI** — the ADR-172 feature shipped to production reachable only by typing the URL.

He proposed two fixes: two addable search items, or one item with a setting inside it. **Both were rejected in favour of deleting the special case**, because the palette was never depending on that slot: it has a global ⌘K handler plus a *permanent, hardcoded* Search button in all four nav layouts (`pillTrailingControls`, `mobileTrailingControls`, the top bar, the side rail). The slot hijack made the palette reachable five ways and the page zero ways, so a slot at `/search` now simply navigates like every other destination. That deletes code rather than adding a second concept or a per-slot flag, and it needs no migration: nothing about stored `navSlots` changes meaning, since a slot pointing at `/search` now does what it always claimed to.

Two supporting renames so the two tools are distinguishable in a bar that can show both: the destination picker's entry is **"Advanced search"** (the palette keeps the plain "Search" button), and `command-index.ts` now lists Advanced search as a jump target — reaching for the tuned page is the natural next move when a quick search missed, which is exactly the case ADR-172 exists for. `Launcher`'s `onSearch` prop went dead with the tile branch and was removed; the drawer's palette button arrives via `barRow`.

**Fixed in passing:** `scripts/verify-nav-and-deletes.mts` had a red assertion on `main` (`tools children cap at 20`) that could never pass — it built a group with **10** children and asserted the parsed length *equalled* the cap of 20. The parser was correct; the test now feeds `MAX_TOOLS_CHILDREN + 5` so it actually exercises the slice. ALL PASS.

**Verified in the browser:** the palette lists "Advanced search" first under PAGES and clicking it lands on `/search`; the permanent rail Search button still opens the palette; the picker offers "Advanced search" as a destination. `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean; `verify-build-mode` and `verify-nav-and-deletes` ALL PASS. **Also affects:** src/components/nav/NavShell.tsx, src/components/nav/Launcher.tsx, src/lib/nav-slot-options.ts, src/lib/command-index.ts, scripts/verify-nav-and-deletes.mts.

**Follow-up 2 (2026-07-30): quick search now carries you into the tuned page, which is the right door for both.** Brandon asked whether mobile quick search had been lost, and proposed the fix: the Search button keeps opening quick search, and *inside that box* there is an option to escalate to the full page. Mobile quick search was in fact never lost (`mobileTrailingControls` still opens the palette, verified at 375px), but the proposed affordance was the missing piece, and the plumbing already existed in a form nobody could find: pressing Enter in the palette with a query and **zero** results silently pushed `/search?q=…`. A hidden path on an empty result set is not a feature.

It is now a **permanent footer button in the palette**: "Advanced search for <query>" when something is typed, an explanatory line when not, always visible rather than only when the palette comes up empty. "I can't find it" is exactly the moment you want stacked criteria, so the affordance belongs there and not one layer deeper. The handoff carries the typed query through `?q=` (the prefill the page already supported for the Discover panel, ADR-127), so escalating never costs a retype. `goAdvanced()` is the single function behind both the button and the Enter path.

**The "Advanced search" row added to `command-index.ts` in follow-up 1 was removed as part of this**, deliberately: with a permanent footer, a PAGES row is a second, worse door to the same place. It competes for the arrow-key selection and, unlike the footer, drops the query on the way. One affordance, always present, context-carrying.

**Verified on mobile at 375px** (the surface Brandon asked about): tapping the bar's magnifier opens quick search, typing `budget` updates the footer to "Advanced search for budget", and tapping it lands on `/search` with the query prefilled, 50 ranked matches and highlighted snippets already rendered, Tune ready. `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean. **Also affects:** src/components/search/CommandPalette.tsx.


## ADR-173: The comment card is a popover in the note's own coordinate space, and the outline lists the comments
**Date:** 2026-07-30
**Status:** accepted. Not core (no schema, no body format, no provider seam), so no both-agree gate. Follow-on to ADR-170 (comments) and ADR-167 (the outline's positioning model). No migration; UI only.
**Context:** ADR-170 shipped and Brandon used it. Four things came back, plus one thing he wanted next: *"I see all my comments in one place, click them to scroll to that location."* All five ship together, because they touch the same glyph and the same outline.

**The four fixes, by root cause rather than symptom:**

1. *"The note text is a bit big, almost looks like a header."* `.cmt-note` used `font-size: 0.85em` and inherited weight and letter-spacing from whatever it annotated, so a comment on an `h2` rendered at 0.85 × that heading, bold: a second headline. It now resets every inherited text property and sizes in `rem`. The card also moved from surface-1 (nearly the page color) to surface-2 with the stronger hairline, because it wasn't reading as a distinct object.
2. *"Clicking the comment chip or the text jumps my window to the top of the note."* The editor row rendered above `<EditorContent>` next to the sticky toolbar, and its autofocused textarea scrolled the document to the top to reveal itself. **The row is now a popover** (`CommentPopover.tsx`), shared by the editor (textarea) and the read view (rendered, read-only).
3. *"I can't click inside text that has a comment on it."* A separate cause with the same report: the open handler lived on the anchored **text**, so a click there could never place a caret. That handler is deleted. Only the card/icon opens the popover, and commented text is ordinary clickable text again.
4. *"Make the comment icon a speech bubble (on mobile it looks like two lines, like an `=` sign)"*, then *"any way to improve it? it's a little wonky."* The mobile `=` was an `::after` pseudo-element pin on the anchor — and **being a pseudo-element it could not be hit-tested, which is why the whole commented phrase had to be the tap target.** `.cmt-note` itself now collapses into a tappable filled speech bubble (`--cmt-bubble` mask), which fixed the glyph and the tap target in one move. The glyph itself was a circle with a thin spike for a tail (mush at 16px stroked, worse filled at 14px); it is now a rounded rectangle with a proper triangular tail.

**Why a popover and not "fix the row's scroll":** the row's problem was that it lived somewhere other than the comment. `CommentPopover` positions **in the host wrapper's coordinate space, not the viewport**, so it scrolls with the note instead of detaching from the comment it belongs to. At ≥1024px (the same breakpoint the margin gutter uses) it opens absolutely over the card where the card already sits; below that it is a fixed popup at `top-16` with a scrim, which is deliberately clear of the on-screen keyboard rather than under it.

**Clicking away SAVES a non-empty draft rather than discarding it.** The popover floats over a document you are meant to keep clicking, so dropping typed text on a stray click would be a trap. Escape and ✕ discard. That asymmetry is the decision, not an oversight.

**The outline's Comments section.** A "Comments · N" list under the heading list in `FloatingToc`, from the **same live DOM read** as the headings, so it tracks edits as you type through the existing 200ms-debounced MutationObserver with no new machinery.
