Two locked choices, made by Brandon against rendered mockups:

- **Two-line rows** (the note, then the anchored text in dim smaller type). The note alone ("tighten this") often doesn't say where it points.
- **No comment ticks on the collapsed rail.** The rail stays headings-only; comments appear once the outline is open. He chose the quieter rail.

**The open question, answered: keep the two-heading gate as it is.** The consequence of the quiet rail plus `MIN_HEADINGS = 2` is that a note with comments but 0–1 headings gets no outline, therefore no comment list. Brandon accepted that over relaxing the gate and giving the rail a lone bubble: long notes have headings, short ones don't need an index, and the comments are still reachable in the margin (desktop) and on their inline bubbles (mobile). The alternative would have reopened the rail decision in exactly the case where the rail would otherwise be empty.

**No active-section tracking for comments,** unlike headings: highlighting "the comment nearest the viewport" would fight the heading highlight for attention, and the list is short. Rows get hover styling only. Clicking a row scrolls to the **anchored text**, not the card, because on a wide screen the card floats out in the margin a line or two off from what it points at.

**The bubble path is now a named export** (`COMMENT_BUBBLE_PATH` in `toolbar-icons.tsx`) rather than a third copy. `markdown-editor.css` keeps its own copy in `--cmt-bubble` because CSS cannot import; both sides carry a comment saying to keep them in step.

**One bug the plan carried, caught in the browser.** The plan's anchor-rebuild walked back while `previousElementSibling.classList.contains("cmt")`. A nested mark **inverts the nesting** — `**bold**` inside an anchor renders `<strong><span class="cmt">bold</span></strong>`, not the other way round — so the walk stopped at the `<strong>` and the row showed the tail fragment ("inside it") instead of the phrase ("a run with bold inside it"). The walk now accepts an element that *is* `.cmt` **or contains one**. It stays self-bounding: an earlier comment's `.cmt-note` sits between two runs and holds no `.cmt`. This is ADR-170's "editor-only imperfection" (the read view emits exactly one span) surfacing in a consumer that reads both.

**Found in passing, deliberately not fixed here** (both predate this slice): the Tiptap editor does not parse a **point comment** (`{>>note<<}` with nothing anchored) — it stays literal text in the editor while the read view renders it as `.cmt-point` — so the editor's comment list is short by one on such a note; and the read view renders `##` as `<h3>`, pushing `###` to `<h4>` and out of the outline's 1–3 scan, so the read view's heading list can be shorter than the editor's.

**Verified in the browser** at 1280px and 375px, both editor and read view (Half A had **never once been rendered** when it was written — it was verified numerically only, so this pass was the point). The card computes to normal body size on an `h2`; opening a comment no longer moves the viewport; the popover lands on the card and scrolls in lockstep with it (−200px against a −200px scroll); clicking commented text puts a caret in it at the expected offset with the anchor's `cursor` back to `auto`; the mobile note is a 22×18 bubble-masked tap target with the retired pin's `content: none`. The outline's section renders in all three open presentations (pinned sidebar, flyout, bottom sheet) and not on the collapsed rail; the count matches; the bold-anchored row shows the whole phrase; a point comment renders one line with no empty second line; a jump lands the anchored text 16px below the sticky chrome, not under it; editing a note updates its row live; and a note with no comments shows no divider and no empty header. `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean.
**Affects:** src/components/markdown-editor/CommentPopover.tsx (new), src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownPreview.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/markdown-editor.css, src/components/markdown-editor/comment-mark.ts (`posInCommentSpan()` deleted, dead with the text-click path), src/components/markdown-editor/toolbar-icons.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/useIsDesktop.ts (generalized to `useMediaQuery`), src/components/canvas/FloatingToc.tsx.

## ADR-174: A comment bridges lines by repeating its note, not by widening the syntax (extends ADR-170)

**Date:** 2026-07-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Branch:** `claude/multiline-comment-bridging-994f76`

**Context:** Brandon: *"Comments need to be able to bridge multiple lines without generating multiple comments. Not sure how to achieve that technically, since it's based on MD on the back end."* Selecting text across two paragraphs produced two comments: two margin cards, two rows in the outline, and editing one silently diverged from the other.

**Why it split.** CriticMarkup is **inline**, so one `{==anchored==}{>>note<<}` pair cannot cross a block boundary: an anchored span would have to open inside one `<p>` and close inside another. Tiptap already knows this — its serializer closes and reopens an inline mark at every block boundary *and* every hard break — so a three-paragraph selection serializes as three pairs on its own. On top of that, editing was bounded the same way: `extendMarkRange` resolves through `getMarkRange`, which walks `$pos.parent`, so a save rewrote the caret's paragraph and left the other segments carrying the old note.

**The decision: the note text IS the comment's identity.** Adjacent pairs carrying the same note are ONE comment — one margin card (after the first line), one outline row, one hover group, one edit, one delete — with every line it covers underlined. Nothing about the syntax changes, so an exported `.md` still degrades legibly in iA Writer or Obsidian, and a comment can never run away past a line.

**Do NOT widen the regex to `[\s\S]` instead** (the fix `comment-markdown.ts`'s own earlier ponytail note suggested, now rewritten to say the opposite). A single multi-line pair would emit invalid nesting across a paragraph break, could not round-trip through the editor's mark, and would hand an unclosed `{>>` the whole document to swallow — the exact hazard the single-line match was chosen to prevent.

**"Adjacent" means only structure sits between the two pairs** — whitespace, a bullet, a blockquote marker, a heading's `#`s, a table pipe, a hard break's trailing backslash (`BRIDGE_GAP`). Real prose between them is text the comment doesn't cover, so the next pair starts a new comment. The editor half states the same rule against the doc: block nodes and hard breaks never end a run, only inline content with a different note (or none). A fenced code block between two same-note comments breaks the run too, which is why `mapOutsideFences` became `mapLines(line, inFence)` — grouping is stateful, so a caller that never hears about fenced lines would bridge straight across one.

**Hover across blocks needs one class, because CSS adjacency stops at the block.** `markdown-editor.css` pairs an anchor with its card via `+`/`:has()`, which is what keeps comments free of ids — but that cannot reach a segment in another paragraph. `comment-hover.ts` toggles `.cmt-lit` on everything sharing the comment's `data-note` (the attribute the mark already rendered; `renderComments` now emits it too, so one selector serves the editor's ProseMirror plugin and the read view's delegated handlers). The `:hover` rules stay as the no-JS baseline.

**Known ceiling, accepted:** identity is a **string**, so two genuinely different comments with byte-identical notes and nothing but structure between them merge into one. Cheaper than an id the syntax has no room for; the upgrade path if it ever bites is an id, not a wider match.

**Verified live** on the dev-auth preview, editor and read view: a selection dragged across paragraph → heading → paragraph becomes one comment (3 underlined segments, 1 card, 3 pairs in the saved markdown); list items and soft breaks bridge the same way; editing that one card rewrites every segment and persists; Delete clears all segments and keeps the prose; hovering any segment or the card lights the whole group (fill `rgba(250,204,21,0.16)`, strong underline) and clears on leaving; the outline's gathering yields 3 rows for 8 segments, with the bridged anchor preview reading as a sentence ("the tail of paragraph one and the head of paragraph two" — joined with a space between blocks, seamlessly within one). `scripts/verify-comment-markdown.mts` now covers both halves (54 checks, including the editor's range walk over a headless doc). `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean.

**Note for the other builder:** this touches comment RENDERING and grouping, not the `{format, text}` contract or the CriticMarkup syntax itself — no schema change, no new markup. It is close enough to the canonical-body-format line that Brandon should mention it to Tyler before it merges.
**Affects:** src/lib/editor/comment-markdown.ts, src/components/markdown-editor/comment-mark.ts, src/components/markdown-editor/comment-hover.ts (new), src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownPreview.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/markdown-editor.css, src/components/canvas/FloatingToc.tsx, scripts/verify-comment-markdown.mts.

## ADR-174a: The comment hover highlight is a ProseMirror decoration, and the card is edited in place (fixes ADR-174)

**Date:** 2026-07-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Branch:** `claude/comment-hover-inplace-edit`

**Context:** ADR-174 shipped and broke three things in the editor at once, all reported together: hovering a bridged comment didn't highlight, clicking a comment's card didn't open its editor, and clicking inside commented text didn't place the caret (arrow keys still got in). One cause, and it was the hover mechanism.

**The bug: a class on a mark span is a foreign DOM mutation.** ADR-174 lit a comment's segments by toggling `.cmt-lit` on them, which is fine in the read view and wrong in the editor, because there the anchored text is ProseMirror's DOM. PM's `DOMObserver` records the attribute change (`registerMutation` only exempts `view.dom` itself, `contenteditable`, and an empty-to-empty `style`), re-reads that range, and redraws the span. The redraw replaces the element under the pointer, the browser fires `mouseover` on the new one, the handler sets the class again: **measured at ~60 redraws per second while the pointer simply rested on a commented word.** That thrash is what ate the highlight (the element never survived long enough to paint), the card's click (its DOM was replaced between mousedown and mouseup) and click-to-place-caret (PM was busy reconciling a "foreign" DOM change mid-click).

**The fix, in the shape PM expects:** hover state lives in the plugin (`commentKey`, set by a meta-only transaction) and the highlight is `Decoration.inline(run.from, run.to, { class: "cmt-lit" })` over the comment's whole range. `setLit` returns early when the hovered comment is unchanged, which is what makes a loop impossible: PM's own redraw re-fires `mouseover`, and the repeat must be a no-op. A meta-only transaction changes neither doc nor selection, so it never reaches `onUpdate` (no save) and leaves `useEditorState`'s derived toolbar values identical (no React re-render).

**The card keeps a plain class toggle, deliberately.** Widget decorations are exempt from the observer (`WidgetViewDesc.ignoreMutation`), so its class is invisible to PM. Rebuilding the card widget for hover state was rejected: a **tap** has no hover frame before the press, so replacing the element between mousedown and mouseup would swallow it on mobile.

**Consequence for the CSS, and why it has three selectors.** The read view puts both classes on one span (`.cmt.cmt-lit`); the editor's decoration makes PM wrap the text in its own span INSIDE the mark's span, so the nested case (`.cmt .cmt-lit`) re-declares the underline and paints a strong line over the parent's translucent one rather than recoloring it. Both are correct; don't collapse them.

**In-place editing (Brandon: "I don't want a new pop-up OVER the note, the note should just BECOME editable in place").** ADR-173 positions the panel at the card's own box, but the card stayed visible underneath, so the panel read as a second thing covering it. The card now hides while its own note is open (`.cmt-note-editing`, `visibility: hidden` so the float keeps its space and the prose doesn't reflow), which turns the same panel into "the note became a field." `visibility` over `display` matters: the rect that positions the panel is captured before hiding.

**Verified in a real browser** at 1280px and 375px, editor and read view: hovering either paragraph of a bridged comment lights all its lines plus the card (fill `rgba(250,204,21,0.16)`, strong underline) and clears on leave; **0 DOM mutations in a second of resting hover** (the regression test for this bug); clicking the card hides it and opens the field in its place with focus in the textarea; Escape restores the card; Save rewrites both segments (2 pairs in the markdown, 1 card) and restores it; clicking inside commented text places the caret at the clicked offset with the editor focused, and typing there stays inside the anchor; the mobile bubble still opens the popup. `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean, 54 verify checks pass.
**Affects:** src/components/markdown-editor/comment-mark.ts, src/components/markdown-editor/comment-hover.ts (read-view only now), src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/markdown-editor.css.

## ADR-175: "Is a person connected?" has one answer — the generic edge, not a typed field

**Date:** 2026-07-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Branch:** `claude/person-connection-inconsistency-81387e`

**Context:** Brandon, off a screenshot of an inbox task filed by the meeting-minutes automation: *"All I want to know is, IS there a particular person connected to this? And there are several places where that might be true or not true, and they might not agree."* The task's Linked Here listed Kent Hoffsmith and Roger Knowlton, while its PROPERTIES "People" row sat empty at "+ Add."

**The diagnosis: one table, one disagreeing role string.** There is no second storage mechanism — every person connection is a `relations` row. But the task type carried a user-created relation field keyed `people`, and a typed field reads **only** edges with role = its key, source-side only (`outgoingRelationsByRole`). Meanwhile nearly every writer of person edges stamps the default `related`: the Inbox "+ People" chip (its Project sibling on the same line passes `role="project"`, People passed none), MCP `create_item relateTo` (no role parameter at all), `promoteActionItem` (relates every meeting attendee), MCP `relate_items`, `+ Relate`, Discover's Link. So a person linked by any automatic path was *structurally unable* to appear in the People field, and adding them there would create a second, parallel edge for the same pair (the unique is `(source, target, role)`).

**The decision: make the one disagreeing surface conform to the ten that already agree.** A person is connected to a task iff any confirmed edge to a person item exists, either direction, any role. Brandon: *"if I'm linking someone to a task, I always want that person showing in all places that search for people edges."*

- **The task `people` typed field is retired** (migration `0049_person_edges_generic.sql`): role `people` edges fold into `related` (dedupe against existing twins), and the field is dropped from `types.property_schema`. Idempotent, no-op on an instance that never made the field.
- **The task rail gets a bespoke People row** (`PeopleRow`, rendered by TaskCanvas next to the remaining typed fields): reads role-blind + both-direction via `listRelatedItems`, edits through `RelationField` with a new null-role mode (adds POST the default `related`; removes are role-blind, so the ✕ works whichever writer created the edge). Mention-only persons render as read-only `@` chips — the body owns those edges.
- **RelatedPanel gains `claimPersons`** (prop-driven, passed by TaskCanvas): confirmed persons are claimed by the rail's row and don't repeat under Linked Here — the same claiming events already do for their People card. Suggested person edges stay in the panel's Suggested section, where confirm/reject lives. Prop rather than host-type check on purpose: the ADR-069 grid layout for tasks has no People row, so it must keep showing persons in the panel.
- **The Inbox People chip now shows state:** `relatedSummaryFor` grew an optional `type` filter (SQL-side, so the per-anchor cap can't crowd persons out), the Inbox list and Triage deck fetch person summaries per task row, and the chip renders linked first names in the filled style instead of pretending nothing is attached. It stays add-only; removal lives on the canvas.

**Rejected: teaching every writer to stamp `role='people'`.** That needs a role parameter added to MCP `create_item`, per-type field-key resolution in every automatic writer, the opposite backfill — and it re-breaks the next time a writer forgets. The role-blind direction is self-healing because `related` is already everyone's default.

**Untouched on purpose:** event `attending`, group `members`, hiring `reference` — those roles carry real semantics (attendance ≠ mentioned). The `relation` property kind itself is unchanged (tags and project still work role-exact); this retires one user-created field, not the mechanism.

**Known ceiling:** if "People" ever needs to mean something narrower than "any linked person" (e.g. *waiting on*), the typed-field mechanism is still there — declare a new field with its own key and the writers that should stamp it. Also worth a check after deploy: any saved view rule filtering on relation role `people` would now match nothing (none known).

**Affects:** drizzle/0049_person_edges_generic.sql (new), src/components/relations/PeopleRow.tsx (new), src/components/relations/RelationField.tsx, src/components/relations/RelatedPanel.tsx, src/components/canvas/TaskCanvas.tsx, src/lib/relations.ts, src/components/inbox/RelatePicker.tsx, src/components/inbox/InboxTaskControls.tsx, src/components/inbox/TriageDeck.tsx, src/app/inbox/page.tsx, src/app/inbox/triage/page.tsx.

## ADR-176: A slide mark means "put this on the screen" — its own channel, not a color

**Date:** 2026-07-31 · **Status:** Accepted · **Branch:** `sermon-presentation-export`

**Context:** Brandon, on the Sunday hand-off: *"When I preach, I take my manuscript and I export a version of it to give to the sound booth that is running slides. They don't need or want all the coloring and personal notes that I make."* Two documents wanted from one manuscript: a stripped black-and-white copy for print/PDF, and a separate list of the passages and quotes going on the screen.

**What the real manuscripts already do.** Reading "Don't Worry" (a live sermon item) settled the design before any code: the text-color channel is already carrying semantics by hand — red for Scripture, pink for the repeated sticky statement, blue for a key insight, orange for emphasis, green for transitions and illustrations. So the marker for "this goes on the screen" could not be a text color. Brandon: *"not all verses go on the screen… and there might be quotes or other statements that I want on the screen that are not the sticky statement."*

**The decision: the marker is a BLUE HIGHLIGHT (`<mark class="hl-blue">`, colors.ts).** Background and foreground are orthogonal marks in both the editor and the serialized markdown, which is the one property no other channel has — a highlight can layer over the red that means "this is Scripture" without either claiming the other's slot. Brandon's constraint was exactly this: *"if a verse goes on the screen, then I need to highlight it, and if I highlight it, then it won't be red anymore… we need an option that can handle multiple layers of formatting."* Verified in both nesting orders: the red span computes `rgb(242,58,74)` sitting on the highlight wash, and a mark inside a blue span computes the palette blue.

- **No new syntax and no editor code.** The marker-pen control, the `hl-*` serializer, the parse side, and the print CSS all already existed. The highlight channel was unused in every existing manuscript, so nothing had to be migrated.
- **ONE color, not any highlight** (Brandon, 2026-07-31, revising the first build): the other eight marker-pen colors stay available for ordinary highlighting, so "I marked this for the screen" can never be confused with "I marked this for me." Non-blue highlights are still **flattened out** of the booth copy like any other formatting it doesn't need — the booth copy carries no highlight markup at all, and the cue is how a slide announces itself there. A non-blue highlight sitting between two blue ones **breaks** a bridged run, which is correct: that text belongs to neither slide. The color is read via `highlightColorName`, so the class is the primary hook and a background-value fallback still counts (a paste path that drops the class).
- **`booth-export.ts` is ONE pass with TWO outputs**, deliberately not two functions: slide N in the slides document must be the same slide as the `**[SLIDE N]**` cue in the manuscript, and splitting the pass would let the numbering drift. The cue is the point — a list of slides with no cue for when to advance is useless to whoever is running them.
- **Bridging is inherited from ADR-174.** Tiptap closes and reopens an inline mark at every block boundary, so a highlight dragged across three bullets serializes as three marks; adjacent marks with nothing but block scaffolding between them are ONE slide with ONE cue, the same rule (and the same character class) comments use.
- **The strip list, per Brandon:** colors flattened, `~~struck-through~~` material removed *content and all* (it's what he cut), `++underline++` unwrapped to plain text, CriticMarkup notes dropped (already the print default, ADR-170). Bold and italic survive as the one emphasis channel. A line whose only content was struck through is dropped rather than left as an empty bullet.
- **The slides document is ONE child note, rewritten each run.** A sermon takes edits up to Sunday morning and a fresh note per press would pile up near-duplicates; `updateItem` snapshots the previous body to `revisions`, so nothing is lost. No new table, no new column, no pointer to carry — it's found by parent + title suffix.
- **PDF stays the browser's.** `?booth=1` is the existing self-contained print document with a stripped body, so its `@media print` rules remain the PDF leg (Principle 5 — no PDF dependency, same posture as Save Offline).

**Fixed in passing, and load-bearing: `mark { color: inherit }`.** The UA stylesheet gives `<mark>` its own `color` (black), and an element's own color beats one inherited from an ancestor — so `<span style="color:red"><mark>verse</mark></span>` rendered a **black** verse. Highlighting colored text silently destroyed the color, on every surface. One rule in `globals.css` (in-app) and `color:inherit` in print-html's `HL_CSS` (the separate self-contained stylesheet). This is what makes the layering promise true rather than aspirational; don't drop either copy.

**Not core, but adjacent to it.** No schema change, no syntax change, no change to the `{format, text}` contract — this is a *consumer* of a mark the format already had, the same posture ADR-174 took. Worth a word to Tyler because it assigns a workflow meaning to a body-format primitive.

**Known ceiling:** `SLIDE_COLOR` is one constant, so there is exactly one on-screen channel. A second kind of slide (say passage vs. quote, rendered differently) would mean a second color and a `kind` on `Slide`. Also: the button lives on the shared `ItemUtilitiesFooter`, so every type gets it, not just `sermon` — a type gate is the cheaper change if it turns out to be noise on tasks.

**Affects:** src/lib/editor/booth-export.ts (new), scripts/verify-booth-export.mts (new), src/app/api/items/[id]/slides/route.ts (new), src/components/canvas/PresentationExport.tsx (new), src/app/items/[id]/print/route.ts, src/lib/print-html.ts, src/app/globals.css, src/components/canvas/ItemUtilitiesFooter.tsx.

### ADR-176 addendum (2026-07-31): the marker is a slide MARK, not a highlight

**Status:** accepted (Brandon + Tyler, 2026-07-31). 🟢 **CORE**, unlike ADR-176 itself: the original read a primitive the body format already had, whereas this ADDS an element to the canonical body dialect (`<ins class="slide">`), the same category as ADR-145's `<details>` block. Tyler agreed before merge. Recorded in CLAUDE.md's dialect sentence, which is the contract. Additive and back-compat: a body with no slide mark is byte-identical, no schema change, no migration, no new dependency.

Brandon, after using the shipped blue-highlight version: *"In practice, the blue on top of the colored text is painful."*

**The blue highlight was the wrong channel, and the reason generalizes.** It encoded the marker in a COLOR, layered on text that already carries color meaning. Two failures followed: a blue wash under red Scripture is genuinely hard to read, and a blue marker on the palette's blue insight text has almost no contrast against it. Brandon's own next instinct, a thick blue underline, has the same defect plus a worse one: `markdown-editor.css` already states the visual contract in as many words, *a COMMENT owns the underline channel, a HIGHLIGHT owns the fill channel*, so an underline would have been the third tenant of a channel already shared by comments and `++underline++` emphasis, and a slide overlapping a comment would stack two underlines in the same three pixels.

**The decision: a dedicated mark in a THIRD channel, signalled by shape.** `<ins class="slide">…</ins>`, rendered as a blue rule bracketing each END of the span, with a very faint tint. Chosen from a side-by-side mockup of the three candidates over Brandon's actual manuscript colors. Because the signal is a shape rather than a color, it reads on top of all five text colors, and it coexists with a comment's underline and a highlight's fill on the same words without any of the three fighting.

- **`<ins>` and not a `span`, for three reasons that all have to hold.** (1) A slide almost always wraps a colored span, and `<span class="slide"><span style="color:…">…</span></span>` is same-tag nesting: the non-greedy regex both the export and the markdown tokenizer use would close on the inner `</span>` and capture a broken fragment. (2) `<mark class="slide">` would be claimed by the existing Highlight mark, whose tokenizer takes any `<mark>` and reads an unrecognized class as a bare highlight, so using it means surgery on a shared extension. (3) `<ins>` is claimed by nothing here (CriticMarkup's `{++ins++}` is deliberately not implemented, ADR-170) and degrades legibly as underlined text in any other markdown reader.
- **The mark carries no attributes.** Unlike the color and highlight marks it has exactly one state, so there is nothing to round-trip; the entire visual is CSS, in two places (`markdown-editor.css` for the app, `print-html.ts` for the self-contained document). `text-decoration: none` is load-bearing there: `<ins>` is underlined by the UA stylesheet, which would drop it straight back into the comment's channel.
- **A toolbar button immediately left of the comment bubble** (a screen-on-a-stand glyph), because the two are the same gesture for different audiences: a comment is for you, a slide is for the room. It toggles like bold. With a caret inside an existing slide it extends to the whole mark first, so the toggle clears the span instead of setting a stored mark at the cursor, which is the trap the comment toolbar path hit in ADR-174.
- **`"slide"` joins `HTML_WRAPPED_MARKS`.** It emits its content inside raw inline HTML, so without that entry every rich-to-source flip re-escapes the escapes inside a slide and eventually eats the bold.
- **Highlights went back to being highlights**, in all nine colors, and are flattened out of the booth copy like any other formatting it doesn't need. Clean swap, no back-compat path and no migration: the blue-highlight build was live for roughly half an hour and nothing in the data used it.
- **`mark { color: inherit }` stays.** It was found while the marker rode the highlight channel, but it fixes a real bug on its own terms: highlighting colored text should never repaint the text.

**Unchanged:** the booth copy, the `[SLIDE N]` cues, bridging, the strip list, the slides child note, and the PDF leg. The export just reads a different marker.

**Known ceiling:** one mark, one meaning. A second kind of slide (passage versus quote, rendered differently) would need a second mark or an attribute on this one, at which point the attribute-less simplicity above goes away.

**Affects:** src/components/markdown-editor/extensions.ts, src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/toolbar-icons.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/markdown-editor.css, src/lib/editor/booth-export.ts, src/lib/print-html.ts, scripts/verify-booth-export.mts.

## ADR-177: Backspace in a list deletes the line, and an empty bullet is written unambiguously

**Date:** 2026-08-01 · **Status:** Accepted · **Branch:** `fix/editor-outdent-empty-bullets-undo`

**Context:** Three editor complaints from Brandon on the same afternoon of outline work, two of them one bug wearing two faces. *"If I de-indent a bullet it drags all of the sub bullets over with it… de-indenting should only apply to the line I'm currently on."* And: bullets in the "Don't Worry" manuscript that *"render as broken somehow. The text in them is larger, like a heading, and I can't click into those blank lines at all."*

**Outdenting was a red herring; Backspace was the bug.** Reproduced in the real editor: the toolbar button, Shift+Tab, and Backspace-at-line-start all ran the identical standard lift, and a sub-bullet moving with its parent is forced by markdown itself — a nested item has no indent of its own, it is *defined* as one level under its parent, so "B at level 1 with C still at level 3" cannot be written. What Brandon was actually doing, per his own follow-up, was **deleting a line**: cursor to the front of a bullet, Backspace until it merges upward. Tiptap's ListKeymap binds that key to `liftListItem`, so removing one line took three presses and each press re-organized the outline underneath it.

**The decision: at the start of a list item, Backspace joins backward; outdenting keeps Shift+Tab and the toolbar button.** `ListBackspaceJoin` (priority 1000, beats ListKeymap's 100) merges the line into the line above in ONE press. Deliberately narrow, so the rest of the key's jobs survive: with a selection it returns false (Backspace deletes the highlighted bullets), and `undoInputRule` still runs first (backspacing right after typing "- " undoes the bullet).

- **`joinTextblockBackward`, not `joinBackward`.** The plain join pulls the item up as a *second paragraph inside the bullet above* — still two lines, one marker — and needs a second press to merge the text.
- **Two commands, one keypress**, so there is one undo step and the intermediate state is never painted. When the item is the **first item of its list**, its sub-bullets are promoted a level *before* the join. That is exactly the case where the line above lives outside this list (the parent's line, or the paragraph before it), so the join leaves a gap the children have to move into; without the promotion the item's shell stays behind as an empty bullet holding children that are suddenly a level too deep. Brandon, on seeing that first build: *"If the line is empty, it should go away and drag the sub bullets over. But it should NOT outdent BEFORE the line goes away and merges up."* With a preceding sibling there is no gap, nothing is promoted, and the children keep the depth they had.
- **The promotion lifts the CHILDREN, not the item.** Lifting the item is equivalent while its list is nested, but at the top level `liftListItem` un-lists it and flattens the whole subtree — the destructive case. Lifting the sub-list's items (`NodeRange` + `liftTarget`, all items at once so none can be absorbed as a sibling of another) behaves the same at every depth.

**The "giant heading" was an empty bullet, and the spec agrees with the bug.** An empty marker cannot interrupt a paragraph in CommonMark, and a lone `-` on the line after a paragraph *is* a setext heading underline. So `- text` followed by an indented `- ` turns the sentence above into an `<h2>` and swallows the bullets. markdown-it (every render, print, share, export path) and marked (the editor) both do it, because both follow the spec. Nothing was corrupt in the data; the ambiguous form was simply written by the serializer and read back the only way it can be read.

- **On the way out, `spaceEmptyListItems` inserts one blank line** before an empty item that would open a nested list, which is the only spelling CommonMark reads as intended. Narrow by design: an empty item at or above the previous item's level already parses correctly and stays tight.
- **On the way in, the editor needs more than that.** marked is stricter: an empty item *opening* a nested list falls out of the list entirely and lands as a literal `- ` paragraph, blank line or not. There is no spelling of "empty first item" it accepts, so `hydrateEmptyListItems` gives each empty item one zero-width space of content just before marked reads the text and `stripSentinelText` takes it back out of the parsed document. **The sentinel is never stored** — both halves are editor-internal, and what lands in `items.body` stays plain CommonMark. Don't "simplify" this to one pass; the two parsers disagree and both have to be satisfied.
- **Patched at the markdown manager** (`EmptyListItemFix`, the same `onBeforeCreate` discipline as `MarkdownEscapeFix`), because `getMarkdown()`, `setContent`, and `insertContent` all route through `parse`/`serialize`. One patch, every caller.
- **Bodies at rest are not rewritten.** An old body heals when it *loads* and when it *renders* (the pass also runs in `markdown-render.prepare` and the OneDrive export), and only gets rewritten when Brandon next edits that note. No migration, no mass touch of production data.

**Also shipped: Undo/Redo on the toolbar** (leading the bar, the one spot that stays visible on a phone, where there is no Ctrl+Z). StarterKit's UndoRedo already carried ~100 grouped steps of history; this only exposes it. The pair shares one settings id, so one checkbox hides both.

**Not core.** No schema change, no change to the body dialect or the `{format, text}` contract — a serialization *normalization* and an editor keybinding. The stored markdown is strictly more standard than it was.

**Known ceiling:** the sentinel is a per-parser workaround, so if @tiptap/markdown ever swaps marked for a CommonMark parser, `hydrateEmptyListItems`/`stripSentinelText` can go and the blank-line pass alone will do.

**Affects:** src/lib/editor/list-markdown.ts (new), scripts/verify-list-markdown.mts (new), src/components/markdown-editor/extensions.ts, src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/toolbar-icons.tsx, src/lib/markdown-render.ts, src/lib/export/engine.ts.

## ADR-178: Underline gets a toolbar button, and `++text++` finally renders outside the editor

**Status:** accepted (Brandon, 2026-08-02).

**Not core.** No schema change, no syntax change, no change to the `{format, text}` contract. This is a *consumer* of a mark the format already had, exactly the posture ADR-176 took before its addendum (which was core precisely because it ADDED `<ins class="slide">`). Nothing new enters the dialect here. Worth a word to Tyler anyway, since it touches the shared renderer.

**Context:** Brandon asked for an underline button on the formatting toolbar. The mark turned out to already exist: `@tiptap/extension-underline` ships inside StarterKit and is registered unconditionally, so Cmd+U has always worked and has always written `++text++` into bodies. The ADR-176 addendum names `++underline++` as a sitting tenant of the underline channel, and ADR-161 tuned how it inherits text color. What was missing was a button, a settings row, and a renderer.

**The real defect the button exposed:** markdown-it has no `ins` rule, so every server-side surface (Save Offline, share, print, the OneDrive export's HTML, and the FTS document) rendered `++text++` as literal plus signs. That gap predates this change; adding a discoverable button would have made it common. Fixed at the root rather than at the button.

**The decision:** a minimal inline rule in `markdown-render.ts` mapping `++text++` to `<u>`, registered before `emphasis` so the plus signs never reach the emphasis machinery. Inner content is re-parsed inline, so bold, italic, and color spans inside an underline survive. `markdown-it-ins` was declined: roughly 90 lines of dependency for one delimiter, against Principle 5.

**Known ceiling:** the rule matches the nearest closing `++` instead of doing markdown-it's nesting-aware delimiter pairing, so `++a ++b++ c++` pairs shallowly. A mark cannot nest inside itself, so the editor cannot produce that, and neither can a person who means it. Upgrade path if it ever bites: port markdown-it-ins's tokenize/postProcess pair.

**Also:** `++underline++` is now named in CLAUDE.md's dialect sentence. That is documenting an element that was already there and is now fully rendered, not adding one.

**Verification:** `verify-print` covers the render, nested formatting inside an underline, and the two things that must stay untouched (`2 ++ 2` and `++` inside a code span). `verify-booth-export`, `verify-comment-markdown`, `verify-body-modes`, `verify-list-markdown` green. tsc and eslint clean. StarterKit's unconditional Underline registration confirmed in the installed 3.26 dist. **In-browser eyeball still pending:** the dev-auth preview never got past the app shell's loading state this session, so the button has not been clicked in a real browser.

**Affects:** src/lib/markdown-render.ts, src/components/markdown-editor/toolbar-icons.tsx, src/components/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.tsx, scripts/verify-print.mts, CLAUDE.md.

## ADR-179: A third token purpose — browser-minted, labeled app tokens (Build → API Tokens)
**Date:** 2026-08-08
**Status:** accepted (CORE — extends the machine/API auth contract; additive only. Flag for Brandon as a heads-up: a new optional payload field and a third signing secret that defaults to unset, so his instance is unchanged until he sets it.)
**Context:** Tyler stood up a new external app (Overtone) that needs to push data into Ledgr, and couldn't find a way to get it a token. ADR-160 had in fact built browser minting, but only for two purposes and neither fit: the MCP button (Build → AI & MCP) issues `mcp` scope, wrong for an HTTP-API caller, and the `api`-scoped button lives under User Settings → **Save from the web** labeled "clipper token" — nobody reads that as "our API." Worse, both buttons *render as nothing* until their purpose's signing secret is set (`TokenMinter` shows a disabled hint; `ClipperSetup` hides the button outright), and Tyler's instance had **none** of the `LEDGR_*` auth secrets set in Vercel — so the feature was simultaneously mislabeled and invisible. The remaining path was the `make-token.mjs` CLI + an env edit + a redeploy per token, which is exactly what ADR-160 set out to remove.
**Decision:** Add a **third purpose** to the ADR-160 pattern rather than widening either existing one:
1. **`LEDGR_APP_SECRET`** — a third HMAC signing secret. App tokens are `access`/`api` (identical shape to clipper tokens, so the four `api` routes need **no change**), signed with this key alone. Rotating it revokes every app token while leaving MCP, the phone connector, and the clipper untouched. That isolation is the entire reason it's a separate secret and not a reuse of `LEDGR_CLIPPER_SECRET`.
2. **A label on the token** — `signAppToken(sub, label)` embeds an optional `lbl` (lowercase/digits/hyphens, ≤32, the same rule as `make-token.mjs`'s name). `verifyApiToken` reports the caller as `app:overtone` instead of an anonymous `api` caller, so machine-route logs are traceable per app. The field is **optional and additive**: every pre-ADR-179 token verifies unchanged, and an unlabeled app token reports a bare `app`.
3. **`/build/api` "API Tokens"**, its own Build → MAINTAIN entry — the findable home. Name the app, click Generate, copy once. It also states the endpoints an `api` token opens, a working `curl`, the revocation semantics, and a live status row for all three credential paths (app / clipper / static env), so "why is there no button" is answerable from the page itself.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected reusing the clipper secret with only a relabel — it was the cheaper change, but then revoking Overtone would kill the web clipper, and the per-purpose kill switch is the property ADR-160 was built around; a third caller deserves the same treatment as the first two. Rejected a fourth secret per app (unbounded env growth for a single owner). Rejected — again, and for the same reasons as ADR-160 — an `api_tokens` DB table with per-token listing and individual revoke: it's a `schema.md` change and would make the pure/sync verifiers async across ~20 routes. The cost is unchanged and now explicitly stated on the page: no list of live tokens, and revocation stays coarse (rotate the purpose's secret). The label buys back *identification* without buying *revocation* — worth being precise that those are different things.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-minted-tokens.mts` extended with assertions 6–10: roundtrip, label round-trip, `verifyApiToken` naming the caller `app:overtone`, isolation in both directions against the clipper and MCP paths, **the app-secret rotation killing app tokens while a clipper token survives**, label validation (case/space/length/empty), `signAppToken` throwing on a bad label, and an unlabeled token reporting `app`. All pass. Live against a running dev server with the real secret: `POST /api/machine/items` with a minted token → **201** (item created), bogus token → **401**, no token → **401**; the test item was soft-deleted afterward. `/build/api` renders 200 with the name input and Generate button present in the DOM (the disabled hint absent). `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on all changed files (one pre-existing unrelated tsc error in the generated `.next/dev/types` for `src/app/page.tsx`).
**Affects:** src/lib/auth/oauth.ts (`appSecret`/`appConfigured`/`isValidTokenLabel`/`signAppToken`/`verifyAppToken`, `verifyApiToken` third branch, optional `lbl` on `AccessPayload`, `issueAccessToken` label param); src/lib/auth/mint-actions.ts (`mintAppToken`); src/components/build/AppTokenMinter.tsx (new); src/app/build/api/page.tsx (new); src/lib/build-nav.ts (MAINTAIN entry); scripts/verify-minted-tokens.mts; .env.example; runbook.md §3. New secret is additive — deploying without `LEDGR_APP_SECRET` just leaves the Generate button disabled; nothing existing breaks.

## ADR-180: Subtasks and recurring tasks reach the MCP surface (no new machinery)
**Date:** 2026-08-11
**Status:** accepted (CORE — extends the machine/MCP API contract; **additive only**: four new tools, four new optional input fields, one new output key on a shape that already existed. Nothing renamed, nothing removed, no schema change, no migration. Flag for Brandon as a heads-up rather than a blocking review — his instance behaves identically until he deploys, and then only gains tools.)
**Context:** Tyler: "the MCP needs to be able to do Subtasks, and Recurring tasks as well. Currently the MCP cannot do either." Correct, and the gap was purely in the exposure layer: nesting has existed since slice 7 (`parent_id` + `listSubtree` + the "n of m done" rollup) and native recurrence since ADR-073/076/083/085 (the RRULE subset, the per-date completion log, carve, materialized mode, relative subtasks). The MCP layer simply never surfaced any of it — `buildWriteRaw`'s `WRITE_FIELDS` whitelist omitted `parentId`, so `create_item`/`update_item` silently dropped it, and the only route to a repeat rule was hand-writing `properties.recurrence` through `propertyPatch`, i.e. asking the model to compose an RFC-5545 string blind. So Claude could file a task but never break it down, and could never make one repeat.
**Decision:** Four tools, all thin wrappers over the libs the REST routes already call — no new engine, no new table, no new column:
1. **`list_subtasks`** — `listSubtree`, nested, body-free, with the progress rollup on the root and every node that has task children.
2. **`add_subtasks`** — the "break this down into steps" call: a mixed array of title strings and `{title, type?, status?, urgency?, dueDate?, scheduledDate?, url?, bodyMarkdown?}` objects, defaulting to the task type. **Validated all-or-nothing**: every entry runs through `parseItemPayload` before the first `createItem`, so a typo in the last title can't leave half a checklist behind (there's no batch transaction to lean on).
3. **`set_recurrence`** — the rule setter. Three ways in: a natural-language `repeat` phrase through the **same `nl-date.ts` parser quick-add uses**, structured parts, or (on a task that already repeats) a **partial edit** where the stored rule's parts carry through and only the passed fields change. Always builds via `makeRecurrence`, so the stored string is a normalized RRULE from the supported subset and the model never composes one.
4. **`update_occurrence`** — one date of a virtual series: `complete` / `uncomplete` / `carve`. Deliberately **idempotent**, not a toggle: asking for the state a date is already in is a reported no-op. A wrapped toggle is a trap for a retrying model — "complete it" twice would silently un-complete it.
Plus: `parentId` and `scheduledDate` added to `create_item`/`update_item`; a `recurrence` block on `get_item` (described rule, projection, next uncompleted date, log tails) that is **absent entirely** for a non-recurring item, so a plain task's response is byte-for-byte what it was; and `scheduledDate` added to `rowView`.
**Why / alternatives:** Three judgment calls worth recording.
- **Editing a rule KEEPS the completion log** (`resetLog: true` opts out). This **diverges from the canvas control**, which calls `makeRecurrence` and thereby wipes `completeInstances`. Divergence was the lesser evil: a model tweaking `until` on a live series should not silently discard months of "I did this" stamps, and stale stamps are harmless because every reader filters the log against the rule's own projection. The UI's wipe is arguably a latent bug; not touching it here.
- **`"monthly on the 3rd"` is normalized locally, not by widening `nl-date.ts`.** That phrasing is one a model reaches for, and the shared parser reads it as a *plain* `FREQ=MONTHLY` — no `BYMONTHDAY`, and **no error to notice** (it only looks right because dtstart usually is the 3rd). The parser's own spelling is `"the 3rd of the month"`. Rewriting the MCP-side phrasing into the spelling it knows fixes the trap without changing what Brandon's typing does in quick-add, where the phrasing is his habit, not ours.
- **Rejected a `complete_current_occurrence` tool.** `update_item` with a done status already routes through the recurrence-aware `updateItem` and advances the series; a second door to the same gesture invites the model to pick the wrong one. The tool descriptions say so explicitly instead.
Also rejected: reimplementing "next occurrence" arithmetic in the tool layer (`recurrence-service` owns advancing `scheduled_date`, the status flip at series end, and relative-subtask recomputation — none of it is duplicated); and exposing `occurrenceMode: "materialized"` as anything other than an explicit opt-in, with `update_occurrence` redirecting a materialized series to its real occurrence item rather than half-working.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-mcp-tasks.mts` (new, 90 checks, ALL PASS) drives the real dispatcher `callTool` rather than the handlers directly, so arg parsing, `ItemError`→`isError`, and the response shape are all in the path a Claude client actually sees. Live Neon under throwaway owners, cleaned up in `finally`. Covers: tool registration + the new input fields appearing in `tools/list`; `parentId` on create, re-parent, lift-to-top-level, and both cycle guards; `add_subtasks` order/types/bodies, the rollup counting task children only, and **two all-or-nothing cases creating nothing**; nesting two levels deep; seven natural-language phrases each asserted to their exact RRULE *and* description, including the normalized `"monthly on the …"` forms; structured parts with `until`; `count`+`until` rejected together; both `byDayOrdinal` spellings; completion anchor; partial edit preserving rule *and* log; `resetLog`; `clear` (and clear-when-already-clear as a no-op); the `recurrence` block present when recurring and **absent when not**; complete/uncomplete idempotence in both directions; non-occurrence, bad-date, non-recurring, and materialized rejections; carve producing a detached non-recurring item while the series skips that date; completing the current occurrence through `update_item` advancing the planned date without closing the series; and **owner scoping on all four new tools**, asserting the other owner changed nothing. Two of the five initial failures were real findings, not bad expectations: `rowView` never returned `scheduledDate` at all (so the planned date was invisible across the *entire* MCP surface — search, list, get, create, update), and the `"monthly on the 3rd"` degradation above. `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, and `next build` clean (the one pre-existing unrelated tsc error in generated `.next/dev/types` for `src/app/page.tsx` is untouched).
**Affects:** src/lib/mcp/tools/tasks.ts (new — the four tools + `recurrenceView`); src/lib/mcp/tools/args.ts (`parentId`/`scheduledDate` in `WRITE_FIELDS`; `optYmd`/`optEnumArray`/`optIntArray`); src/lib/mcp/tools/items.ts (the new fields on create/update, the `recurrence` block on `get_item`, description updates pointing at the new tools); src/lib/mcp/tools/serializers.ts (`scheduledDate` on `rowView`, optional because the FTS row shape doesn't select it); src/lib/mcp/tools/index.ts (registry); src/lib/mcp/server.ts (connect-time `INSTRUCTIONS` — the one place every client reliably surfaces to the model, so it's what actually gets these used); scripts/verify-mcp-tasks.mts (new).

## ADR-181: MCP shapes a project end to end, and Layer 2 finally has a writer
**Date:** 2026-08-11
**Status:** accepted (CORE — extends the machine/MCP API contract; **additive only**: five new tools, new read fields on `list_types`, one new lib function. Nothing renamed or removed, no schema, no migration. Brandon acked the ADR-180 contract extension; this is the same posture.)
**Context:** Two asks from Tyler. (1) "Make projects so the user can define what their status terms are in the build menu side." (2) "Make sure the MCP can shape projects end to end — pick what tools are shown, add things to each tool, and add tasks, notes, etc. to each project."
**Ask 1 was already built, and shipped unchanged.** `StatusSchemaEditor` (ADR-106, building on ADR-082) renders the "Completion tracking" panel on `/build/types/[key]/edit` for **every** type, and `project` already carried five custom terms (Ongoing / Waiting for Others / Paused / Future / Done) with label, color, per-category default, add and remove. Verified live: the page returns 200 with all five labels in editable inputs. **The gap was findability, not capability** — nothing anywhere pointed at that panel, so "where do I rename my project stages?" had no visible answer from the type index. Fixed with one badge (`statusHint`) on each Build → Types row: "5 statuses" / "done checkbox" / nothing for a type with no status, titled to name the panel it links into. Deliberately did not rebuild the editor.
**Ask 2 was real, and one half of it was missing from the whole app, not just MCP:**
1. **`types.default_widgets` (Layer 2) had no writer anywhere.** `resolveComposition` has overlaid record → type → generated since PJ3, and the type layer was read in three places, but nothing could write it: no lib function, no route, no UI. The only editable layer was Layer 3 (a single record, via "+ Add section" and the gear). `setTypeDefaultWidgets` (types.ts) is that writer, and `set_type_layout` is its first caller. null clears (fall back to the generated set), which is deliberately **not** the same as `[]` (this type shows no sections); both are legal and preserved exactly. It refuses a shape `parseComposition` rejects rather than storing nothing, because that parser is tolerant-by-design for the render path and a write must not silently clear.
2. **Five new tools:** `get_record_layout` (what shows / hidden / addable, and whether the layout comes from the record, the type, or the built-in default), `set_record_layout` (Layer 3), `set_type_layout` (Layer 2), `add_to_record` (put a task/note/milestone/event/link inside a record, creating one or many, or filing an existing item in — the `/api/records/[id]/contain` equivalent, same allow-list and same role rule: tasks keep `project`, everything else `contains`), and `set_type_statuses` (define the status terms, the MCP half of ask 1). `list_types` now also reports `statusMode` + the effective `statuses` + `statusesAreCustom`, so a model can read the terms before using them.
**Why / alternatives:** Decisions worth recording.
- **show / hide / order / options as ops, not a whole-composition PUT.** A model resending a full widget array would drop what it forgot, the same trap `update_type`'s full-`propertySchema` replace already has. Ops make the common request ("stop showing Meetings on projects") a one-liner that can't clobber the rest. One pure `applyLayoutOps` serves both layers so they cannot drift.
- **Editing a record bases on its EFFECTIVE layout, not an empty one.** A record still inheriting must keep the sections it currently shows, so the first edit snapshots what's on screen. The consequence, asserted in the verify script: a record diverging *after* the type hid a section inherits that hide rather than resurrecting it. That's the PRD's "a record diverges from its type, it never defines it."
- **Widget options are validated against each widget's own declared option schema** (select choices, number ranges, the universal `limit` 1–50), so a layout write can't store a value the gear would never produce.
- **Hiding never deletes, restated at the tool boundary.** `hidden: true` keeps the instance and never touches the backing items; the tool descriptions say so, because a model asked to "remove the tasks section" must not reach for `update_item` on the tasks.
- **`add_to_record` sets HOME** (primary residence), which is what makes an item *belong* to the record rather than merely link to it — what digests, breadcrumbs and roll-ups count. Worth noting for accuracy: the typed collection cards (Tasks/Docs/Meetings/Milestones/Links) query `type + relatedTo` and are **role- and home-agnostic** (`boundFilter`, Tyler 2026-07-01), so a plain `relate_items` was already enough to make a task *appear* in a project's Tasks card. Home is what makes it live there. `relate_items` remains the right tool for a cross-reference.
- **A Build UI for Layer 2 shipped in the same slice (Tyler asked for it directly after the MCP half).** `TypeSectionsEditor` — the "Record sections" panel, placed immediately after "Completion tracking" on the type edit page, so *what sections show* and *what the status terms are* are both manually editable in one place. It writes through a focused route (`PATCH /api/types/[key]/widgets`), like `/statuses` and `/layout`, so it can't clobber a whole-definition builder edit. Three deliberate choices: it **seeds from the effective layout** (the stored default if there is one, else the built-in starting set), so a first save is a faithful copy of current behavior plus the one change being made rather than a blank slate; it writes **every** catalog section with `hidden: true` on the off ones, so turning one back on restores its options and position, and so the Build door and the MCP door store the same shape; and it carries `behaviors` (the digest settings) through untouched, since this panel doesn't own them. Reorder is ↑/↓ buttons, not a drag dependency (Principle 5, and the sibling status panel sets that precedent). Styled from the semantic token layer (ADR-141) rather than raw neutrals.
**A bug this introduced and the verify script caught:** the mode-only path of `set_type_statuses` passed a null schema to `setTypeStatusConfig`, and in **select** mode null means the explicit "inherit the default" choice (it's what the Build panel's "Inherit default" radio sends). So switching a type back to named stages **wiped the owner's custom terms** — precisely the opposite of the defer-by-hiding promise the tool's own description makes. Fixed by resending the stored schema on a mode-only change; `inherit: true` is the deliberate way to clear. `setTypeStatusConfig` itself is unchanged and correct: its comment about flipping back restoring the terms holds only if the caller doesn't pass null, which is now stated at the call site.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-mcp-records.mts` (new, **91 checks, ALL PASS**) through the real `callTool` dispatcher against live Neon, under throwaway owners **and a throwaway type** (types are instance-global, so every type-level write targets it; the real `project` type is only ever read, and the script asserts its `default_widgets` is untouched). Covers the pure op algebra (hide marks rather than removes, show doesn't duplicate, a new section appends, a partial order pulls to front, options merge and override); status terms end to end (keys derived from labels, labels verbatim, order, **renaming by resending a key leaves the item where it was**, dropping a term re-buckets its item, no-Done rejected, unknown category rejected, mode-only round trip preserving terms, `inherit`); both layout layers (write, order, hide, reset, inheritance source flipping record/type/generated, a diverged record unaffected by the type default, unknown section/option/choice/limit all rejected, a no-op call rejected); `add_to_record` (one, many, filing an existing item, dates, self-containment rejected, uncontainable type rejected, shared-body-across-many rejected) with each created item asserted to land in the **card's own query**; and owner scoping on every new tool. Also **live in a browser**: an MCP-shaped real project page rendered with Meetings and Milestones gone, Timeline added, the Docs card present, and "Showing 1 of 2 →" proving the `limit` option took effect; artifacts removed afterward. `verify-mcp.mts` updated (its tool list is exhaustive) and back to ALL PASS, `verify-mcp-tasks.mts` still ALL PASS, `tsc` + `eslint` + `next build` clean.
**Build UI verified live** on `/build/types/project/edit`: 200 with **both** panels present ("Completion tracking" and "Record sections"), the sections listed in the project's real starting order (Status, People, Progress, Tasks, Milestones, Notes, Meetings) followed by the available-but-off ones. `PATCH /api/types/project/widgets` round-tripped a composition with a hidden flag, a `limit` option and the digest behaviors intact; a newly created project then reported `source: "type"` with exactly the saved three sections, and its page rendered Tasks + Milestones with Docs/Meetings/Timeline absent. The reset path (`composition: null`) returned the type to its prior state, and `project.default_widgets` was confirmed back to null with the test item removed — the real type was left exactly as found.
**Also fixed:** `verify-mcp.mts` asserts the tool list exhaustively (`toolList.length === EXPECTED.length`), so **ADR-180 left it failing** — that slice ran its own new script, tsc, eslint and the build, but not this pre-existing suite. Both slices' tools are now in its expected list and its readOnly/write assertions.
**Affects:** src/lib/types.ts (`setTypeDefaultWidgets` — the first Layer 2 writer); src/lib/mcp/tools/records.ts (new — the four record/type tools + the pure `applyLayoutOps`); src/lib/mcp/tools/types.ts (`set_type_statuses`, statuses on `list_types`); src/lib/mcp/tools/index.ts (registry); src/components/build/TypeSectionsEditor.tsx (new — the Layer 2 panel); src/app/api/types/[key]/widgets/route.ts (new — its focused route); src/app/build/types/[key]/edit/page.tsx (renders the panel next to Completion tracking); src/app/build/types/page.tsx (`statusHint` badge); scripts/verify-mcp-records.mts (new); scripts/verify-mcp.mts (tool list).

## ADR-182: One Search icon in the nav, and the owner picks what it opens
**Date:** 2026-08-11
**Status:** accepted (not core — nav/UI, plus an additive `update_nav` field. No schema: `searchMode` is another key in the `users.settings` jsonb blob, defaulted on read like every other setting.)
**Context:** Tyler: "There are two types of search now, a popup search and a page search. These seem to both pop up automatically, and the user only needs one by default. Also, the popup search seems to be baked in rather than being a user choice… the popup search appears darker to me than the other icons. In fact what I'm thinking is search is a single icon in the build menu, and the user decides if they want that search icon to be a page or the pop up. Should solve everything cleanly." All three complaints were accurate and all three had one cause.
**The cause:** Ledgr grew two search surfaces — the ⌘K command palette and the `/search` page (stacked criteria with per-criterion confidence, ADR-172) — and each got its own affordance independently. `/search` was seeded into `DEFAULT_NAV_SLOTS`, *and* a permanent palette button was hardcoded into **all four** nav layouts beside New/More (the desktop pill, the mobile fixed bar, the top bar, the side rail). So a default nav showed **two** search icons; only one of them was configurable; and the hardcoded one carried its own `text-neutral-500` while the slots beside it on a rail/top bar render through `itemColors` at `text-neutral-400` — **that one tone is the "darker" icon**, and it was invisible to intent because the two buttons were written in different places. The prior note in `NavShell` (an ADR-172 follow-up) had explicitly rejected special-casing `/search`, on the grounds that hijacking the slot left the *page* unreachable. That reasoning was right about the tradeoff and wrong about the options: the answer is a setting, not two icons.
**Decision:** Tyler's framing, implemented literally. **One** Search destination in the picker (it was listed as "Advanced search" to tell the two apart — that label existed only because both showed at once), and a new `searchMode: "palette" | "page"` deciding what it opens. Default `palette`, because that's the fast path and the one every layout thought worth pinning. The four hardcoded buttons are **deleted**, so the Search icon is now a slot like any other — which is what fixes the color **by construction**: it takes `className` from the same per-layout builder as its neighbors, so it can never drift from them again. Set on **Build → Navigation**, above the slots editor. `⌘K` still opens the palette in **both** modes: a shortcut costs no bar space, so choosing "page" never strands the palette, which answers the old note's objection without spending a second icon.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejected two destinations in the picker ("Search (popup)" / "Search page") — it's the smaller change and keeps `renderSlot` dumber, but it puts the *same* icon in the list twice and invites exactly the double-affordance this ADR removes; "one icon, one choice" is also what was asked for. Rejected keeping one hardcoded button and merely recoloring it: that fixes the symptom, leaves search unremovable, and leaves two code paths to keep in sync. Rejected making the palette a `tools`-style slot with its own pseudo-href (e.g. `#palette`): `/favorites` already establishes the pattern of an href-identified destination that opens an overlay in place, so `isSearchHref` sits beside `isFavoritesHref` and no new slot vocabulary is needed.
**The non-obvious part — the mobile drawer.** `launcherTiles` flat-maps the owner's nav slots into plain `{label, href, icon}` tiles rendered as `<Link>`s, and the tile only appears when that slot **isn't** visible in the bar. So an owner whose Search slot overflowed out of the bar would get a drawer tile that quietly did the *other* thing — a link to the page while the setting said popup. `LauncherTile` gained an optional `onSelect`, and a tile that has one renders as a button that closes the drawer first (the same ordering the bar slot uses, so the overlay isn't stacked behind the drawer). Found by counting affordances in the rendered HTML rather than by reading, which is why the verification below counts both modes.
**Verification:** Live in a browser against the real dev owner's customized nav, counting affordances in the served HTML in **both** modes. `palette`: one button titled "Search (⌘K)", **zero** `/search` links (so the bar slot *and* the drawer tile both open the overlay). `page`: **zero** palette buttons, two `/search` links (bar slot + drawer tile, both navigating). Search stays reachable in either mode, and no surface shows it twice. Build → Navigation renders the panel with both options; `PATCH /api/settings` flips it and the nav re-renders server-side. The setting was returned to its default afterward. `tsc` + `eslint` + `next build` clean; `verify-mcp` ALL PASS.
**Affects:** src/lib/settings.ts (`SEARCH_HREF`, `SEARCH_MODES`, `searchMode` on `UserSettings` + default + parse); src/components/nav/NavShell.tsx (`isSearchHref` + the palette-mode slot branch, the four hardcoded buttons removed, the search tile's `onSelect`, two stale comment blocks corrected); src/components/nav/Launcher.tsx (`LauncherTile.onSelect`, button-vs-link tile); src/components/nav/Nav.tsx (passes the setting); src/components/build/SearchModeEditor.tsx (new); src/app/build/navigation/page.tsx (renders it); src/lib/nav-slot-options.ts (one "Search" entry); src/lib/mcp/tools/workspace.ts + serializers.ts (`searchMode` on `update_nav` + `navView`, so the model can read and set it too).

## ADR-183: Additive MCP surface is not core, and editing a repeat rule keeps its completion log
**Date:** 2026-08-11
**Status:** accepted (Brandon, in response to Tyler's two ADR-180/181 heads-ups). Part 1 amends the CLAUDE.md "Building together" core list, so it needs Tyler's ack; flagged in `COLLAB.md`. Part 2 is a one-behavior bug fix, not core.

**Ack recorded 2026-09-06 (Tyler agrees, relayed by Brandon in session).** Part 1's carve-out is now agreed by both, not just live in the file, so an additive-only MCP or API change ships solo without a further ack. First use under the settled rule is ADR-249, which adds an optional `source` argument to `create_item`. Recorded here because the pending state was cited in three places (`COLLAB.md`, ADR-249, PR #365) and a rule that is agreed should stop reading as outstanding. Noted honestly: the agreement reached this file through Brandon rather than as Tyler's own written line, so if Tyler wants it worded differently, this is the line to amend.
**Context:** Tyler shipped ADR-180 and ADR-181, both flagged CORE-but-additive, both asking Brandon to ack a contract extension after the fact. He also flagged a deliberate divergence: editing a recurrence rule through MCP keeps the per-date completion log, while the canvas `RecurrenceControl` wipes it. Brandon's answers, one to each.

**Part 1: purely additive MCP/API surface drops out of the core list.**
Adding a tool, adding an optional argument, or adding a field to a response is now a solo, move-fast change. What stays core is changing or removing what already exists: renaming or deleting a tool, changing an argument's meaning or a response shape, tightening validation on an existing call, or changing how a tool authenticates. The test is whether an existing caller keeps working byte-for-byte.
**Why:** the both-agree gate exists to stop two people making different decisions about the same foundation. A new tool makes no decision the other person has to live with, because nothing that already worked changes. Brandon: "MORE capable API/MCP isn't something that will hurt the general usage of the app." In practice the gate produced two long heads-up notes asking for an ack that was never in doubt, which is ceremony, not protection. Removal and mutation keep the gate, because those genuinely can break the other instance's clients.
**Alternatives rejected:** keeping the whole MCP contract core (the status quo, which just cost two rounds of acking additive work); dropping the MCP contract from core entirely (rejected, a renamed or removed tool silently breaks the other person's connected clients and deserves a conversation).

**Part 2: editing a repeat rule now keeps the completion log, in the app too.**
`RecurrenceControl` rebuilds through `makeRecurrence` on every save, and that function is the fresh-rule constructor: it hardcodes `completeInstances: []` / `skippedInstances: []`. So changing "every Tuesday" to "every other Tuesday" discarded the whole record of which Tuesdays were actually done. The edit path now carries both arrays forward, matching what `set_recurrence` already does (ADR-180).
**Was the wipe ever deliberate? No.** Nothing in ADR-076 (the recurrence design), ADR-083, or ADR-085 states or implies clearing history on an edit. ADR-076 §9 says only that editing the rule "edits the series item and applies to future computation." The give-away is in the control itself: the same save path deliberately carries `anchorMode`, `occurrenceMode`, `maintainDueOffset`, `byDayOrdinal` and `byMonthDay` through an edit, with a comment explaining that dropping them would be wrong. Preserving state across an edit was the intent; the two log arrays were simply missed, because they live inside the constructor rather than in the caller's option list. Tyler's read ("arguably a latent bug") was right.
**Why keeping is correct:** the log is owner-authored history, the one thing in the recurrence blob that cannot be recomputed. Stale entries are inert, since every reader (next-occurrence, the completions calendar, the ICS EXDATE emitter) filters the log against the rule's own projection, so a date the new rule no longer generates is ignored rather than misread. The failure mode of the old behavior was silent and unrecoverable: no toast, no revision of `properties`, nothing to undo.
**`makeRecurrence` itself is unchanged,** and deliberately so. Its other callers (quick-add via `nl-date.ts`, and enabling a repeat for the first time) want a fresh, empty log; the edit case is the caller that must say otherwise. A guard comment at the call site says this, so a later reader doesn't fold the two lines back into the constructor.
**Verification:** live through the real UI on the dev instance. A task set to `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU` with two logged completions (2026-08-11, 2026-08-18), edited in the `RecurrenceControl` panel from "every 1 week" to "every 2 weeks", then read back over the API: rule became `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=TU` and `completeInstances` still held **both** dates. Before this fix that same click stored an empty array. The edit also leaves 2026-08-18 stale (no longer an occurrence under the new interval), which is the inert case the reasoning above relies on. `verify-recurrence` (the pure engine, unchanged here) and `verify-mcp` ALL PASS; `tsc` + `eslint` clean. Test item removed afterward.
**Affects:** CLAUDE.md ("Building together" core list, the additive carve-out); src/components/canvas/RecurrenceControl.tsx (carry the two log arrays through an edit); COLLAB.md (Tyler heads-up).

## ADR-184: A missing auth key fails closed, and an unresolvable session says so
**Date:** 2026-08-11
**Status:** accepted (touches the **auth provider seam**, which CLAUDE.md lists as core — but as hardening, not reshaping: the `AuthProvider` interface, its one selection point, and `resolveOwner`'s signature are all unchanged. Brandon's instance carries the identical fail-open, so this wants his eyes.)
**Context:** Tyler, 2026-08-11: "my user menu disappears sometimes… I did the redeploy and it went away… I just did the redeploy again and it asked me to login, after login the menu was back." Read as a nav bug (the ADR-182 nav commit had just shipped, so it was the obvious suspect); it wasn't one. That commit's `NavShell.tsx` diff only deletes the four hardcoded Search buttons and never touches the More kebab, and the `Launcher.tsx` change is purely additive. Tyler's own read was the right one: "maybe I'm logged in but not really?"
**The cause:** `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` is read in **two** places that, when it's absent, fail in **opposite directions**. `src/proxy.ts` fell back to `() => NextResponse.next()` — no `clerkMiddleware`, so **nothing is protected** — while `src/lib/auth/index.ts` fell back to `nullAuthProvider`, so **every caller reports as signed out**. The door stands open and the server believes the building is empty. That cascades quietly: `getCurrentUser()` → null → `resolveOwner()` → null → `Nav.tsx`'s `if (!owner) return null` → **the entire nav renders nothing**, bar and rail and kebab and user menu together, while the page body renders fine because each page resolves the owner separately. So a fail-open on a production deployment holding real data presents as one cosmetic symptom: a missing user menu. The keyless fallback itself is legitimate and stays — a fresh clone and a CI `next build` must run before Clerk exists, and Phase 4's local mode swaps the provider the same way.
**Decision:** Three changes, each at the layer that owns the failure.
1. **Fail closed on a deployed environment.** `src/lib/auth/keyless.ts` (new) answers "is Clerk configured, and is keyless allowed *here*", keyed on `VERCEL_ENV` (set to production/preview on any deployment, unset locally and in CI — exactly the split the fallback wants). Missing key + deployed → the middleware returns **503** and logs one JSON line per blocked request. Public routes still pass: `/api/machine/*`, `/api/mcp`, the Todoist webhook, `/share`, and `/api/ics` authenticate themselves with a scoped token, an HMAC, or an unguessable URL and never depended on Clerk, so a missing key doesn't also break cron, MCP, and the calendar feed. `/health` is outside the matcher, so the diagnostic surface stays up.
2. **Name the second failure.** `resolveOwnerState()` returns `signed-out | unrecognized | owner`, and logs a `warn` with the identity whenever an authenticated session matches no `users` row (a re-created Clerk user, a changed primary email, a restore that lost the `clerk_id` link). `resolveOwner()` is now a thin wrapper over it and keeps its `Owner | null` signature, so all ~80 callers are untouched.
3. **Show it.** The home route renders an explicit "Signed in, but not recognized" state naming the email, replacing the anonymous scaffold hero that both states used to share.
**Why / alternatives:** **Rejected redirecting to `/sign-in` on a null owner**, which is the obvious fix and is wrong for the case that matters: the session is *valid*, so Clerk sends an already-signed-in visitor straight back and the redirect **loops**. An unrecognized session is not recoverable by signing in again as the same identity — it has to be shown, not retried. Rejected throwing from `authProvider` when the key is missing: `next build` prerenders through that path, so a throw breaks the very CI builds the fallback exists for; middleware only runs at request time, which is precisely where the door needs closing. Rejected asserting on `NODE_ENV === "production"` (true for CI builds too, same breakage) in favor of `VERCEL_ENV`. Rejected retrofitting all ~80 page-level `resolveOwner()` call sites to a redirecting `requireOwnerPage()` — that's a real cleanup but a large mechanical diff that shouldn't ride along on an incident fix; logged in `next_steps.md` instead.
**Verification:** `tsc` + `eslint` + `next build` clean. `verify-provider-seams` still PASSes all four auth checks — `keyless.ts` deliberately imports nothing (not `@clerk/nextjs`, which would make it a fifth seam file and trip the guard; not `src/lib/log.ts`, which would pull the DB client into the middleware bundle, so the 503's log line is written inline in the shape `log.ts` emits). *Note:* that script reports one **pre-existing** FAIL, unrelated and untouched here — it greps `/api/machine` routes for `verifyMachineToken(`, but four of them gate on `verifyApiToken()` + `resolveMachineOwner` (the ADR-117 shim, added in `db6ae4b`). They are authenticated; the guard is stale and needs teaching the second name.
**Affects:** src/lib/auth/keyless.ts (new); src/proxy.ts (`failClosed`, the three-way handler choice); src/lib/owner.ts (`OwnerState`, `resolveOwnerState`, the unrecognized-session warn); src/app/page.tsx (the unrecognized state); src/components/nav/Nav.tsx (comment only — records that a nav-less page means "no owner resolved" and points at the two guards above).

## ADR-185: Create-on-miss asks what the thing is, instead of minting an untyped stub
**Date:** 2026-08-12
**Status:** accepted (narrows the **create half** of ADR-067's `unmarked` placeholder decision; does not retire the placeholder. Non-core — no schema, no API contract change, no new dependency — but it changes a documented decision, so it's logged.)
**Context:** Tyler, 2026-08-12, from his punch list: typing `@Jake Tourtillott` in a body with no matching item produced a chip reading **"unmarked Jake Tourtillott."** That's ADR-067 working as designed (create-on-miss makes an `unmarked` item, `inbox: true`, triaged later by retyping), and the design is what he objected to. His rule: *"a user shouldn't be able to create something that isn't connected to anything, so if the system can't tell what it should be, the system should just ask."*
**Decision:** Keep the `@` **search** universal and change only the **create** row. The single "Create X" becomes **one typed create row per type the name could be**: `person` first, `project` second, **"Unsorted"** last as the escape hatch. Each row wears that type's own glyph and names the type on its right edge, in the same shape as a result row — so the block reads as one question with three answers rather than a command whose consequence is hidden. A query that already names a type (`@/person Jane`, or a relation field with a declared `targetType`) has nothing to ask, so it yields **exactly one row** and behaves as it did before.

Built as **one shared module** (`src/lib/mention-create.ts`) owning the row set, the triage rule, and the POST — not five edits — because there are **five** create-on-miss surfaces: the body editor's `@` picker, the capture title's, the task-add card's, the generic "+ Relate" box, and a null-`targetType` relation field. Sites 4 and 5 weren't in the punch-list note; they carry the same bug in their untyped path and are now consistent.
