**A second, pre-existing inconsistency the consolidation exposed and settles:** the three `@` pickers sent `inbox: true` even for a *scoped* `@/person Jane`, while `RelationField` sent `inbox: !targetType`. One rule now, in one expression (`needsTriage`): **only the catch-all needs triage.** A named type arrives with a title, a type, and — at every one of the five sites — a relation the moment it's made, so there is nothing left for triage to decide. Flipping that one function changes all five surfaces.
**Why / alternatives:** **Rejected narrowing the `@` search to people/projects**, the other obvious reading of the complaint: searching every type is real capability (inline-linking a meeting or a song), and removing it would trade a labelling bug for a lost feature. The bug was only ever the create fallback. **Rejected a two-step "Create…" row that expands into a type picker:** it hides the common case behind an extra keystroke and breaks the flat `selected` index every one of the five surfaces already uses for arrow-key navigation. **Rejected offering every creatable type:** three rows is a question, ten is a menu to read — anything beyond person/project is reachable by scoping the query instead. **Rejected fixing one site now and the rest later:** doing one leaves four still minting stubs, i.e. the exact inconsistency the change is for. **Rejected retiring `unmarked`:** it's still the right answer when the user genuinely doesn't know yet, and quick-capture still files straight to it; what changes is that it stops being the *silent default* for a name the system could have asked about. The `PREFERRED_CREATE_TYPES` list is a constant rather than a setting — a settings surface for it is the upgrade path if the two defaults ever stop fitting, not a v1 requirement.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-mention-create.mts` (new, **31 checks, ALL PASS**): row order, labels, per-type glyphs, the scoped single-row case, a type missing from an instance being skipped rather than rendered dead, the pre-registry escape hatch, unique row keys, the triage rule from both directions, and a **structural guard** asserting all five files create through the shared helper and that none still defaults a create to `"unmarked"` — so a sixth surface can't quietly drift back. Plus **end-to-end against the running dev server and live DB**: picking Person and Project creates that real type with `inbox=false`, the escape hatch creates `unmarked` with `inbox=true`, and a created item relates immediately (test items soft-deleted to Trash afterwards). `tsc` + `eslint` + `next build` clean; `/`, `/today`, `/tasks`, `/inbox`, `/notes` and an item page all 200. **Not verified in a real browser** — no browser automation was available in the session, so the popup's rendered rows are covered by the pure/structural checks and the live API path, not by a click-through.
**Affects:** src/lib/mention-create.ts (new — `createTargets`, `needsTriage`, `createMentionTarget`, `createRowText`, `UNSORTED_TARGET`); src/components/capture/mention-ui.tsx (`MentionPopup` takes `createTargets` in place of `showCreate`, and `onCreate` takes the picked target); src/components/capture/MentionTitleField.tsx; src/components/tasks/AddTaskCard.tsx; src/components/markdown-editor/mention-suggestion.ts; src/components/relations/AddRelation.tsx; src/components/relations/RelationField.tsx; scripts/verify-mention-create.mts (new).

## ADR-186: A named layer scale, and one open floating panel at a time
**Date:** 2026-08-12
**Status:** accepted (non-core — no schema, no API, no dependency. Adds a token tier and a shared client primitive, so it's the kind of standard worth writing down: new floating UI should reach for a tier, not a number.)
**Context:** Tyler, 2026-08-12, punch-list item with a screenshot: the `@` / relate typeahead and the item **"⋯" kebab** painted over each other, text bleeding through. His note guessed two causes — "competing `z-` values, and/or two popovers open at once with no dismiss-on-open coordination." Both were right, and they are separate bugs.
**Cause 1 — a z-index tie across stacking contexts.** The kebab menu is `absolute z-50` **in the page flow**; the editor's mention popup was `z-index: 50` on **`document.body`**. Same number, different stacking contexts, so the winner came down to DOM order and ancestor stacking — which is exactly what "text bleeding through" looks like. The app already had five de-facto tiers (30 sticky, 40 chrome, 50 modal/in-page menus, 60 portaled panels, 70 transient), and the mention popups were the two surfaces sitting in the *wrong* one: 50 for the editor's, and **z-20** for the textarea one, which lost to page chrome at 40.
**Cause 2 — nothing coordinated the two panels.** Each owns its own `open` state and its own outside-click listener. The catch: **an outside-click listener never fires for a panel that opens from a keystroke**, and the `@` popup opens from typing. So nothing ever told the kebab to stand down, and both stayed open claiming the same corner.
**Decision:** Two changes, one per cause.
1. **A layer scale as tokens** (`--z-sticky/chrome/modal/float/top` in `globals.css`), documenting the tiers the app already used rather than renumbering the world, with the reasoning in the comment block. The rule that prevents the next tie: **a panel portaled to `<body>` belongs at `--z-float` or above, never at `--z-modal`.** Both mention popups moved to the float tier, where every other body-portaled typeahead already lived.
2. **`src/lib/floating.ts`** — a surface announces on open, every other open surface closes. Wired into all seven top-level floating surfaces (three `@` pickers, both relate boxes, the kebab, the shared `Popover`). Sub-popovers *inside* a menu deliberately don't announce, so "Save as template" still opens within the kebab.
**Found in passing, a real second bug:** `.ledgr-mention-popup` was `position: absolute` while being placed from `getBoundingClientRect()` — **viewport** coordinates read against the **document**, so on a scrolled page the popup landed off by exactly the scroll offset. Now `fixed`, which is the coordinate space those numbers were always in.
**Why / alternatives:** **A broadcast rather than a context/registry:** these panels are scattered across server-rendered trees with no common client ancestor to hold a provider, and one of them isn't a React component at all — it's imperative DOM inside a Tiptap plugin. A `window` event is the one channel all three shapes already reach, and it matches the existing `ledgr:outbox` idiom (Principle 5: no new dependency). **Rejected raising the mention popup to a brand-new number above everything** — that's how the ladder got tangled in the first place; the popup belonged in an existing tier. **Rejected renumbering all ~30 `z-` usages:** the tokens document the tiers and the guard covers the surfaces that actually collided; a mass rewrite is churn with its own regression risk. **Rejected a single global "one popover" store** holding the open id: it would need every surface to register and de-register correctly, and a missed cleanup leaves the app unable to open anything — the broadcast fails safe instead (a missed listener just means one panel doesn't auto-close).
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-layering.mts` (new, **31 checks, ALL PASS**): the tiers are declared and ascend, float outranks modal, the popup is `fixed` + tokenized, placement doesn't double-count scroll, no `className` in the typeahead sits below the float tier, all seven surfaces announce, both halves of the reported pair also listen, and the primitive ignores its own id / is SSR-safe / adds no import. **A z-index tie is invisible in code review** — each file is fine alone, the bug lives only in the relationship between two files nobody reads together — which is precisely why it earns a guard. Also confirmed in the **served CSS** that the rule ships as `position: fixed; z-index: var(--z-float, 60)`, and that all five tokens ship in the production build. `tsc` + `eslint` + `next build` clean; `/`, `/today`, `/tasks`, `/inbox` and an item page all 200. **Not clicked through in a real browser** (no browser automation in the session), so the overlap is verified structurally and via the served CSS, not visually.
**Affects:** src/app/globals.css (the tier tokens + the why); src/lib/floating.ts (new); src/components/markdown-editor/markdown-editor.css (`fixed` + the float tier); src/components/markdown-editor/mention-suggestion.ts; src/components/capture/mention-ui.tsx (z-20 → float tier); src/components/capture/MentionTitleField.tsx; src/components/tasks/AddTaskCard.tsx; src/components/relations/AddRelation.tsx; src/components/relations/RelationField.tsx; src/components/canvas/ItemActionsMenu.tsx (announces + listens); src/components/ui/Popover.tsx (announces + listens); scripts/verify-layering.mts (new).

## ADR-187: Optimistic state has to reach the row, not just the control
**Date:** 2026-08-12
**Status:** accepted (non-core — perceived-performance polish. Logged because the *diagnosis* is the reusable part: "is it optimistic?" is the wrong question, "how far does the optimistic state reach?" is the right one.)
**Context:** Tyler, 2026-08-12, two punch-list items both described as a "slight pause" — one on adding a task, one on completing one. The trap: **both paths were already optimistic.** The row paints the instant the card commits (`InlineAddTask` + `AddTaskCard.onOptimisticAdd`); the circle fills the instant it's clicked (`TaskCheckCircle`). So the obvious check passes and there appears to be nothing to fix.
**The actual cause, in both cases: the optimistic state stopped half way.**
- **Add.** The provisional row kept *announcing itself as unfinished* — `opacity-70`, labelled "Adding…" — for the full window until the coalesced refresh flushed: **500ms** debounce plus a **400ms** tail (`list-refresh.ts`), ~900ms. But the task became real when the POST resolved, around 150ms. So the row spent roughly 750ms telling the user it was still working on something already done.
- **Complete.** The circle filled instantly, but the row's **strikethrough reads the server's `statusCategory`** while only the circle held local state. The completion looked *half-applied* — filled circle, un-struck title — until the refetch landed.
**Decision:** Thread the optimistic state out to the row in both paths.
- `persist()` returns the created id; the card fires `onOptimisticSettle(tmpId, realId)` **before** scheduling the refresh. The settled row drops the muted look, drops "Adding…", and picks up a **real `TaskCheckCircle` bound to the real id** — so it's fully usable before the server row exists, and the refresh becomes an invisible reconciliation instead of the end of a wait.
- `TaskCheckCircle` gained `onOptimisticChange`, fired on click **and on the failure revert** so the row can never disagree with its own control. `TasksWidget` applies it over the server prop until the flush clears it.
**Why / alternatives:** **Rejected shortening the 500ms debounce**, which is the tempting fix and the wrong one twice over: the window exists so a triage burst costs one refetch instead of one per click, and a mid-burst refresh can reorder rows under the pointer. The problem was never that the refetch was late — it was that the UI kept *looking* pending while it waited, so the fix belongs in the appearance, not the timing. **Rejected a leading-edge debounce** (refresh immediately, then coalesce the rest) for the same row-reordering reason. **Rejected optimistically removing a completed row from its list:** `TasksWidget` is the only list rendering this circle and it deliberately *keeps* done tasks, styled `line-through`. Whether a completed row should leave is a per-list filter question the shared circle cannot answer, and guessing would wrongly hide rows in lists that show done work — so it isn't guessed at. The 400ms post-flush tail also stays: it exists so a provisional row overlaps its real replacement briefly rather than leaving a gap, and with the row no longer looking pending, its cost is now invisible anyway.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-optimistic-tasks.mts` (new, **19 checks, ALL PASS**), guarding the parts that re-break easily: settlement is reported **before** the refresh is scheduled (after would restore the whole wait), the response body is read **before** the relations branch (a body can only be consumed once — it used to be parsed only when there were relations to write), "Adding…" and the muted class are both conditional, the settled map is cleared on flush so it can't grow across a session, the failure revert is mirrored outward, the row reads the override *before* the server prop, and the debounce is still 500ms so any future change to it is a deliberate one. `verify-mention-create`, `verify-layering`, `verify-sigils`, `verify-structures` all still ALL PASS; `tsc` + `eslint` + `next build` clean; `/`, `/today`, `/tasks`, `/inbox` and a project page all 200. **Not clicked through in a real browser** (none available in the session), so the improvement is reasoned from the code paths and guarded structurally, not measured visually.
**Affects:** src/components/tasks/AddTaskCard.tsx (`persist` returns the id, `onOptimisticSettle`); src/components/tasks/InlineAddTask.tsx (settled rows render real); src/components/tasks/TaskCheckCircle.tsx (`onOptimisticChange`); src/components/canvas/widgets/TasksWidget.tsx (row-level done override); scripts/verify-optimistic-tasks.mts (new).

## ADR-188: The pre-merge check, and six suites nobody was running
**Date:** 2026-08-12
**Status:** accepted (non-core — no schema, no API, no dependency. It changes the *process*, though: `main` now has a gate, and a red gate on `main` means a broken production deploy, so it wants Brandon's awareness.)
**Context:** `next_steps.md` had asked for this twice, in the same words both times: *"worth fixing the check itself, not just the third occurrence."* Two August 2026 build breakages **merged green** — an `unknown` passed to a `string` param (PR #214), then a second named export in `src/app/page.tsx`, which a Next.js page file may not carry. `next build` runs the generated-route typecheck, so in both cases **every Vercel production deploy from `main` was failing**, and both were found by someone noticing later rather than by a check. The cause turned out to be simpler than "the check doesn't run tsc": **there was no CI workflow at all.** All ten workflows in `.github/workflows` are operational crons (backup, calendar-sync, health-check, …).
**Decision:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — typecheck → lint → build → the pure verify suites, on `pull_request` **and** on `push` to `main` (the second breakage arrived by direct push, not a PR), with `if: '!cancelled()'` on each step so one run reports all four results instead of one fix per push. Plus `npm run ci`, so a developer can run locally exactly what CI runs.
- **No secrets, verified rather than assumed.** The build passes with neither `DATABASE_URL` nor a Clerk key: the db client is a lazy singleton that only needs a URL when a query runs (`src/db/index.ts`, whose comment says exactly this), and ADR-184's keyless auth fallback keys on `VERCEL_ENV`, which GitHub Actions does not set — that split was designed for this case. A secretless CI also runs on fork PRs and cannot touch production data.
- **`scripts/verify-ci.mjs` DISCOVERS the pure suites** (51 of 130) instead of reading an allowlist, because an allowlist reintroduces the exact failure this fixes: something nobody remembered to register. A new pure verify script joins CI the moment it lands. It clears `DATABASE_URL` when running them, so a script that quietly depends on the DB while dodging the classifier fails there rather than mysteriously in CI. The 79 DB/server-backed suites stay a local/manual step — CI has no business holding Neon credentials.
**What the gap had already cost: six verify scripts were failing and nobody knew.** All six were **stale tests, not code bugs** — worth recording, because the instinct on a red test is to change the code:
1. **`verify-songs` + `verify-papers`** asserted `canvasIdForType("note") === "markdown"`. It is `"longform"` (ADR-157).
2. **`verify-build-mode`** asserted `/dashboards/<id>` is a Build path. It deliberately is **not** — and the code comment records why: claiming `/dashboards/...` as Build once made Build mode the only way to view an unassigned dashboard. The test now says so, so nobody "fixes" the code back into a known bug.
3. **`verify-provider-seams`** reported four `/api/machine` routes as unauthenticated. All four gate on `verifyApiToken()` + `resolveMachineOwner` (the ADR-117 OAuth shim, `db6ae4b`) while the guard grepped only for `verifyMachineToken(`. **Confirmed all four 401 by reading every handler before loosening it**, then made the check **per exported handler** rather than per file — stricter than the original, since a new ungated handler in an already-gated file used to pass. 20 handlers across 18 routes.
4. **`verify-graph-auth`** asserted the *configured* branch unconditionally, so it could only pass on a machine holding real `GRAPH_*` secrets. It now asserts the branch that applies (null when unset) — real behavior, no secret needed, and CI-safe.
5. **`verify-markdown-escape`** spelled red `#e03e3e`, the BlockNote/Notion red from before the current palette. `textColorName` doesn't recognize it, so the tokenizer correctly declined the span, it fell through to marked's generic inline-HTML path, and the doc parsed **empty**. Now derived from `BLOCKNOTE_COLORS.red.text` so a palette change can't re-break it.
**Why / alternatives:** **Rejected an allowlist of verify scripts** (see above — same failure mode). **Rejected running the DB-backed suites in CI:** it would mean production-adjacent Neon credentials in Actions, and they'd be unavailable to fork PRs; the seam between "pure" and "backed" is real and worth keeping. **Rejected making lint failures non-blocking** — but note lint currently reports *warnings* only, so it blocks on errors alone; the two pre-existing unused-import warnings were cleared so the new check starts with clean output, since a check that ships noisy teaches people to ignore its output. **Rejected a `required status check` branch-rule as part of this change:** that's a GitHub repo setting, not a file, so it can't ride in a commit — it's the follow-up below, and until it's set the workflow reports but does not actually *block* a merge.
**Follow-ups owed:** (1) mark `CI / check` a **required status check** on `main` in GitHub branch protection, or the gate only advises; (2) the 79 DB-backed suites still have no automated runner and may hold more stale expectations of the kind found here — a local `verify:all` against a scratch database is the obvious next step. *(A third follow-up, repointing the git remote after the repo moved to the `strategicli` org, was done the same day — Brandon moved it so both builders can push, and the repo is public deliberately. Neither is a defect; see next_steps.)*
**Affects:** .github/workflows/ci.yml (new); scripts/verify-ci.mjs (new); package.json (`typecheck`, `verify:ci`, `verify:list`, `ci`); scripts/verify-songs.mts; scripts/verify-papers.mts; scripts/verify-build-mode.mts; scripts/verify-provider-seams.mts; scripts/verify-graph-auth.mts; scripts/verify-markdown-escape.mts; scripts/verify-project.mts + scripts/verify-scheduled-time.mts (unused imports).
## ADR-189: A user guide, held once and served three ways
**Date:** 2026-08-12
**Status:** accepted (solo). The MCP resource is **purely additive**, which ADR-183's carve-out makes a move-fast change. The upkeep rule in "When you finish a slice" is a new standing convention affecting both builders, so it is logged here and flagged in `COLLAB.md` rather than merged silently.
**Context:** Tyler kept asking for features he already had. That is not a Tyler problem: nothing in Ledgr tells you what Ledgr does. `CLAUDE.md` says how it is built, `ledgr-prd.md` says what was intended, `runbook.md` says how to operate it, `decisions.md` says why each choice was made. Four documents, ~184 ADRs, and no answer to "what can I do, and where is it." The app itself has no help surface at all — `/build/claude` doesn't even mention the two MCP resources it already serves. A feature nobody knows about is indistinguishable from a feature that was never built, and by 184 ADRs that gap is most of the product.
**Decision:** One source, three doorways.
1. **The source** is `src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts` — a markdown template literal in a `.ts` wrapper, exactly the pattern `guide.ts` already uses for the workspace-shaping and memory-protocol guides. No `fs` read, no bundler config, no file-tracing rules, and it behaves identically in the serverless MCP route and in a server component.
2. **The doorways** are the MCP resource `ledgr://guide/using-ledgr` (ungated — "what can Ledgr do" holds no owner data and is useful to every client), the in-app page `/build/guide` under MAINTAIN, and the two links that reach it: the Work "More" menu and the command palette.
3. **The content** is a feature index, not a tutorial. Every entry names a capability and the route that reaches it, because the failure mode was *not knowing a thing exists*, which a task-oriented walkthrough answers worse than a scannable list.
4. **It is instance-agnostic.** Both deploys serve the same text, so it describes what is in the code and never one owner's actual types, views, or data. For "what do *I* have", it points a reading AI at `describe_workspace` / `list_types`.
5. **Keeping it current is a process rule, not automation.** A slice that changes what the owner can do updates the guide in the same PR. `CLAUDE.md`'s "When you finish a slice" says so and `/ship` asks before merging — the two places every slice already passes through.
**Why / alternatives:** **Rejected generating the guide from code** (route tables, ADR titles, tool registries). It would drift less and read far worse: the thing that makes this useful is a human sentence saying what a feature is *for*, which no generator writes. A one-line reminder in an existing checklist is a smaller mechanism than a generator, and if the guide visibly rots we can revisit. **Rejected splitting into per-area resources** — one page until it outgrows one page, at which point the top level becomes an index and the sections become sibling URIs; that is the upgrade path, not the starting point. **Rejected an in-app page that duplicates the markdown** for styling reasons; the page renders the same constant through `markdownToHtml`, so the two can never disagree. **Rejected extending `/changelog`** — that is builder-facing commit history and answers a different question. **Rejected keeping it MCP-only:** asking an assistant is a fine door, but not the only one a person should need.
**Two small things it required.** The command palette matched labels only, so someone typing "help" would never find an entry called "User Guide"; `BuildEntry` and the palette's destination result grew an optional `keywords` array, scored identically to the label. And `.ledgr-prose` ships with the *lazy editor bundle*, so the guide page imports `markdown-editor.css` directly — without it the page renders unstyled, the same class of bug the strict `cssChunking` fix chased.
**Verification:** `tsc` + `eslint` + `next build` clean. `scripts/verify-user-guide.mts` (new) covers all three doorways: the resource resolves and the other two guides still do, the route is in `BUILD_ENTRIES`, the guide renders to structured HTML, and the palette finds it by "guide", "help", "docs" and "manual" but not by an unrelated word. It also asserts that **every `/build/…` route the guide cites is a real Build entry**, so the guide cannot ship naming a page that doesn't exist. Rendered and eyeballed in the browser.
**Affects:** src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts (new, the source); src/lib/mcp/guide.ts (`readGuideResource`); src/lib/mcp/server.ts (`resources/list`); src/app/build/guide/page.tsx (new); src/lib/build-nav.ts (the MAINTAIN entry + `keywords`); src/lib/command-index.ts (the `keywords` hook); src/components/nav/NavShell.tsx (the More-menu link); scripts/verify-user-guide.mts (new); CLAUDE.md, README.md, COLLAB.md, .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md (the upkeep rule).

## ADR-190: The body dialect lists only what is built (the four Pandoc features were never implemented)
**Date:** 2026-08-12
**Status:** accepted (CORE — edits the canonical body format's written contract. Brandon decided, Tyler agreed 2026-08-12.)
**Context:** A verification sweep during the ADR-189 user-guide work went looking for the code behind the dialect's Pandoc half and found none of it. CLAUDE.md has described the canonical body format as "CommonMark/GFM plus Pandoc features — footnotes, superscripts, citations, attribute spans" since ADR-037 (2026-06-13), and that sentence carries unusual weight: it declares itself "the dialect's written contract," and adding to it is a core change needing both-agree plus an ADR. None of the four were ever built.
**The evidence:** `src/lib/markdown-render.ts` constructs `new MarkdownIt({html, linkify, breaks})` with **zero `.use()` calls**, and `package.json` carries no markdown-it plugin of any kind (no `markdown-it-footnote`, `-sup`, `-attrs`). Its only custom rules are three hand-rolled ones: `ledgr_transforms`, `task_lists`, and `ledgr_underline`. The shared Tiptap editor registers no extension for any of the four either — ADR-090 in fact depends on that, noting the `^id` block anchor is collision-safe precisely because "no superscript extension is enabled." So in an ordinary body, `[^1]` renders as the literal characters `[^1]` on print, share, OneDrive export, and into the FTS document. Footnotes work in **Papers only**, through Papers' own machinery: a plain textarea (ADR-048 §5 says why outright — Tiptap "neither renders nor exposes an insertion handle for" them) and a regex in `src/lib/papers/msm-docx.ts` that hand-parses `[^id]:` for the `.docx` export. Papers' citations are the MSM citation engine emitting formatted footnote prose, not Pandoc `[@key]`. Nothing anywhere handles `^sup^` or `{.class}`.
**Decision:** Correct the contract to describe what exists. The dialect is CommonMark/GFM + the inline HTML colors/highlights + `<ins class="slide">` + `<details>` + `++underline++` + CriticMarkup comments. The four Pandoc features come out, replaced by an explicit statement that footnotes are Papers-only by design and that superscripts, citations, and attribute spans are not implemented at all. CLAUDE.md also gains a standing rule for the list: **it names only what is built**, so a reader who cannot find the rendering code should treat the list as wrong and fix it, not assume a hidden implementation. Adding any of the four to the shared dialect later remains a core change like any other.
**Why option A (describe what is built) over option B (keep them, marked "reserved"):** B was tempting — it preserves ADR-037's ambition, and ADR-037's reasoning genuinely leaned on Pandoc features to justify dropping BlockNote-canonical for papers and songs. It was rejected because the four are, on inspection, **only useful in papers**, and Papers already has the one that matters, in the form its own workflow needs. Reserving syntax for a need that a module has already solved its own way is headroom nobody will use, and it keeps the both-agree gate pointed at things nobody can break. The deciding evidence is that the overstatement had already misled real work: `explorations/mindmap-tool-prd.md` planned per-node styling on the premise that "the body dialect already allows attribute spans," which was never true.
**Documentation debt this closes:** the same claim was repeated in four other places, all corrected here — `ledgr-prd.md` §4.1, §"Editor & body format", and §"Document format"; `next_steps.md`'s v0.18 preamble (annotated rather than rewritten, since it records what was decided that day); and the mindmap exploration's false premise. Two artifacts are left alone deliberately: **ADR-037 is not edited** (an ADR records what was decided at the time, and what it decided was genuine intent that simply never got built), and the **user guide needs no change** — its "Not here yet" section already told the reader the truth, that footnotes, superscripts, and citations "are not in the shared editor" and that footnotes "work only inside the Papers module." The shipped user-facing doc was accurate before the contract was.
**A second inaccuracy in the same sentence, fixed alongside:** CLAUDE.md and the PRD both said `.docx` is rendered "via pandoc." It is not, and never was — ADR-048 rejected pandoc explicitly ("system binary, not Vercel-friendly") and shipped the `docx` npm package instead. `grep -rn pandoc src/` returns only comment prose. Same defect class, same sentence, so it is corrected here rather than left for a later sweep to rediscover. (Pandoc remains a legitimate *future* option in `explorations/rich-export-and-theming.md`, which is untouched.)
**One loose thread, not fixed here:** `src/lib/editor/visible-text.ts` strips "a Pandoc footnote marker" so word counts ignore `[^1]`. That is now the only general-path code that knows footnotes exist, and it is harmless and arguably still right — a `[^1]` typed into an ordinary note is not a word either way — so it stays, with the inconsistency recorded here rather than papered over.
**Verification:** documentation only, no code touched, so no test surface. The claim was checked the other way as well: `grep -rniE "footnote|superscript|citation|pandoc|attrs" src/` returns only Papers-module hits, ProseMirror `node.attrs` (unrelated), and comment prose.
**Affects:** CLAUDE.md ("Editor & body format"); ledgr-prd.md (three spots); next_steps.md (v0.18 preamble); explorations/mindmap-tool-prd.md; COLLAB.md (heads-up).

## ADR-191: PWA share target survives a cold Clerk session via a public POST + protected GET claim split
**Date:** 2026-08-13
**Status:** accepted
**Context:** Sharing to the installed PWA (Android share sheet → `POST /capture/share`) failed with an error page whenever the app had been closed for over a minute; retrying immediately after opening the app worked. Root cause: Clerk session JWTs live 60 seconds, and Clerk heals an expired one via a redirect "handshake" that `@clerk/backend`'s `isRequestEligibleForHandshake()` only allows for a GET. The share target became a POST (`src/app/manifest.ts`) when file/transcript sharing was added on top of the original URL/text share — the exact GET-only choice ADR-016 made "so the share stays a plain navigation." A cold share therefore arrived with a stale token, `resolveOwner()` read it as signed out, and `auth.protect()` 307'd the POST to `/sign-in`, which 500s on a POST. This was never a Neon/DB issue, and `public/sw.js`'s v8 POST handling was already correct.
**Decision:** Split the flow across a public, self-authenticating POST and a protected GET that can complete the handshake. (1) `/capture/share` (exact path, no wildcard, in proxy.ts's `isPublicRoute`) now runs even with no valid Clerk session; it still calls `resolveOwner()` itself. **Owner present:** unchanged behavior (file → inbox transcript, URL/text → inbox item). **Owner absent** (expired token, or no session at all): the POST can't safely write anywhere, so it 303-redirects the payload to `GET /capture/share/claim` — a short URL/text share rides directly in the query string (`buildClaimQuery`, URL-encoded, empty fields omitted); a file share, or a URL/text share whose encoded query would exceed ~6KB, is JSON-stashed first (`{kind, title, text, url?}`) under a random-UUID key (`share-stash/<uuid>.json`) via the existing R2-backed `StorageProvider` (`putObject`/`publicUrl`/`deleteObject` — no new client, no interface change), capped at 2MB so an abandoned claim can't run away with storage. (2) `/capture/share/claim` is deliberately **not** in the public matcher, so it stays Clerk-protected. Being a GET document navigation, a stale token here goes through Clerk's handshake and gets silently refreshed before the handler runs; a genuinely signed-out visitor is bounced to `/sign-in` with `redirect_url` preserving the exact claim URL, so the share survives sign-in. The route re-resolves the owner (defensive fallback to `/` on ADR-184's "unrecognized" state), reads either the query params or the stash object (`isValidStashId` — strict UUID-format match only, so the route can never be steered into reading an arbitrary storage key), calls the same `createInboxTranscript`/`captureSharedUrlOrText` the authenticated POST path already used, and best-effort deletes a claimed stash object (a failed delete never fails the request).
**Why the alternatives were rejected:** Reverting the share target to GET (ADR-016's original choice) would lose file/transcript sharing, which is why it became a POST in the first place — not an option. A service-worker-side stash-and-retry was rejected: it depends on SW cold-start timing relative to the share intent, which is the exact flakiness class ADR-016 already saw and hand-rolled a conservative SW specifically to avoid; a server-side stash with a deterministic redirect has no such race. Silently extending the Clerk session TTL was rejected: 60s is Clerk's default and not this app's to change, and even a longer TTL only shrinks the window, it doesn't close it.
**Deliberate corners (marked `ponytail:` in code):** a stash object that's never claimed relies on the 2MB/6KB caps at write time plus a future R2 lifecycle rule to age it out, not a cleanup cron. A refreshed/re-visited claim URL can re-run `captureSharedUrlOrText` and double-capture the same text share; soft-delete + inbox triage is the existing safety net for any duplicate capture, so this rides on it rather than adding de-dup bookkeeping.
**Verification:** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `node scripts/verify-ci.mjs` (54 pure suites) all pass; the one pre-existing failure (`verify-editor-shortcuts.mts`, a Tiptap keybinding scan) reproduces identically on `origin/main` before this change, unrelated. New `scripts/verify-share-claim.mts` exercises the two pure helpers directly: `buildClaimQuery` (encoding, omission of empty fields, empty-share case) and `isValidStashId` (accepts a real UUID, rejects null/empty/path-traversal/prefixed/malformed input).
**Affects:** `src/proxy.ts`, `src/app/capture/share/route.ts`, `src/app/capture/share/claim/route.ts` (new), `scripts/verify-share-claim.mts` (new).

## ADR-192: `phone` and `email` property kinds — declared intent over a guessed key
**Date:** 2026-08-13
**Status:** accepted (CORE — the property-kind list in `schema.md`; additive, no migration)
**Context:** From Tyler: a person's phone number on a mobile device should be tappable, not something you read and retype into the dialer. The premise turned out to be half-true, and the half that was false is the actual argument for this change. `CustomProperties.tsx` already rendered `tel:`/`mailto:` links and the right on-screen keyboard — but it derived the intent from the field's **key**, matching `/phone|mobile|\btel\b|cell/` and `/e-?mail/`. So a field keyed `mobile_2` got a dialer and one keyed `contact_line` did not, for no reason visible to the owner, and the affordance existed only on the record canvas: a phone column in a list view was dead text everywhere. The heuristic's own comment said it was "a display heuristic over the existing kinds, not a new property kind," which was an accurate description of a stopgap.
**Decision:** Add two scalar kinds, `phone` and `email`, to `PROPERTY_KINDS`. They are `text` in storage and differ only in how they render: a `tel:`/`mailto:` link, and `type`/`inputMode` on the input so a phone field raises the dialpad keyboard. The intent is **declared once in the builder** instead of inferred per render from a key the owner may never have thought about.
- **The stored value is never rewritten.** Nothing validates or reformats it. Phone formats are a swamp (extensions, country codes, `x203`, letters), and a field that refuses a valid number is worse than one that renders an odd one. `(309) 555-0142 x12` displays verbatim; only the href is normalized.
- **One module owns the href rules** (`src/lib/contact-links.ts`, pure, no deps) because two surfaces need the same answer and would otherwise drift: the canvas panel and the list's table layout. `verify-contact-links` asserts `CustomProperties.tsx` no longer hand-rolls a `tel:`/`mailto:` string, so a future edit can't re-inline them.
- **Extensions are cut from the href, and this is the one non-obvious rule.** Naively stripping non-digits turns `(309) 555-0142 x12` into `tel:309555014212` — the extension digits read as more of the number and it **misdials**. `telHref` therefore cuts anything past a `,`/`;` and a trailing `x|ext|extn|extension` before stripping. The extension stays visible on screen so the owner can enter it after the call connects. Encoding it as `,,12` (DTMF pause) was rejected: pause support varies by dialer, so a wrong pause is a silent misdial too. (Caught by writing the doc comment first and then finding the code disagreed with it.)
- **The legacy key heuristic stays, scoped to `text`.** Production data — Brandon's Notion import, Tyler's people — holds contact fields typed `text`, and this change does not get to require retyping them all. A declared kind always wins; the heuristic is back-compat only. Nothing migrates.
- **Filtering is text filtering** (`contains`/`eq`/`neq`/`set`/`empty`) over the raw value. A stored `(309) 555-0142` does not match a `3095550142` search, and pretending otherwise would need a normalized shadow value nothing writes.
- **List linking is the table layout only.** The compact row layout wraps the entire row in a `Link` to the item; an anchor inside an anchor is invalid HTML and would steal the row tap. `ViewRenderer` gained an optional `propertyKinds` map (defaulted `{}`, the exact shape and resolution site as the existing `propertyLabels`), threaded through the four places that already resolve a type's `propertySchema` for rendering.
**Rejected:** *Keeping the key heuristic and widening its regex* — every widening is another invisible rule, and the failure is silent in both directions (a field named "Emergency contact" holding a number still loses). *Validating or normalizing on write* — see above; also destroys `x203` and international formats. *A single `contact` kind with a sub-type* — two kinds is less machinery than one kind plus a discriminator, and the two behave differently enough (dialpad vs `@` keyboard) that the split is the honest model. *Rendering links in the compact row too* — invalid nested anchors; a real HTML constraint, not a preference.
**Verification:** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run build` clean. New `scripts/verify-contact-links.mts` — **66 checks, all pass**, pure so `verify-ci.mjs` discovered it automatically (55 pure suites now, up from 54). It covers the href rules (formatting, `+` preservation, six extension/note-cutting cases, the "no digits → no link" floor), that a declared kind beats the key, that the legacy `text` heuristic still fires for imported data, that a phone in an unrecognized text key gets **no** link (the motivating gap, asserted so it stays visible), the input-type/keyboard mapping, the filter operators, and four structural guards. `verify-types.mts` (DB-backed) updated for the count and run green against the dev DB. **Not clicked through in a real browser** — no browser automation in this session; the tap-to-call behavior on a physical phone is unverified by construction, since a desktop browser cannot exercise a dialer.
**Owed:** Brandon's ack. This is core (it extends the `schema.md` property-kind list), and it is additive-only — his instance behaves identically until he declares a field with one of the new kinds. Raised in `COLLAB.md`.
**Affects:** `src/lib/types.ts`, `src/lib/contact-links.ts` (new), `src/lib/view-where.ts`, `src/components/build/CustomProperties.tsx`, `src/components/build/TypeBuilder.tsx`, `src/components/build/StructureBuilder.tsx`, `src/components/views/ViewRenderer.tsx`, `src/lib/view-render.ts`, `src/lib/related-views.ts`, `src/lib/dashboard-resolve.ts`, `src/lib/dashboard-widgets.ts`, `src/components/lists/ViewLensBody.tsx`, `src/components/dashboards/WidgetBody.tsx`, `src/app/views/[id]/page.tsx`, `scripts/verify-contact-links.mts` (new), `scripts/verify-types.mts`, `schema.md`, `src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts`.

## ADR-193: The offline fallback page is a live directory of what's pinned, derived from the pin cache alone
**Date:** 2026-08-14
**Status:** accepted (not core — nothing here touches the data model, body format, type/canvas model, provider interfaces, or the MCP contract)
**Context:** Save Offline (PRD §4.7, ADR-019) pins an item's print render into `ledgr-pin-v1` under both `/items/{id}/print` and `/items/{id}`, so that item's URL loads with no network. But there was **no path to a pinned item except already knowing its address.** The PWA's `start_url` is `/`, which is not pinned, so cold-launching the installed app in airplane mode fell through to `public/offline.html` — a static dead end reading "You're offline / Try again," with no links and no state. Pin Sunday's sermon on Saturday night and there was no reliable way to reach it Sunday morning. The pin worked; the discoverability did not, which made the feature's promise mostly theoretical.
**Decision:** `public/offline.html` becomes the offline landing page: it lists everything pinned on that device, most recently saved first, each row linking to its pinned copy. The service worker's routing is **unchanged** — it was already correct.
- **The list is derived entirely from `ledgr-pin-v1`. There is no registry.** `cache.keys()` filtered to `/^\/items\/([^/]+)\/print$/` picks one row per item, and that single regex also collapses the bare `/items/{id}` twin and skips every pinned image URL. Titles come from the `<title>` the print renderer already writes (`print-html.ts`), scraped from the cached bytes. A `localStorage`/IndexedDB registry was rejected specifically because it is a second store that can drift from the pins it describes, and can outlive them: it would confidently list documents a cache clear already removed.
- **`offline.html` was already the right place**, for a reason worth naming: it is the service worker's fallback for every failed navigation, including the cold `/` open, and a static page has no Next router, so **every link on it is a hard navigation** that lands on the existing `request.mode === "navigate"` branch where the pin fallback already lives. Nothing in `sw.js` needed to change. Editing `manifest.ts`'s `start_url` was rejected: it would degrade every normal online launch to fix a case the fallback already covers.
- **Rows sort on the stamp, not on cache key order.** `SaveOffline` now stamps a `Date` header on the pinned response (a hand-built `Response` carries none). Insertion order happens to be a correct proxy today, but a re-save `cache.put`s over the same key, and only an explicit sort guarantees that row returns to the top regardless of how a browser orders `keys()`. Pins from before the header sort last and show no date rather than a wrong one.
- **The `VERSION` bump in `sw.js` is part of the change, not hygiene.** `offline.html` is precached into `SHELL_CACHE` and served cache-first, so editing it without bumping leaves every installed device on the old copy, silently, with nothing to debug. `v9` carries no behavior change of its own. Any future `PRECACHE` edit owes the same bump; `verify-offline-landing` asserts `VERSION > v8`.
- **The SPA-navigation gap is real and self-healing, so it is deliberately not "fixed."** A client-side `<Link>` tap issues a plain `fetch` for `/items/{id}?_rsc=…`, which is not `mode: "navigate"`, so it lands in the catch-all fetch branch, whose `cache.match` has no `ignoreSearch` and misses on the cache-buster. Next's `fetchServerResponse` then catches the failure and returns the original URL, which the router turns into an MPA navigation; **that** hard load hits the navigate branch and serves the pin. Two paths converge there: even if the worker returned the pinned HTML, `!isFlightResponse` triggers the identical fallback. **Adding `ignoreSearch: true` to the catch-all was rejected** — it would let a pinned HTML document answer API and RSC requests that asked for something else, a worse failure than the one it replaces.
- **Styling stays hand-written inline CSS, not the ADR-141 token layer.** Self-containment is this file's whole purpose: it must render with nothing else cached, so it can never load `globals.css`. The inline `<script>` is safe for the same reason it adds no fetch, and this origin has no CSP.
- **Free side effect worth documenting:** `offline.html` is a static file Next serves, so visiting `/offline.html` **online** renders the same live list. That is the Saturday-night "did my pins land?" check, at zero code cost, and it is in the user guide.
**Rejected:** *A real `/offline` Next route* — it would need its own pin, and the list must still be computed client-side from the cache, so the server adds only a second thing to keep pinned and a snapshot that goes stale the moment you pin something new. *Teaching the service worker to build the list* — the page can read the cache directly; a message round-trip puts logic in the file that is hardest to update on a device. *A "back to saved items" link in the print renderer* — it would put a dead link on every printed page and every online print view to serve one offline case the browser's back button already handles.
**Files:** `public/offline.html`, `public/sw.js`, `src/components/canvas/SaveOffline.tsx`, `scripts/verify-offline-landing.mts` (new, 20 checks, pure), `src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts`.

## ADR-194: Satellite instances update themselves from Build → Updates, gated on the schema axis
**Date:** 2026-08-14
**Status:** accepted (NOT core — a new Build/MAINTAIN page, a fail-closed env gate, and two ops scripts; no schema, body-format, type-model or MCP-contract change; additive to every existing instance)
**Context:** Tyler is standing up instances for Michelle (GitHub `michellecollins1212-rosanne`, account created 2026-08-14) and Miles, and the propagation question is the one that had no good answer. The recorded plan (next_steps.md, 2026-08-13) was **fork, then Tyler syncs the fork by hand**, because Tyler has `push` but not `admin` on `strategicli/ledgr` (re-verified via the API this session: `admin:false`, org role `member`), so he cannot add collaborators and the repo being public makes forking the only self-serve route. That plan works and leaves Tyler as the permanent manual step for people who will never open a terminal. Tyler's framing: *"what would be best is if the UI indicated the repo needs an update and a click let her download the latest on her own."* He then extended it to himself, on the grounds that Brandon pushes too. That extension is what made the feature honest, because **Tyler's risk is not the same as Michelle's**: his Vercel deploys from `strategicli/ledgr` directly, so his code is never behind, while his **database** silently is. Confirmed live mid-session: `origin/main` moved 4 commits ahead (PRs #256, #257) while this work was in progress, and `prod-tyler` does not exist on origin, so main is his production branch and those commits deployed to him automatically.
**Decision:** One page, `/build/updates` (Build → MAINTAIN), answering "is this instance current?" on **two independent axes that fail for different people**:
- **Code.** A **satellite** deploys from a fork and receives nothing until that fork is synced; a **source** instance deploys from the shared repo and receives every push automatically. Satellite-ness is derived from Vercel's own `VERCEL_GIT_REPO_OWNER`/`VERCEL_GIT_REPO_SLUG` against `GITHUB_REPO`, so a satellite needs **no configuration to be identified**. A source instance is told plainly there is nothing to pull rather than being shown a dead button.
- **Schema.** The migration journal is a **static JSON import**, so it ships inside the deployed bundle and describes the migrations the *running code* expects; comparing it to `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` needs no network and works on every instance, configured or not. Verified in the build output: the journal lands in a chunk the route both requires and traces into its function (`.nft.json`), not a filesystem read.
- **The button is `POST /api/updates`** → GitHub's `merge-upstream` on the fork, which is the same operation as the web UI's "Sync fork". Pushing to the fork's deploy branch *is* the deploy, so the client island then polls the status route until the running commit reports current: the answer flipping is the new deploy answering. Stopping at "pulled" would leave someone reloading a page that still shows the old version.
- **`LEDGR_SELF_UPDATE` gates it, and fails closed.** `off` (default) is status-only; `safe` allows updates that touch nothing under `drizzle/`; `on` allows any. **`on` is only correct with Build Command `npm run build:satellite`** (`migrate.mjs && next build`), where a bad migration fails the build and Vercel keeps the previous working deploy live — the failure mode is a non-deploy, not a broken instance. The gate requires a recognized mode rather than excluding `off`; **the verify script caught it failing open** (an unrecognized value granted permission, since the runtime normalizer was the only thing closing it), which is precisely the bug a permission gate must not have.
- **`npm run instances:sync` remains, for the case the button cannot cover:** it migrates each database **first** and syncs each fork **second**, and refuses to sync a fork whose migration failed. `npm run instance:new` collapses the four-step provisioning (migrate → seed → owner row → verify) whose steps, skipped, produce the ADR-184 "Signed in, but not recognized" screen that reads as a bug.
**Rejected:** *Tyler hosting everyone's Vercel projects against the shared repo* — simplest propagation (zero sync step) but puts all ops on one person and other people's production apps on one Hobby account; kept on the table as the low-effort fallback. *A sync workflow inside each fork* — GitHub disables Actions in forks by default, and the workflow file itself commits to their `main`, which breaks fast-forward and drifts the fork, the exact trap the 2026-08-13 note flagged. *Running migrations from the update route* — the running code holds the **old** `drizzle/` folder and cannot apply migrations it does not have; fetching them from GitHub is too clever to trust. *Making migrate-on-deploy the default for everyone* — it contradicts the standing migrate-before-deploy rule (§1j) for source instances that have a release script; it is opted into per satellite instead.
**Verification:** `tsc`, `eslint`, and `next build` clean. New `scripts/verify-updates.mts` — **36 checks, all pass**, pure so `verify-ci.mjs` discovered it automatically (**56** pure suites, up from 55); `npm run verify:ci` all 56 green. It covers the pending-migration rule (including that an out-of-order `when` reports as **not** pending, matching the migrator's real behavior rather than a nicer-sounding one), the real journal's monotonicity, the full applicability matrix, case-insensitive satellite detection, and structural guards (journal is a static import not an `fs` read; the route is owner-gated; POST re-checks applicability server-side; `build:satellite` migrates *before* building). Split from `verify-updates-live.mts` deliberately: `verify-ci.mjs` classifies by connection-string mentions in source, and a stale header comment naming `DATABASE_URL` was enough to pull the pure guards out of CI. Live: `verify-updates-live.mts` green against the dev DB (state `current`, 50/50). `verify-user-guide.mts` green, including that every `/build` route the guide cites exists. **Not exercised end to end:** no fork has been created yet, so `merge-upstream`, the deploy poll, and the satellite code path have **never run against a real satellite** — they are code-verified and unit-verified only. No browser touched the page.
**Owed:** Nothing from Brandon (not core). A COLLAB.md note, since the Build sidebar gains an entry on his instance too, where it will correctly report "deploys from the shared repository, nothing to pull" plus a live schema check he may find useful.
**Affects:** `src/lib/updates.ts` (new), `src/lib/github/client.ts`, `src/app/api/updates/route.ts` (new), `src/app/build/updates/page.tsx` (new), `src/components/updates/UpdateButton.tsx` (new), `src/lib/build-nav.ts`, `src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts`, `scripts/instances-config.mjs` (new), `scripts/new-instance.mjs` (new), `scripts/sync-instances.mjs` (new), `scripts/verify-updates.mts` (new), `scripts/verify-updates-live.mts` (new), `instances.example.json` (new), `package.json`, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`, `runbook.md` §1k.

## ADR-195: Read-aloud is a per-type toggle plus a menu entry, using the browser's own speech engine
**Date:** 2026-08-15
**Status:** accepted (**core-adjacent**: two additive boolean columns on `types`. Purely additive, defaults false, no existing behavior changes. Logged for the both-agree contract; Tyler's ack outstanding at merge, see COLLAB.md.)
**Context:** Brandon rehearses sermons while driving and cannot read the manuscript. The ask was to hear an item read back, primarily on Android, ideally anywhere. Three tiers were weighed. The conversational tier (Claude app voice mode over the Ledgr MCP) already works with no build and covers "remind me how the intro goes," but degrades toward summary on a 9,000-word manuscript. The neural tier (render to mp3, store in R2) gives the best voice and true screen-off playback, and Azure's free tier of 500k characters a month covers roughly sixteen sermons at no cost, but it adds a provider call, a stored artifact, and a regenerate-on-edit problem. This ADR builds the middle tier and leaves the other two available.
**Decision:** The browser's built-in `speechSynthesis` reads the item body. Zero new dependencies, no API, no per-use cost, works on every device that runs the PWA (Principle 5).
- **Two per-type booleans on `types`, not a new table or a jsonb key.** `listen_enabled` and `listen_open_in_edge` mirror `show_in_quick_capture` exactly, down to the setter, the route shape, and the toggle component. A jsonb settings blob was rejected for the same reason `show_in_quick_capture` is a column: these are queried per type on every canvas render, and a column keeps that free.
- **The entry point is the item's `⋯` menu, not a control on the canvas.** An idle player strip above the editor was built first and rejected on sight: it put a permanent affordance on every enabled item to serve an occasional action. The menu already holds the other occasional per-item verbs. **Default off per type** keeps it invisible until asked for, matching the defer-by-hiding posture.
- **Mounted from `ItemCanvas`, not from `MarkdownCanvas`.** The first cut mounted inside `MarkdownCanvas`'s classic stacked return and silently did nothing on any item that resolved to another layout, which browser verification caught on a real sermon. `ItemCanvas` is the one path every canvas type routes through, so mounting there is the structural fix rather than a per-canvas patch.
- **Chunked, sequentially queued speech.** The text is split into sentence-ish pieces capped at 250 characters and queued one at a time through each utterance's `onend`. Chrome silently kills long utterances, which on a manuscript-length body means playback that just stops. Pause is implemented as cancel plus a remembered chunk index, because the native `pause()` is unreliable on Android.
- **A screen wake lock is held while speaking.** Chrome on Android suspends speech when the screen locks, so the phone-in-the-car case needs the lock. It is best-effort and re-requested when the tab returns to visible; failure degrades to shorter playback, not an error.
- **`listen_open_in_edge` redirects rather than adding a second control.** Edge exposes its neural voices through the same Web Speech API, free, and they are markedly better than the system voices. When the setting is on and the browser is not already Edge, the same menu tap opens the item in Edge (`intent://` with `package=com.microsoft.emmx` on Android, the `microsoft-edge:` protocol on desktop) carrying `?listen=1`, which arms the player without auto-playing, since browsers require a gesture before speech. Already in Edge, on iOS, or with the setting off, it falls through to local playback. Making this a per-type setting rather than a permanent link keeps a Microsoft-specific escape hatch out of the default UI.
- **What is read:** the markdown body only. `speechTextFor()` strips fenced and inline code and resolves CriticMarkup (comments dropped, anchored text unwrapped) before `markdownToText()`. Title and other fields are deliberately not read yet; the per-type shape leaves room to add them.
**Rejected:** *A TTS provider call for v1* (better voice, but a cost surface and a stored artifact for something the browser does free; the Azure free tier keeps this a cheap later upgrade). *Reading the rendered DOM* (the canonical markdown is the source of truth and already has a text extractor). *A global on/off* (per-type is how every comparable affordance in the app is scoped, and it keeps the menu clean on types where reading aloud makes no sense).
**Verification:** `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build`, and `verify-user-guide.mts` clean. Exercised in the dev-auth preview on a real 9,289-word sermon note: the toggle persisted, the menu entry appeared only for enabled types, speech actually played (`speechSynthesis.speaking` true, 191 voices), pause, resume, and stop behaved, stop disarmed the strip, `?listen=1` armed without auto-playing, and the floating strip cleared the mobile bottom bar at 375px. **Not exercised:** the Edge redirect on a real Android device, and the wake lock (neither is reachable from the desktop preview).
**Affects:** `src/db/schema.ts`, `drizzle/0050_small_joystick.sql`, `schema.md`, `src/lib/types.ts`, `src/app/api/types/[key]/listen/route.ts` (new), `src/components/build/TypeListenToggle.tsx` (new), `src/app/build/types/page.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/ListenBar.tsx` (new), `src/components/canvas/ItemCanvas.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/ItemActionsMenu.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/action-icons.tsx`, `src/lib/markdown-render.ts`, `src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts`.

## ADR-196: Milestones are completable — checkbox, linked task, or date — and can claim an explicit percent of the project bar
**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Status:** accepted (NOT core — Project Type module internals: the milestone system type's own status_mode/property_schema row, the progress math, and widget UI; no schema.md table/column change, no body-format or MCP-contract change; additive migration)
**Context:** The original milestone semantic (0044, PJ5: "a milestone ARRIVES whether you act or not — no done-state") fit date milestones but not real use. Tyler (2026-08-17): milestones "aren't always date milestones — sometimes they are work milestones," so they need to be completable, ideally by an associated task; and a milestone should be able to carry "points" — "if I got that milestone done it would add 30% to the completion even if that milestone only has say 3 tasks," i.e. the owner declares how much of the project a milestone represents, independent of its task count. He also wants dates optional per milestone (show when set, hide when not).
**Decision:** A milestone now completes three ways, resolved in one place (`src/lib/milestones.ts`) so the widget, the record progress bar, and the project cards agree:
- **Manual** — status_mode flips `none` → `checkbox`; the milestone inherits the system default statuses and gets the same completion circle as tasks (the widget posts the existing `/complete` toggle). Existing rows already sit at `open`, so nothing is rewritten.
- **Linked task** — a new typed relation field `task` ("Completes with task", targetType task, single). Done-ness is DERIVED at read time from the target task's status, never written back, so reopening the task reopens the milestone for free (deterministic, no sync job).
- **Date** — a dated milestone with NO task link keeps the original "arrives" semantic: date passed = complete, badged "passed" rather than "done". A task-linked milestone's date is a target, not a trigger.
- **Points as a percent share** — a new number field `points` ("Points (% of project)"). A milestone carrying one claims that percent of the whole progress bar (`applyMilestoneShares` in project-progress.ts, pure); pooled items (tasks, meetings, unweighted milestones at the old 5-point weight) split the remainder. Shares summing past 100 scale down proportionally; shares with an empty pool rescale to the whole bar.
**Rejected:** *Write-through completion* (task completing writes the milestone's status) — creates an un-reopen problem and a second source of truth. *Points as pool-weight override* — matches the word "points" but not the described behavior; hitting "worth 30%" would take mental math against a moving denominator.
**Also in this batch (no ADR needed, noted for the record):** the Timeline widget dropped its home-only scoping — it now uses the same home-agnostic association as the Meetings/Milestones boxes, fixing milestones that showed in their box but not the timeline; the project Tasks card (and its count) filters to active tasks so finished ones disappear from the card (full list stays on the drill-down page); the section count gear gained an **All** option (persists as literal `"all"`, reads back Infinity, fan-out fetch window bounded at 500); the mindmap's hover +/× buttons got a 400ms hover-intent grace period and the delete × moved flush to the node's inward edge (it sat diagonally off a corner, where reaching it dropped the hover that showed it).
**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, and all 57 pure verify suites clean. Migration `0051` applied to the dev DB (Tyler ran it — the classifier blocks Claude from DB writes); `scripts/verify-record-widgets.mts` rewritten to the new contract and **ALL PASS live (19 checks)**: type flags, the three completion paths, date-is-a-target-when-task-linked, and the share math (30% share = 30% bar; shares alone rescale to the whole). Not yet clicked through in a browser: the widget checkbox, the "All" gear option, and the mindmap hover grace are code-verified only.
**Owed:** COLLAB.md heads-up to Brandon: his instance picks up migration 0050 on his next manual migrate; until then milestones keep the old date-only behavior (the code degrades cleanly — no task field, no points, status stays open).
**Affects:** `drizzle/0051_milestone_completion.sql` (new), `drizzle/meta/_journal.json`, `src/lib/milestones.ts` (new), `src/lib/project-progress.ts`, `src/lib/record-widgets.ts`, `src/lib/project-cards.ts`, `src/lib/composition.ts`, `src/components/canvas/widgets/MilestonesWidget.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/WidgetCanvas.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/SectionCountGear.tsx`, `src/components/build/TypeSectionsEditor.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/MindmapCanvasClient.tsx`, `src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts`, `scripts/verify-record-widgets.mts`.

**Addendum (2026-08-17, same day — refined after Tyler's first real use on the preview).** The checkbox-on-every-milestone shipped above had a wart Tyler hit immediately: a checkbox on a date milestone that will auto-pass anyway reads wrong, and the task link + points were buried on the item page. The model is now **mode falls out of what the milestone carries** — no toggle:
- **Task-linked** ("Completes with task", set right in the "+ Milestone" box, which can also CREATE the task in the record): the row's circle acts on the TASK — one gesture completes both, reopening the task reopens the milestone. A date on it is a target (Timeline placement), never a trigger.
- **Dated, no task:** date-driven, NO circle — the pure original PRD §6 semantic, "upcoming/passed" badges.
- **Undated, no task:** a manual work milestone with a checkbox circle.
- **Completion is stamped:** `updateItem` writes `properties.completed_at` when a milestone enters done (cleared on reopen, composed atomically with any sibling property write). The Timeline places a finished undated milestone at the day it finished (task-mode derives from the task's `updated_at` — an approximation, noted in `explorations/project-review-timeline.md`).
- **The "+ Milestone" box** gains optional points % and the task picker (existing open tasks in the record, create-on-miss); `/api/records/[id]/contain` accepts `points` / `taskId` / `newTaskTitle` for milestones.
- **Timeline widget:** gains the count gear + "Showing N of M →" into a new full chronological page `/items/[id]/timeline` (month-grouped; the seed of the everything-timeline exploration), previews a window around today, and carries an **Uncompleted** tail of open undated milestones that jump onto the axis when finished.
- **Also in the addendum batch (Tyler's same-session asks):** Overview relocated from a section card to directly under the title (same inline editor, toolbar on focus; in-app AI drafting deliberately NOT added — Principle 3, the MCP path already covers "ask Claude to write the overview"); the progress bar's track switched from `bg-neutral-800` to translucent `bg-neutral-700/50` (it was invisible against the peek modal's `bg-surface-2`), header bar and project cards both.

## ADR-197: A project renders as one markdown document — a derived projection, never a stored copy
**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Status:** accepted (NOT core — a rendering of existing data behind the existing markdown view, plus an additive per-item properties stamp; no schema change, no body-format change, no new type. Sits beside `explorations/storage-organization.md`, which stays open for the export-layout half.)
**Context:** Tyler (2026-08-17, finalized same session after feedback): "the project should have a markdown file associated with it" — one document a person can read, or be handed, that tells the whole story of a project without opening Ledgr: who's on it, the summary, milestones, meetings, clickable links, tasks with date-added and date-completed, and the timeline — "that way users don't need to make a new type for that." The trap to avoid was a STORED synced document: every task tick would also be a document edit, two sources of truth, exactly what Principle 1 (DB canonical, markdown one-way) forbids. Tyler chose derived explicitly ("the derived was mostly what I was after"), with a possible future edit affordance noted, not built.
**Decision:**
- **`src/lib/project-markdown.ts`**: `composeProjectMarkdown` (pure string builder, unit-verified) + `buildProjectMarkdown` (gathers the record's collections — the same home-agnostic association every widget box uses — plus milestone states, bounded at 500 rows per collection). Section order is Tyler's: **Summary (the body, verbatim) → People → Milestones → Meetings → Links → Tasks → Timeline.** Links land as `[title](url)` so they're clickable anywhere the file is read; meetings carry their wall-clock time in the owner's timezone; calendar-day dates format UTC (the stored convention).
- **Served where markdown already lives:** `/items/[id]/markdown` (⋯ → Markdown) renders the composed document for widget-home records (canvas id `widgets`: Project, Pursuit, custom hub types) instead of the bare body, labeled `markdown (composed)`, with Copy plus a new **Download .md**. Every other type is byte-identical. The interactive `/items/[id]/timeline` page stays as the timeline's clickable twin (Tyler: keep both).
- **The completion stamp widens to tasks** (from ADR-196's milestones): entering done writes `properties.completed_at`, reopening clears it — the document's "date completed" and the timeline's task entries read it. Recurring series never enter done (they advance), so they're naturally exempt; pre-stamp completions fall back to `updated_at`, an approximation that self-heals as tasks are re-completed.
- **Deliberately NOT done:** editing the generated document (the owner's editable prose is the Overview, which IS the Summary); OneDrive-export integration — the export is incremental on `items.updated_at`, and a project's document changes when its CHILDREN change without touching the project row, so a naïve export would serve stale documents from the Sunday-proof path. That staleness problem is recorded in `explorations/project-markdown-file.md` as the export follow-up's first question, alongside Tyler's "maybe a button to make edits" future note.
**Verification:** `scripts/verify-project-markdown.mts` (new, pure — 17 checks, ALL PASS: section order, checked/unchecked milestones and tasks with their date lines, task-link naming, clickable vs url-less links, wall-clock meeting time, timeline sorts ascending, sparse document degrades to just the h1). `verify-record-widgets.mts` gains the task-stamp check. `tsc`, `eslint`, pure suites clean.
**Affects:** `src/lib/project-markdown.ts` (new), `src/lib/item-mutations.ts` (stamp widened), `src/app/items/[id]/markdown/page.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/DownloadMarkdownButton.tsx` (new), `scripts/verify-project-markdown.mts` (new), `scripts/verify-record-widgets.mts`, `src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts`, `explorations/project-markdown-file.md`, `explorations/project-review-timeline.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (explorations index).

## ADR-198: The project review timeline — the everything-history on a center spine
**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Status:** accepted (NOT core — a read-only rendering of existing data on an existing route; no schema, no new table, no contract change)
**Context:** Tyler's vision from the 2026-08-17 session (explorations/project-review-timeline.md): review a whole project by scrolling through time — "a line in the middle of the page with dates popping up on the left and right and the big dates as like h1 or h2's," meetings and milestones standing out among the everyday ticks (task completions, notes made, links added). The light month-grouped list shipped earlier the same day was always this page's seed; Tyler greenlit the full build after approving the ADR-197 markdown document.
**Decision:** `/items/[id]/timeline` is rebuilt as the spine page, with the data split into its own gatherer:
- **`src/lib/project-timeline.ts`** — `gatherProjectTimeline`: every dated thing in the record merged ascending, in two tiers decided in the data layer. BIG: meetings, milestones (a completed one plots at its ADR-196 stamp and reads "Milestone completed"; an open dated one at its due date as "Milestone due"). SMALL: task completions (the ADR-197 stamp, `updated_at` fallback for pre-stamp history), notes (note date, else created), links added, and the record's own creation as the origin tick. Same home-agnostic association and bounds as the card and the markdown document.
- **Date honesty carried in the data:** each entry knows whether its date is a UTC-midnight calendar day (due dates, note dates → format UTC) or a real timestamp (meeting times, completion stamps → the owner's timezone), because either choice applied uniformly shifts some dates a day. The gatherer also computes the past/future split index — the page stays a pure render (the react-hooks/purity lint rejects `Date.now()` in a component, correctly).
- **The page:** spine centered on desktop (left edge on phones), entries alternating sides with the date opposite the content, month chips and an accent **Today** marker sitting on the line, big entries with kind chips at h2 scale, ticks as one-line text. The "Upcoming" tail keeps the undated open milestones under the same owner-configurable label the card reads. Token-layer styling (ADR-141).
**Rejected:** *task-added entries* (the Tasks section of the markdown document carries added-dates; on the spine they'd double every task and drown the story) and *activity-log ingestion* (the log records adds, not the item dates themselves; items are the source of truth for when things happened, the log for who-did-what narration — revisit if status-change entries are ever wanted).
**Verification:** `tsc`, `eslint` (including the purity fix), all 58 pure suites pass. Not yet browser-verified — the preview click-through is the next step, and the alternating layout is exactly the kind of thing that needs eyes.
**Affects:** `src/lib/project-timeline.ts` (new), `src/app/items/[id]/timeline/page.tsx` (rebuilt), `src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts`, `explorations/project-review-timeline.md`, `next_steps.md`.

## ADR-199: Subtasks ride along with their parent's project; the full task list becomes a real task surface; project + tag become built-in; project cards are configurable and render everywhere
**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Status:** accepted (mostly NOT core — module internals + settings/jsonb config; the one core-adjacent piece is migration `0052`, a data-only `is_system` flip on two seeded type rows, flagged in COLLAB.md for Brandon)
**Context:** Tyler's 2026-08-17 project round, four asks. (1) A task on a project should bring its subtasks — not as top-level clutter, but folded under the parent — and they should count on the review timeline and the full task list. (2) The full task list page (`/items/[id]/collection/tasks`) was a bare read-only list: no completion, no nesting, no row menu. (3) Project and tag should be built-in like task and milestone, so every install ships them (a user can still add their own classifier types alongside tag). (4) The rich "Recent" project card should be achievable on ANY tab or view — Tyler's kanban "Projects Board" showed title-only cards — with the owner choosing which tools each card carries, via Build; per AskUserQuestion, Tyler chose type-default + per-view override both now, cards on all project list surfaces, and the subtask dropdown on both the Tasks card and the full list.
**Decision, in four parts:**
- **Derived subtask membership, never written edges.** `listDescendantTasks` (subtasks.ts) walks `parent_id` under a set of roots in one recursive query (UNION cycle discipline, shared 500 cap, params via `sql.join`). The timeline gatherer unions in completed descendants of the project's tasks as "Subtask completed" ticks, deduped against directly-related tasks. Nothing writes a relation for a subtask, so moving a subtask or un-relating its parent needs no cleanup pass — the read is always current (Principle 3's deterministic posture).
- **One task row, two surfaces.** The `/tasks` row (checkbox, tags, P-badge, status chip, overdue date, SwipeRow/expandable-pill branch) extracted to `src/components/tasks/TaskListRow.tsx`; `/tasks` and the collection page both render it, so they can't drift. The collection page's task branch gains completion-in-place, the row menu, tag chips, subtask expansion, and an `InlineAddTask` pre-bound to the record. The Tasks card gets the same n/m pill (rollups fetched for preview rows only; `WidgetItemRow.subtasks`).
- **Built-in project + tag.** Migration `0052` + seed set `is_system = true` (insert flags + idempotent corrective UPDATE). `ListTabs` switched from `!isSystem` to key-based exclusion so their tabs survive the flip (transcript explicitly excluded — it would otherwise gain a top-level tab). Effect: "built-in" badge, undeletable, sorted with system types; still fully editable. schema.md's `is_system` row updated.
- **Configurable project cards, everywhere projects list.** A pure element catalog (`src/lib/project-card-config.ts`: status / counts / progress / people / key links / Timeline button; absent config = the classic card, empty list = title-only). Type default in `settings.cardsByType` (the listTabs/tocByType posture — no schema change), edited at Build → Types → Project → **Card elements** (`CardElementsEditor`, PATCH `/api/types/[key]/cards`); per-view override in `views.display.card` (ViewBuilder's "Project cards" panel, list/board + project-scoped only). `projectCardsForView` resolves view → type → default and fans out card data; `ViewRenderer` renders the grid for a project list view and rich compact bodies on boards (server board + `BoardDnd.cardBodies`, prebuilt server nodes). The card body is one shared component (`ProjectCardBody`) with a stretched title link and z-raised chips: counts deep-link to the collection pages, Timeline to the spine, key links out; all internal anchors `draggable={false}` so board drag wins. The card grid keeps its no-multi-select gallery exception (ADR-118), now also on view lenses rendering cards.
**Rejected:** *writing relation edges for subtasks at create time* (goes stale on reparent/unrelate; also would have surfaced subtasks as top-level rows, the opposite of the ask); *storing card config in the type's `default_widgets` composition* (the sections editor PATCHes the whole composition and would silently clobber it; settings-per-type is the established pattern with a focused route); *a new `types.card_config` column* (core schema change for what jsonb settings already model).
**Verification:** `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean; all 59 pure suites pass including the new `verify-project-cards.mts` (31 checks: parse tolerance, empty-vs-absent semantics, resolution order, display round-trip, catalog/surface agreement). Migration applied + flip confirmed on the dev DB. NOT browser-verified this session.
**Affects:** `drizzle/0052_builtin_project_tag.sql`, `scripts/seed.mjs`, `src/components/lists/ListTabs.tsx`, `src/lib/subtasks.ts`, `src/lib/project-timeline.ts`, `src/components/tasks/TaskListRow.tsx` (new), `src/app/tasks/page.tsx`, `src/app/items/[id]/collection/[key]/page.tsx`, `src/lib/record-widgets.ts`, `src/components/canvas/WidgetCanvas.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/widgets/TasksWidget.tsx`, `src/lib/project-card-config.ts` (new), `src/lib/settings.ts`, `src/app/api/types/[key]/cards/route.ts` (new), `src/components/build/CardElementsEditor.tsx` (new), `src/app/build/types/[key]/edit/page.tsx`, `src/lib/project-cards.ts`, `src/components/projects/ProjectCardGrid.tsx`, `src/lib/views.ts`, `src/components/views/{ViewRenderer,BoardDnd,ViewBuilder}.tsx`, `src/components/lists/ViewLensBody.tsx`, `src/app/views/[id]/page.tsx`, `src/app/list/[type]/page.tsx`, `src/lib/mcp/user-guide.ts`, `schema.md`, `scripts/verify-project-cards.mts` (new).

## ADR-200: Custom types as tools, task grouping, favorite highlights, and the passive check-in
**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Status:** accepted (NOT core — widget/module internals, settings jsonb, and behavior already modeled by PJ1/PJ7 plumbing; no schema change, no migration)
**Context:** Tyler's second wave of 2026-08-17 project decisions. (1) "We HAVE to do the custom type as tool feature ASAP" — and its mirror, already true: a custom type without a bespoke canvas gets the widget homepage, so a "Book"/"Video" type is a project-style hub today. (2) Task grouping should be optional and configurable. (3) Favoriting a project should highlight the card — visual only, no reordering yet. (4) The shelved Check-in: NO manual button — "it should be enough if the user looks at the project"; per-project checkbox + owner-defined window (default 14d); surface quiet projects "as a p1 task."
**Decision, in four parts:**
- **Custom types as tools.** Synthetic widget defs (`collection:<key>`, widgets.ts) resolved on demand by `widgetById`, so the catalog stays a pure constant and stored compositions never orphan.
