Naming the surfaces matters more here than in the app: on a bespoke type the real content is in `properties` — a paper's Notes, Shape and Quote Bank — so a copy that only moves the body moves half the record.

3. **A JSON 404 for everything unmatched under `/api/machine`** (`[...unmatched]/route.ts`), answering every method. A wrong answer shaped like a right one costs more than an error. It deliberately does not authenticate: "this endpoint does not exist" is not a secret, and a 401 would send a caller hunting for a credential problem that is not there.

4. **Unknown query parameters are a 400** naming both what was not understood and what would have been. Silence turned a typo into a wrong-item result.

`?id=` also became a real filter, one uuid or a comma-separated set, each validated — the bulk read that pairs with the existing batch PATCH.

**On rule 8.** "List queries never select `body`" is a performance rule, not a correctness one, and its purpose survives an opt-in that is off by default and that nothing in the app sets. The exemption is bounded rather than trusted: `MAX_BODY_ROWS = 25` caps a body-carrying page (bodies are unbounded text; a 94KB note is real), and the response says so when it caps rather than truncating quietly. `scripts/verify-items.mts`'s assertion that the default list SQL selects no body still passes unchanged.

**Consequences.** `scripts/verify-machine-read.mts` (24 checks, DB-backed) runs the real handlers with a real minted credential — no HTTP server, no mocks — and covers the lot: the unchanged default payload, byte-identical bodies with the character count asserted both ways, a lossless read → PATCH → re-read round trip, JSON 404s from both new paths, every rejection, and the cap. `/build/api` gains a **Reading content** section documenting the parameters, the cap, the 400s, and that `body` is the `{ format, text }` object on read and on write — the bare-string rejection on write is an existing gotcha, and the symmetry is the thing that makes a byte-exact copy possible.
## ADR-263: an install advertises its published address, read from its own config

**Date:** 2026-09-17
**Status:** accepted (Brandon-directed). **Not core:** one optional argument on a pure function, one field passed to it, and the copy it produces. No schema change, no API change, no change to what any existing caller sends or receives.

**Context.** Brandon's hub moved off its Tailscale Funnel address onto a Cloudflare Tunnel at `https://ledgr.brasco.fyi` on 2026-09-13. Build -> Network kept advertising the tailnet name, because "How other devices reach this one" (ADR-212) builds its list by asking the Tailscale CLI and reading the machine's own network interfaces. A tunnel is invisible to both: nothing the process can see says that requests arrive through it. So the one address the owner actually uses was the one address the page could not name, on the very page whose job is copy-from-here-paste-into-there. The same blind spot had already cost three days of failed browser uploads (runbook section 1, 2026-09-16), because nothing in the app knew its own address had changed either.

**Decision.** `reachableAddresses()` takes an optional `publicUrl` and ranks it first, labelled **Public address** and marked as the recommended one. The value is this install's own `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, which is exactly what it already means and which the R2 CORS script already reads for the same purpose. `normalizePublicUrl()` returns the bare origin, and returns nothing for a blank, unparseable, or localhost value, so an ordinary dev run never tells another device to visit itself. The tailnet hostname, the tailnet IP, and the LAN address keep their order below it, and exactly one row stays marked as preferred.

**Deliberately a config read, not a GUI field, against ADR-222.** The standing rule is that the config file is never the end user's lever. The exception holds here because this value is not a feature switch: it is part of standing the install up, it was already set before this change, and it is already the address the app hands out elsewhere. A settings box would have created a second place to keep one fact in sync, and the failure mode of drift between them is worse than the failure mode this fixes. If an install ever needs to publish an address that differs from the one it answers on, that is when the box earns its place.

**A runtime read, not a build-time one.** The page uses `process.env["NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL"]`, in brackets. Next.js inlines the dotted form of a `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variable at build time, and the supervisor runs `next build` with its own environment rather than the app's assembled one, so the dotted form could bake in as undefined on exactly the installs this is for. The supervisor does pass the variable to `next start`, so reading it at runtime is correct on a local install and on Vercel alike.

**Consequences.** No migration, no new setting, nothing to fill in: Brandon's hub shows `https://ledgr.brasco.fyi` first the next time the supervisor rebuilds. An install with no published address is unchanged. `scripts/verify-network-addresses.mts` covers the ranking, the localhost guard, and the malformed-value guard. The user guide's Network section now describes the published address (ADR-189).
## ADR-264: relative value tokens (`@dayofmonth`, `@today`) for view rules

**Date:** 2026-09-17
**Status:** accepted (not core: view rule definitions are explicitly "move fast, solo" per CLAUDE.md's Building Together section; no ADR strictly required, logged for traceability since it's a new piece of shared vocabulary)
**Context:** Brandon's devotional import (attributes of God, the Baillie prayer diary) needs a view that always shows "today's entry" — the row whose day-of-month property matches today's date number — without editing the saved view every morning. Every existing rule value (`view-where.ts` `WhereCondition.value`) is a literal the owner typed once.
**Decision:** Two reserved string tokens, `@dayofmonth` and `@today`, valid anywhere a rule's `value`/`values` can appear. They are ordinary strings in the stored view definition — no new JSON shape — and are resolved to a literal at QUERY time (`views.ts` `propertyConditionSql`, right before the existing numeric-cast/date-shape logic runs), in the owner's timezone (`todayBounds`/`appTimezoneSync`, the same helpers Today's queries already use). `@dayofmonth` → today's date number as a string ("17"); `@today` → today's calendar day ("2026-09-17"). `RuleBuilder.tsx` offers the day token as a pickable chip whenever a multi_select field's options are all 1–31 (a day-of-month field), and offers the date token as a one-click fill for a number/date single-value input; a token in place shows as a labeled chip with a clear button rather than a raw string in an input box.
**Why / alternatives:** Recurrence (`set_recurrence`) was rejected — a repeating item only advances on completion, and devotional content is read, not completed, so nothing would ever advance. A nightly cron re-stamping "today's" item was rejected as a scheduled job doing work a query-time filter already does (Principle 3: deterministic plumbing stays in code, not a cron). A dedicated `"relative"` value-shape (`{type: "relative", value: "dayofmonth"}` alongside the existing `{type: "exact", ...}`) was considered and rejected as unnecessary ceremony: a reserved string is forward-compatible (an older reader that doesn't know the token just sees a value matching nothing) and needs no schema bump.
**Affects:** `src/lib/view-where.ts` (token constants + `resolveRelativeValue`/`isRelativeToken`/`relativeTokenLabel`), `src/lib/views.ts` (`propertyConditionSql` resolves before branching), `src/components/views/RuleBuilder.tsx` (token affordances), `scripts/verify-view-tokens.mts` (new, pure). Two new saved views ride on it: "Today's Attribute" (`attribute` type, `days` eq `@dayofmonth`) and "Today's Prayers" (`book` type, `day` eq `@dayofmonth` numeric).

## ADR-265: a nav write carries presentation over, never defaults it

**Date:** 2026-09-17
**Status:** accepted (not core: a bug fix behind the existing settings write path; no API, schema, or contract shape changes)
**Context:** Twice now — 2026-09-14 on Tyler's rail, and again 2026-09-17 on Brandon's — an MCP caller added ONE nav destination and every slot in the toolbar came back wearing the generic bullet-list glyph (`NAV_ICON_FALLBACK = "items"`). The mechanism is silent by construction: `update_nav` REPLACES the whole middle-slot list, and `parseNavDestination` stamps a slot whose `icon` is missing with the fallback rather than refusing it. So a caller that reads the nav lossily and writes it back destroys every icon and never errors. ADR-258 is the same shape (type icon/color loss on a wholesale type edit). PR #387 fixed one reader — `describe_workspace` now returns `icon` — but that only closes the path that particular caller took; the next lossy writer, in the Build UI, the REST route, or a future tool, can still do it.
**Decision:** Presentation a nav write does not mention is CARRIED OVER, not defaulted. `keepNavPresentation` (`src/lib/settings.ts`) runs inside `updateSettings`, the one seam every nav write passes through (MCP `update_nav`, `PATCH /api/settings`, the Build navigation editor): for each incoming slot it looks up the slot already stored at that `href` (a tools group by label, since it has no route) and fills in `icon` and `badge` when the incoming slot omits them or sends an unusable icon key. An explicitly sent icon always wins, so a real edit is never blocked; only a genuinely new slot with no prior falls back to the generic glyph. `update_nav`'s tool description now states this instead of warning about the old behavior.
**Why / alternatives:** Rejecting an icon-less slot was rejected — the whole nav parser is deliberately tolerant (a malformed slot is dropped, an unknown icon falls back) so a hand-edited settings blob degrades instead of bricking the toolbar, and a hard error would turn a cosmetic omission into a failed write. Patching each caller to resend icons was rejected as the shape that already failed: #387 patched one caller and the bug recurred three days later. Deriving an icon from the destination's type row was rejected as extra DB work for a case the carry-over already covers.
**Affects:** `src/lib/settings.ts` (`keepNavPresentation`, `updateSettings`), `src/lib/mcp/tools/workspace.ts` (`update_nav` description), `scripts/verify-nav-presentation.mts` (new, pure — runs in CI by discovery).
